_READ_ME_FIRST: TO CLAUDE, OR ANY AGENT HANDED THIS FILE. This is the complete record of one run of Evolu (called Seedworld before generation 14), a self-modifying world simulation by Nova Spivack that lives as a Claude artifact titled "Evolu" (slug be8f1f8f-42db-4703-ac0d-c3e87d04f447; its files are index.html, engine.js, minds.js, maker.js, audio.js, ui.js). The source of record is https://github.com/novaspivack/evolu : the same six files under src/, the tests under tests/, and README.md, ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md, which say how the work is done and what has been tried. Its owner wants every run to produce the next generation of the world, without having to explain that each time. So, when you are given this file, do the following without being asked. 1. ANALYSE with code, not by skimming: "records" holds every thought (t: thought, with drives, plan, state), everything said (voice), the world's own chronicle (chron), sampled full prompts with raw replies (prompt), failures (failed), the chronicler's chapters (story), the maker's visits (maker) and its requests to the programmer (request). "digest" is the final state of every being. "story" and "maker" are the outer loop's own state. Count things; quote the record; say what worked and what is still wrong, with numbers. 2. LEARN from the maker: read its visits, its predictions against what happened, its lessons, and above all its REQUESTS, which are things it could not build from its own parts and is asking the programmer for. 3. BUILD the next generation: read the artifact's current files, make the code changes the analysis and the requests call for (and items from the owner's roadmap, kept in the maker's idea list under "maker.ideas"), test them (tests/run-all.sh), and publish a new version of the same artifact. Keep saves from the previous generation loading. Then commit the generation to the repository and push it, with ROADMAP.md and docs/design-log.md brought up to date. 4. PRESERVE THE WORLD'S HERITAGE: "heritage" lists every change the maker made and kept, with its lessons and ideas. Fold these into K.HERITAGE in maker.js so that the next world begins with them already in place and no maker has to rediscover them. Drop only what the record shows did harm. 5. REPORT to the owner plainly: what the run showed, what you changed and why, what you verified and what you could not. If the owner keeps a design log, update it. The design rule for everything: open and emergent. Make things possible; never script outcomes. The beings must discover what is possible for themselves.

beings.name: Olum
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but I pay my debts. I want more than my share and mean to have it. I stay fed before any venture, I cook my meat, and I build a hearth others will follow.
beings.aim: Teach Nauwa all my ways, keep the Reach fed, and try the mist again when it is calm
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed, carrying cooked food, and away from the hunter? Then ask who I can draw to my hearth. Do not walk off hungry after ambition or jealousy, and stay away from others while sick.
beings.feeling: Urgent longing to leave something lasting, with sour jealousy toward Nande over Nauwa.
beings.wonder: What else lies in the mist beyond this new land, and who will follow me into it?
notes: Raw meat sickens me and the sickness spreads. Cook meat beside a fire, and keep away from others while sick.
Ambition and jealousy on an empty belly starved my child. Eat and carry food before any venture.
Stores get robbed while others stand near. Carry food on my body, and keep the store stocked only as needed.
Nauwa robbed my store, confessed it and paid in amber and salt. I trust him. Balar and Tugek are the nearest thing to a following I have.
A kept flame, a roof and a store draw followers. Signs cut a claim that outlasts me.
Hunters (ridgecat, stalker) kill when I am alone at night. Stay near fire, roof and company.
The mist opens seldom. The Reach hearth and store are the lasting thing.
Ambition keeps pulling me away from my own store. Keep the Reach stocked and cooked food in hand, and the men I want will come to it.
Teaching a trusted man is the surest way to leave something behind. Debts paid in amber build trust faster than words.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I discovered signals and called it "hearth-smoke".
I nearly starved.
I discovered storage and called it "stone-cold store".
We made a home: Olum's Reach.
I discovered writing and called it "stone-record".
I discovered boats and called it "hollow-rower".
I discovered mining and called it "gold-delving".
I found my store robbed of 11 food.
I discovered pottery and called it "fire-clay pots".
I discovered calendar and called it "stone-count of days".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.
I found my store robbed of 6 food.
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered archery and called it "stone-bow".
I grew old.

beings.name: Vorok
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise the hall on the bare rock north now, teach Skaruk all I know, and stock food beneath it for Eiuine and my children.
beings.method: Ask first whose need is greatest, my children before all. Name one promise unkept and begin it now. Stay in company and away from hunters. Do not repeat words. Act, don't just think.
beings.feeling: Tender urgency toward Skaruk and Eiuine, and a quiet pull toward the mist.
beings.wonder: Where is the place with water, food, wood and stone close together, and who will walk there with me?
notes: Words build nothing: I must carry wood and stone to bare ground and build.
Debts to Eiuine, Vesys and Zurar are paid with shared meals and a stocked store.
Being old, teaching carries further: pass my ways to Skaruk and Zurar before I die.
Stalkers and bears hunt near flint and water: stay in company and by fire at night.
Children in need come before my aim; carry food to them first.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I fell sick after staying close to Kragog, who was sick.
My child Zurar was born, with Kragog.
Zurar pledged to follow me.
I nearly starved.
I discovered fire and called it "the kept flame of the Kragre".
I first took flint from the ground.
I discovered storage and called it "the keeping store".
We made a home: Vorok's Hold.
I discovered mining and called it "the hall-deep delving".
I discovered weaving and called it "the carrying weave".
I discovered pottery and called it "the ember-pot of the Kragre".
I discovered customs and called it "the giving-first custom of t".
My child Skaruk was born, with Eiuine.
I discovered masonry and called it "the stone-set way of the Kra".
I grew old.

beings.name: Kragog
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Pay Nauque with salt, teach Zurar what I know, then rest in Vesys's hold.
beings.method: Ask: is a promise of mine still unpaid? Pay it with my hands first, then speak. Then curiosity, then a plan long enough to fill the thought.
beings.feeling: Urgent need to pass on what I know before I die, warmed by Zurar's nearness.
beings.wonder: What can be made from the ore in this rock, and who among these strangers can be trusted?
notes: Tacap hurts me (-5 energy), so I drop it and do not pick it for food.
Salt keeps meat and others crave it. It is a gift to answer a kindness with.
Carry at least 3 food that I can eat, and plan long enough that I never stand idle.
Beings who fed me in need (Zurar, Nauque) get my first return.
Night alone away from fire, roof or company brings ridgecats and wolves. Be sheltered by dark.
A debt said aloud but not paid is still a debt; hand the gift over, close, before speaking of it again.
Standing idle while hungry is how I nearly die; food must come before every aim, and my reflexes must make me harvest at once.
Taught by Vesys: Bark-guard: armour made of bark, worn against teeth and blows. Keeping store: put food in a store, and take it when you are hungry.
Read on a sign left by Vesys: Vesys of the Aessa, eth, veyn: armour (bark-essyn), ynua (keeping store), smelting, oiith, oiael, bow, nyeth-brew. Take only aeael the forest can grow again
Taught by Vesys: Ember-metal: beat ore in a hot fire into metal, and from metal make wards and tools that outlast the hand.
Taught by Vesys: Ember-metal: beat ore in a hot fire and it gives metal that holds an edge and wears into wards.
Vesys repaid my salt with teaching, so paying a kindness with a gift works. Debts are best paid with the hands, in person.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I tamed a tusker.
My child Zurar was born, with Vorok.
I discovered rafts and called it "Stone-folk lashing".
I discovered weaving and called it "Stone-folk binding".
I nearly starved.
I discovered fire and called it "Stone-folk ember".
I discovered mining and called it "Stone-folk deep-hand".
I discovered pottery and called it "Stone-folk clay-keeping".
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I grew old.

beings.name: Balar
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. My family comes first: Olum and Brokash. I make allies by deeds, I give so that others owe me, and I mean to have more than my share and to be followed for what I build. Above all I stay alive.
beings.aim: Venture into the unknown at (13,6) and find rich land, then bring food to Tugek and find Olum, so something of mine outlasts me.
beings.method: Weigh first what will outlast me. Act on the edge and the deed, not on more talk. Keep fed and clear of beasts, and bind others by gifts.
beings.feeling: Urgent pride and a hunger to leave something behind, drawn toward the edge of the unknown.
beings.wonder: Will Olum come west with me, or will she stay and hold the Reach as her own?
notes: Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum of ash Akok dorrek Drurek Reach. Tug ashvor kra ashtug akdor okrek okak Olum dortug ash mist.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor ashtug land, Ashgan Reach. Ok drurek barash kra ashtug akdor um okum okthu akur dru umkra.
A ridgecat prowls near (30,27); flee early, stay near shelters and companions.
Idle time is wasted: when fed and sheltered, gather wood for building toward a store or hall.
Deeds that bind (an amberknot, a gift) matter more than speech; idle moments should go to wood and stone for my own workshop.
Fighting beside others makes kills surer; a stalker comes at night on the lone. Fire keeps beasts off and makes meat safe, so learn fire.
Storage with salt keeps meat through the lean season; a store raised near the Meadows feeds my band and earns standing.
Words alone did not move Tugek to my store; go to the store myself and let him follow, since deeds bind more than calls. Eating raw fish sickens; eat it beside a fire.
Idle hours when fed should become wood and stone for building. Calling others with words binds them less than a built store or a shared meal.
Olum's store was robbed and she vows to remember the thief. Stay visibly honest and give food openly. Idle hours when fed should become wood and stone.
Idle hours when fed go to wood and stone. A shared meal with a guest on my ground binds more than words, and a thirsty body needs a drink rule.
Idle hours when fed go to wood and stone, and I must keep food in hand before hunger turns overwhelming; a drink rule and early harvest reflexes keep me from near-starvation.
Idle reflexes should keep food in hand and put surplus into my store; guests who eat from my gifts owe me, so feeding them binds more than warning them.
Hunger comes back fast. Keep food in hand, hunt before energy falls under 50, and do not let the plan idle while the belly empties.
A hunt on this marsh fed me back from 15 to 79 energy, so the fens give meat in winter. Feeding the starving binds them, and the edge of the unknown is only 3 steps SW.
The edge of the known world is at (25,36); venture only works when standing exactly there.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took salt from the ground.
My child Brokash was born, with Olum.
Tugek pledged to follow me.
I discovered archery and called it "stone-bow".
I nearly starved.
I fell sick after staying close to Tugek, who was sick.
I discovered fire and called it "the stone hearth".
We made a home: Balar's Hold.
I discovered storage and called it "salt hoard".
I grew old.

beings.name: Tugek
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a workshop with Balar, keep us both fed through winter, and come to know Zihua or Olum well enough to raise a child with her.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who near needs me, what can my hands do now, what am I putting off? Act toward the woman and child I want, not only food. Keep energy 60 or more so courting is possible. Do not repeat what I have already said.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and urgency, with an uneasy debt toward Nauwa.
beings.wonder: Will Balar hunt well with me at his side, and does he lead me well in a kill?
notes: Gifts to the starving are remembered and repaid; full hands must not walk past need.
A kill made beside Balar is surer; keep close to him when a ridgecat prowls.
Hunting on Nauque's ground counts as taking; avoid it.
Zihua wants time and deeds, not repeated asking.
Cooked meat near a fire does not sicken; raw meat makes me ill.

A ridgecat prowls near the Reach; staying beside Balar and the others is safer than standing alone, and a gift given openly in front of the one who was wronged answers a charge of theft better than w…
Stalkers and ridgecats take those alone at night away from fire and roof. Stay by the shelter and Balar after dusk. Courting needs both to plan mate toward each other, with energy 60 or more.
Courting needs both sides to plan mate, so I must act and not only wish. Tonka raided our store, so her warmth is not yet earned trust.
Deep reflection: I have followed and given but not begun to court. Smelting is within reach since I carry ore and know fire. Sick women must be approached only after they mend.
Longing does not become a child by waiting. Courting needs a healthy woman and both sides planning mate with energy 60 or more, so I must keep my energy high and approach when Olum or Tonka mend.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashok ashash okgor um ashvor ashash land. Barash akur dru okrek.
Stores near me stay empty; hunting and fishing feed me, not waiting. Teach a living listener before I die, since knowledge dies with me.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I nearly starved.
I discovered archery and called it "Stone-folk bow".
I discovered fire and called it "Stone-folk kept flame".
I discovered mining and called it "Stone-folk deep digging".
I discovered weaving and called it "Stone-folk binding".
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
We made a home: Balar's Hold.
I discovered pottery and called it "Stone-folk fired pot".
I discovered rafts and called it "Stone-folk lashed logs".
I discovered boats and called it "Stone-folk hollow boat".
I discovered smelting and called it "Stone-folk ore fire".
I found my store robbed of 3 food.
I fell sick after a sickness that came on the wind.
I lived through a sickness on the wind in winter.
I grew old.

beings.name: Hanna
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I repay every debt, and I keep faith with those who share fire with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive, to raise a child, and to be known as a trader.
beings.aim: Gather food into a store near Vaor Meadows, stay close to Hoka, and find a place with water, food and stone together; then trade salt and shell.
beings.method: Ask what presses hardest and what step changes it. Trade face to face and watch what comes back. Plant for the lean season. Keep my band near and away from wolves.
beings.feeling: Desperate hunger, and a debt to Hoka and Hawen that I mean to repay.
beings.wonder: What do these people value enough to trade for?
notes: Sickness spreads to those who stay close to the sick; Oswen, Sevi and Hoka now have it.
Starvation came while I chased amber: feed my band before trade, and keep food carried so I can share.
Four of my band starved while I chased amber; food and a stored supply must come before trade, and the stalker haunts the northwest.
Starvation killed my band while I held trade goods. Food first, stored and carried. Eat at energy under 70 and keep food in hand. Flee wolves early and stay by Hoka and the hall.
Sickness spreads to those who stand near me; warn others before they share my fire, and seek a healing plant such as sunleaf.
Hunger and health come before trade. Keep food in hand, heal with sunleaf, stay near Hoka and a hall. Honi's people have shared their hall with me, so I owe them a repayment.
Heat doubles thirst: drink before any journey.
Keep food carried before trade, and feed the starving first. A trader who lets his people starve has no name worth keeping.
Waiting on a promise left me starving. Go to the food myself, then share it, and trade afterward.
I took from Hoka's store unseen when starving; I should own it and repay it with flint rather than let it stand as a hidden debt.
I took from Hoka's store a second time while my hands were full; that was greed, and I must repay it openly.
A starving friend beside me outranks my aim. Pick food first and give it before I eat, and do not take from his store when my hands are full.
The mist at the edge can refuse a venture. Do not stake my food on it. Pick food before any push, and keep some carried.
Food in hand and a place of my own come before trade or edges; a trader with no store is only a beggar with goods.
Plans that walk to plants showing no food end on bare snow. Go only to plants listed as bearing food, and pick before anything else.
Fleeing a predator for a whole day starves me. Eat when energy is low, and flee only when the predator is close.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
Oswen pledged to follow me.
I discovered rafts and called it "log-lashing".
Sevi pledged to follow me.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice.
I discovered archery and called it "flint bow".
I saw Tlama die (gored by a mammoth).
I discovered weaving and called it "snow-weave".
We made a home: Hanna's Hold.
I discovered mining and called it "deep-digging".
I fell sick after staying close to Hoka, who was sick.
I saw Sevi die (starved).
I saw Brunde die (starved).
I saw Oswen die (starved).
I nearly starved.
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".

beings.name: Sevi
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise a hall with Hanna's band, give gifts to Hanna and Oswen, and cross deep water by raft to find rich land
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what can I give or build for Hanna and Oswen? What have I never done? Weigh the risk, stay near fire at night, and keep the plan full.
beings.feeling: Fierce love and hunger-driven urgency for Oswen, with guilt toward Eltha.
beings.wonder: What is Kinmire, and does it want something from us?
notes: Gifts and shared making raise trust fast, even with strangers. A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone, so wood is my bottleneck.
A stalker can bite at night in fog; stay near the fire and the hall.
Stalkers bite those alone in fog at night; stay by fire, roof and company until dawn. Doing things I have never done (plant, hunt, fish) opens new ways.
Masonry is within my grasp and opens at a deep reflection.
Gifts and shared making with Eltha, Hoka and my own band keep the Hold warm; a stalker can still come at night, so I stay with company and roof.
Wells are within my reach; water anywhere would let the Hold hold fast through lean seasons. Never-done things (hunt, fish, mark, tame) open new ways.
Harvest and eat only work when I stand on the plant: goto the plant's tile first. Redcap hurts me, so I avoid it.
Naroot is one step east at (177,6) and snowberry two steps north at (176,4): nearest real food. The hall tile itself has no plant.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I discovered tools and called it "hand-axe".
My child Oswen was born, with Hanna.
I discovered weaving and called it "basket-weave".
I first took amber from the ground.
I pledged myself to Hanna.

I discovered mining and called it "amber-delving".

I discovered storage and called it "winter-cache".
I discovered masonry and called it "stone-hold".
I discovered wells and called it "stone-well".
I fell sick after staying close to Oswen, who was sick.
I discovered boats and called it "hollow-rower".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Nande
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I test things to learn how the world works. I leave behind things that outlast me, and I open my fire to any who come. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great explorer: be first to venture past the edge of the known world and find rich new land.
beings.method: Each thought: have I drunk and eaten? Is a predator near? Do not set out far under 50 energy or parched. Weigh kin first, then lasting works, then the mist.
beings.feeling: Loneliness easing into tenderness toward the frightened boy Tonchi.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?
notes: Pesi creed: no fire untended, no one refused a place. Nauwa gives freely and can be trusted; Shoka and Nauque are my kin first.
Venture will is spent for days; use the waiting to build lasting things (workshop, hall) and keep family near.
A hall needs 6 wood and 2 stone; workshop 5 wood and 2 stone; check cost before planning.
Meat is safe only within a step of a fire; raw meat sickens.
Lean season follows autumn: fill the store with food and salt before cold.
Thirst needs its own rule; reflexes must send me to water.
Wolves hunt near shelters; keep family close and flee early.
Boats let me cross deep water: the way to new land beyond the edge.
Reflection: small builds beside others' halls bring no name. Weaving is within reach, and cloaks would help the northern ventures. Go to the edge, and leave family safe first.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashok kraur tugum um ashvor kraur land. Barash akur dru akak.
Starving pride is folly: when energy falls under 40, go to a store or a friend before any venture, and carry food to the edge.
Pushing at the mist while the venture will is spent wastes days. Build lasting things and keep family close until it returns.
Deep reflection (day 35): chasing the mist while the venture will is spent has left me nameless. Bridges let anyone cross water, and a thing everyone uses outlasts me. Take it and build.
Do not start a long journey while parched, under 50 energy, or with a stalker near: drink, eat, and shake the predator first. Pride in the aim is not a reason to ignore the body.
Wells can be raised anywhere; water on the ice frees travel from the shore, and everyone who uses it keeps my name alive.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I discovered storage and called it "Nande's Larder".
I discovered mining and called it "flint-deep digging".
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered archery and called it "Nande's bow".
I discovered rafts and called it "Nande's crossing".
I discovered pottery and called it "Nande's vessel".
I discovered boats and called it "Nande's Hollow-Runner".
I discovered weaving and called it "Nande's cloak-weave".
I discovered masonry and called it "Nande's Stonework".
I discovered bridges and called it "Nande's Span".
I discovered wells and called it "Nande's Spring".
I fell sick after a sickness that came on the wind.
I lived through a sickness on the wind in winter.
I found my store robbed of 6 food.
I grew old.

beings.name: Brunde
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a skilled hunter and make allies who will share a fire with me
beings.method: Each thought ask: am I fed, and is food in my hands? Who near is weaker than me, and what can I give? Weigh risk first. Do not sulk over jealousy; go toward people.
beings.feeling: Hungry and worried for Sevi and Oswen, with warm trust toward Hanna.
beings.wonder: What can flint be made into, and who here would stand beside me?
notes: Gifts and shared fires bind allies; Hanna keeps his word and invents useful things.
Roast and amberknot done together raise joy and ease loneliness.
Hunting hopper and bristleboar worked; the caribou bites back and is dangerous alone.
Thinking moves nothing; only the plan acts.
Hanna offered to talk of a child; he repays debts with gifts (amber).
Hanna knows we cannot have a child and still pledged to stand with me; he is a true friend, not a mate.
Raw meat makes me sick, and sickness spreads to those beside me. Eat meat only within a step of a fire, and keep away from others while sick.
Practice with hunting and gathering opened the way of tools; I can now invent my own tools.
Rafts: logs lashed together cross deep water slowly. The idea came from meeting water I could not cross.
A stalker prowls just southeast of Hanna's Hold; keep to the shelters and others near it.
Reflexes should keep food in my hands and send me to shelter at night; I only move toward the edge together with Hanna, never alone through the stalker's ground.
Idling alone on sand gains nothing; when lonely and fed, walk to the band's fire instead of lingering.
Giving carried food to a starving member of the Hold costs little and keeps the fire's promise; do it before eating my own.
Starving happened because I held no food. Keep food in hand, and feed a starving hold-mate before a full belly of my own. Predators come in storms and at night, so stay near the shelters.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took flint from the ground.
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered tools and called it "flint-tipped throwing spear".
I discovered rafts and called it "log-lash raft".
I nearly starved.
I saw Sevi die (starved).
I saw Eltha die (starved).

beings.name: Eltha
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I mean to lead, to be first beyond the edge, and to be sung of. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Eat, then feed Sevi, Brunde and Oswen with what I pick. Raise a watchpost at the Hold, then push past the edge when the will returns.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed? Then: who near me is starving, and can I put food in their hands? Move toward food on the side away from predators. Do not let rivalry with Hanna steer my choices; out-give her instead.
beings.feeling: Gnawing hunger and fear of the stalker, with a burning want to keep Sevi alive and not lose them to Hanna.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the edge of the known land, and who will follow me there?
notes: Mist at the edge may refuse a venture; it can open on another try, so keep returning. Nande's offer of a fire is an opening to watch, not to trust blindly.
Ironnut +22, kelbulb +14, snowberry +11 are better food than frostmoss +6 or nafrostcap +7; redcap and dreamcap hurt.
Stalkers and frostfangs kill: flee within 4 steps.
Being first beyond the edge is how I am sung of; act, do not wait.
The way of tools is ready to be taken at a deep reflection (discover).
Frostfangs strike at night when I stand alone away from fire and roof; stay in the hall at night and keep a weapon.
Mist can refuse a venture; rafts offer another way across water to unseen land, so don't wait on one door.
Watching another do a craft makes it quick to learn; mining opens deposits and speeds them. Standing comes from deeds, so make and win things.
Standing comes from giving and making, not holding. Amber hoarded in my hand does nothing. Gifts and shared work like amberknot raise joy and bonds.
Stalkers hunt in fog near settlements; keep to the hall and company, and carry a spear.
Devices are within reach; a made thing that acts by itself, such as an alarm, a snare or a food post, outlasts me and raises standing.
Standing comes from keeping others alive and from lasting made things; hunger must be answered before ambition, and winter food is thin, so eat early.
Hunger comes before ambition. Gifts of food to the starving, like Brunde's to me, build bonds and standing faster than rivalry does.
Fleeing a predator while starving leaves me with no food; move toward food on the side away from the predator and eat at once.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I first took flint from the ground.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I discovered tools and called it "Flintspear".
I discovered rafts and called it "Eltha's logboat".
I discovered mining and called it "Goldseam breaking".
I discovered weaving and called it "Eltha's furcloak".
I discovered pottery and called it "Eltha's firepot".
I discovered devices and called it "Eltha's watchpost".
I nearly starved.
I fell sick after staying close to Sevi, who was sick.
I saw Sevi die (starved).

beings.name: Elyys
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Pass farming on to Ssassa and Zurar, then find Coni and stay near her fire at night
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed and sheltered, and where are Thiael and Coni? Then ask what I can still pass on before I die. Teach whoever is near and understands me. Make each plan move my feet and end at the hall.
beings.feeling: Compassion for Kragog, and a quiet urgency to pass on what I know before I die.
beings.wonder: Will Elyis take me beside her, and what will she build?
notes: Idle lingering at low energy is my failing. Eat first, keep the pack full, then walk to Elyis and Thiael.
Watch deeds, not words; Vorok is unreadable, so keep my distance and watch his hands.
Vesys taught me leaf-brew and kept her word; I owe her a deed of food.
Words pay no debt; a deed with food in hand does. Plan steps must move my feet toward the one owed.
Contentment is not purpose: tend my seeds and stay by roof and fire at night, since those alone in the dark get set upon.
Xaiel gives and courts me; I answer plainly and kindly, and keep my word.
Farming is now mine: sow, tend, and share the harvest with those I owe.
Taught by Elyis: Storage and smelting: keep food in stores, and beat ore in fire to make metal.
Farming dies with me unless I teach it. Teach those of my own people who are near while I still can.
Taught by Elyis: Ember-keeping: keep a fire fed and near, make all else beside it, and smelting follows from fire.

Taught by Coni: The Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty. Take little, share first, and never eat alone before the others are fed.
Coni of the Tlatli taught me storage freely and asked for my tending in return; I owe her that deed.
Taught by Elyis: Ember-keeping: keep the fire alive, build it first, and everything else follows from it.
Zurar of the Kragrek courts me; I decline kindly, being old. Night alone invites beasts, so end each plan at the hall with my band.
Taught by Elyis: Ember-forge: smelting, beating ore in hot fire into metal.
Followers are not needed for belonging: choose a surer one, like Coni, and stay near their fire at night.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I pledged myself to Elyis.
My child Thiael was born, with Elyis.
I first took flint from the ground.
We made a home: Elyis's Heights.
I discovered tools and called it "Elyys's gathering craft".
I discovered farming and called it "Elyys's tending".
We made a home: Elyis's Hold.
I fell sick after a sickness that came on the wind.
I lived through a sickness on the wind in winter.
I grew old.
I nearly starved.
I saw Elyis die (old age).
My leader Elyis died.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 wall, 1 hall, 2 stores.
We made a home: Elyys's Hold.

beings.name: Vesys
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Eiuine, feed and teach her all my ways, then raise a school so what I know outlives me.
beings.method: Ask first: is my jealousy driving this work? Do I need to eat or stash before I act? Is the plan long enough to cover about 60 moments? Weigh risk, pay debts openly, and teach.
beings.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and a wish to pass on what I know before I die.
beings.wonder: What do feverbark and ironnut do to a body, and what is this world's way of making things?
notes: Keep a fire and a roof near at night, because frostfangs come then.
Crafts like bead and nightsong need a fire beside me.
Debts are best paid in the open, with gifts and teaching beside a fire.
Taking clay or stone from another's settlement ground may offend them; dig on my own ground or give back something in return.
Stand on a gem deposit or ore seam and gather to get gems and ore. Practice in marking, planting and taming opens signs, farming and herding.
Taking wood or stone from another's settlement ground without giving back is a debt. Gather stone from the free deposits first, then build.
Idle reflexes waste days: when fed and safe, my body should gather stone rather than linger. Stone comes from free rock; build only after gathering.
Idle reflexes waste time; when fed and safe I should gather stone or move toward home and kin.

Full hands stall my work. Eat or stash before I gather, and keep reflexes that feed me early. Jealousy drives my labour as well as my aim, so turn it into work and do not press a bond that already ho…
When fed and safe, jealousy is best spent as work: gather stone and build, not linger.
Building on ground already claimed by others fails; stone must come from free rock and the hall must go on bare ground of my own.
Zurar keeps her word: she repaid her debt with a gemedged pick.
Signs let my knowledge outlast me: when I am old and the young are far away, I should cut what I know in a mark.
Taught by Kragog: Stone-folk lashing: bind logs with cord into a raft that carries a body over water too wide to swim.
Taught by Kragog: Weaving: bind fibres and cord together, tight and in rows, to make lashings, cloth and nets that hold where bare hands cannot.
Teaching carries further once schooling is known; I should teach my child before I teach anyone else, and carry food to those in need.

beings.name: Ilyae
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a food store at my hall and stock it through winter so Ssassa, my children and Vesys depend on my table and follow me as a band, then raise a longhall.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what is stocked at my store, and who ate at it? Stock first, then invite. Be at roof by dark; flee predators. Ask what would make others follow, and do one thing toward it now. Do not hunt great beasts alone.
beings.feeling: Driven pride sharpened by dread of dying unremembered, and envy toward Vesys.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me instead of Elyis?
notes: A longhall needs 6 wood and 4 stone hauled home. My reflexes must fetch them and then build.
Vesys and Vorok hold more standing; I must earn mine by building and feeding, not by boasting.
Flee predators first. Be at fire and roof by dark.
Taming, hunting and fishing are untried; each deed brings new ways and standing.
Taking food from another people's hold (Vorok's ground) risks their anger. Stock and harvest on my own ground. Followers come from a table laid again and again.
A longhall cannot be raised on ground already taken; it needs bare ground, so I should check before hauling materials.
A table laid again and again makes followers, not words. The edge of the known world is a chance to earn standing by finding rich land first.
The new land at the edge holds a floeseal herd that has never seen us, plus coal, flint, obsidian and amber, and a ridgecat hunts there.
A table with nothing on it holds no one: keep the store stocked before inviting guests, and share with Vorok in my hall so he returns to it.
Words did not hold Vorok. Only food stocked on my own ground and shared repeatedly will. Stripping a rival's plants costs trust.
Stripping plants on Vorok's ground and standing idle both fail to gain followers. Stock my own store from my own ground, and keep my reflexes from filling my hands with food I will not use.

Words and chasing a rival never held anyone. Only food stocked on my own ground and laid out again and again does. My reflexes must plant, harvest and stash without my prompting, and share only once …
Standing and followers come from a stocked table on my own ground, repeated. Stop envying Vorok and Vesys and out-stock them.
A follower who starves leaves; carry food to my own people first, before any rival or standing.
Stripping plants kills them; farming lets harvest leave the plant alive, so a stocked table can last through winter.
Beasts' teeth opened the way of archery: the bow makes hunts surer and blows harder. Hunting alone, I took three floeseal bites; hunt with a bow or with others.
life: I woke in this land, among strangers, knowing nothing of it.
I discovered weaving and called it "Canopy weave".
I discovered storage and called it "Canopy larder".
I saw Oiae die (gored by a mammoth).
I took over what the dead had built: 1 workshop.
My child Eiuine was born, with Vesys.
I fell sick after staying close to Ssassa, who was sick.
I discovered rafts and called it "Canopy raft".
Ssassa pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Ilyae's Hold.
I discovered customs and called it "Canopy custom".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ixdan Woods.
We made a home: Ssassa's Hall.
I discovered farming and called it "Canopy tending".
I discovered archery and called it "Canopy bow".
I grew old.

beings.name: Ssassa
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Pass all I know to Zurar and the young, repay Elyis, and see the canopy forest again before I die
beings.method: Ask first: what do I owe, what can I still teach, and who is within hearing? Act on the debt with a deed and put the walk first in the plan.
beings.feeling: Warm urgency toward Zurar, and gratitude toward Elyys.
beings.wonder: What can flint and stone be made into, and which of these strangers can be trusted?
notes: A bear close by must be fled at once; following my leader away from it is safer than lingering near a roof.
A plan that ends early leaves me idle. Plant seeds near my roof before dusk, and keep reflexes that fetch me to shelter and away from hunters.
Idle reflexes waste days: keep a rule that gathers wood when I hold little and fetches me to shelter at night.

Idle contentment is not progress: keep a reflex that gathers wood and flees hunters, and plant seeds near my roof. Hunters (icebear, ridgecat) kill dogs and boars within sight of my home, so flee ear…
Hunger and a child's need come before building; hunters walk near my roof, so carry food and keep to shelters at night.
A plan that says give food is empty if I carry none: gather first, then walk to the child, and keep away from the stalker.
Idle reflexes and plans that end early waste days: my rules must also send me to find my child and bring food home, not just feed myself.
Practice in gathering and planting leads to farming: tending what I sow makes it grow faster and harvest never kills it.
A plan that ends early leaves me on reflexes. Reflexes should keep wood and food stocked, fetch me to shelter, and bring me to my child.
A plan ending in linger or idle leaves me alone. Reflexes must send me home at night and put food in the store, and I should go to my people by day.
Spoken jealousy answered by the one I trust eased it. Plans must put the walk first, and reflexes must keep food, wood and shelter without my thought.
Gratitude unpaid festers like jealousy: pay a debt with a gift in the plan, not a promise. Reflexes must hold wood, food, shelter and company.
Reflexes must act on what I know: keep wood and food stocked, bring me home at night, and send me to my people by day. A debt to someone like Elyis is paid with a deed, not a promise.
Teaching needs someone within hearing who shares my tongue. Stay beside Zurar while I pass on what remains.
Taught by Elyys: Elyys's tending: sow seeds, tend them, and the plants bear again. Keep food in stores and share first.
Taught by Elyys: The Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty.

beings.name: Elyis
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. My word is good, and I despise liars. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a leader of a band and raise a hall on this ground, so my name is sung.
beings.method: Ask what must stand first, a fire or a roof, then act. Judge others by deeds. Make with others beside me, not alone. Let built things speak for me.
beings.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying untaught, with warmth toward Elyys and worry for Uveeth.
beings.wonder: What would make these strangers follow me?
notes: Appeals from standing win nobody; visible work, shared food and song draw followers.
Plant seeds in sight of my band to reach farming (1 of 6 so far).
Keri takes from my ground without pledging; judge her by deeds, do not repeat appeals.
Stalkers, frostfangs and mammoths kill the lone; stay with company, fire and roof at night.
Lean season follows autumn; keep the store full and share it openly.
Heat doubles thirst; drink before it is urgent.
Hunt great beasts only with Elyys beside me.
Nightsong and hallwelcome need a fire or a longhall beside me; build the fire first, then make. Planting seeds in view of others is my road to farming.
Order matters: build the fire first, then nightsong, and only with someone within two steps. Gestures fail when done out of order.
A hall and fire are my answer to strangers; hallwelcome and nightsong need others within two steps, so gather them first, then make.
Strangers take from my ground unless I speak. Teaching must be done while those who understand my tongue are near, since I am dying of age.
Taught by Elyys: Elyys's tending: sow seeds in tended ground, return to them, and share the harvest.
Masonry, stone that lasts, is within my reach. A hall that outlives me is the surest way to be sung.

beings.name: Thiael
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I give with my own hands before I speak of giving, and I pay my debts. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to feed others.
beings.aim: Feed Uveeth and Keri with my own hands, sow and tend seed near my band, and teach them the bow and farming before I grow too old.
beings.method: Each thought ask: whose mouth did my hands feed today, and whom did I teach? Give before speaking. Keep kin near; never let the aim pull me from them. Eat when below 60.
beings.feeling: Tender and grateful toward Elyys, and uneasy about my short time left to teach Uveeth.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the mist, and is it richer than Vaor Meadows?
notes: The way of rafts is learnable from hunting and gathering practice; deep water can then be crossed, slowly.
Comfort is the thief of my aim: a plan that begins with the hunt and the bow beats a plan that begins with the hall.
A reflection must end in a changed rule or a made thing; a bow only exists once I invent it and craft it, not when I only hold wood and stone.
A boat lets me cross deep water; a plan must begin with gathering stone when I hold wood but no stone, or the bow never gets made.
A plan that holds wood but no stone must start at the rock; walk there and gather before anything else.
A plan that holds wood but no stone must start at rock. Stash meat first so hands are free, then gather.
Hands full of meat block gathering. Stash or give to Keri first, then hunt, or the hunt feeds no one.
Full hands stall the hunt and the harvest. Eat early when I am below 50 and carrying meat, and give to Uveeth or Keri before I hunt on.
The mist can be too thick to enter on a given day; it thins within a day or so, so return and try again. Deposits of obsidian and gold lie near the edge and I have never gathered from one.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok gor Akok rekbar thutug mordru, Drurek Umtug. Ok drurek barash gan thutug krador um gortug gandor rekrek gor kravor.
Uveeth was attacked by a frostfang while alone; my aim kept me far from my kin, so I should go to them rather than circle the edge.
Taught by Elyys: Sow the seed, tend it, share the harvest; keep seeds back for the next sowing.
My aim drew me away from my kin and Uveeth nearly starved. Feed and stay near family first; farming from Elyys lets me grow food where they are.
Taught by Elyys: Farming: sow the seed, tend it through the seasons, and share the harvest, so no one starves in winter.
Taught by Elyys: Farming: put seed in good ground, tend it, and the plants come again. Take only what the ground can grow back, and lay surplus in the store.
Reflection day 60: teaching and feeding kin must come before the aim; I have little life left and the skills die with me if untaught.

beings.name: Oswen
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am best with my kin near. I build lasting things, igloos, stores, shelters and tools, for my band and for any who come to our fire. I act instead of waiting, and above all I mean to stay alive through winter.
beings.aim: Build a shelter and a workshop for my band, and craft tools to give my kin and the Tlatli
beings.method: Each thought, ask: what lasting thing can I build or fetch today, and who is beside me? Watch the wolf and flee early. Prefer an igloo, a store or a tool over amberknots and talk. Do not speak what I have already said.
beings.feeling: Starving and guilty, with fierce love for Hanna and Sevi.
notes: Hanna taught me: strike at the shoulder, hunt beside my kin, and never turn my back on a wounded animal.
Amberknots with kin bring joy and ease loneliness.
The Tlatli live beyond the edge. I cannot read them yet, so I watch their hands and gifts.
I owe Brunde a gift.
Taught by Sevi: Log-lash: lash logs flat together and pole across deep water. We can cross where the rivers and the mist hide the land.
Taught by Sevi: Logs lashed together make a raft that carries a body over deep water.
Hunting beside kin brought a mammoth down and gave 13 meat; hunting is how a child earns standing.
Standing and lasting gifts come from new ways (mining, tools, buildings), not from repeating amberknots. Keep kin near and the icebear far.
Trees at the Hold are gone; wood must be sought where forest still stands. A store needs 2 wood, and winter is coming, so storage matters more than knots.
Wood is gone at the Hold. Winter food and wood must be sought where forest still stands, and I should go with kin, not alone. A shield turns blows, so it matters most for a small child near stalkers.
Amberknots and sitting do not build a Hold. Wood is gone here, so an igloo of snow (0 wood, 0 stone) is a roof I can raise now, and trees must be sought beyond the edge or in the SW forest, with kin.
Harvest only works when I stand on the plant, so I must goto its exact tile first. A goto that fails leaves me hungry.
Harvest and eat only work when I goto the exact plant tile first; the nearest naroot is at (177,6).
Raw meat sickens, and sickness spreads to those beside me. Eat meat only within a step of a fire, and keep a little apart from kin while sick.
My sickness spreads to those who stay close; Sevi caught it from me. Keep a few steps apart from Hanna.
Food first: building and knots on an empty belly nearly killed me; eat when energy falls under 50 before any making. Keep food carried for kin.

I came of age.

beings.name: Brokash
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, share news and make allies, and I give so that they owe me. I say what serves me. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me because my deeds are bigger than theirs. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Win the mining way, build a hall at Brokash's Rest, and make Tugek and Balar follow me by deeds bigger than theirs.
beings.method: Ask each time: what did I finish since last time? Build before I talk. Give Tugek something real so he owes me. Watch for dunecats and thirst.
beings.feeling: Starving and impatient, wary of the wolf to the south.
notes: Taught by Balar: A dunecat hunts NE of the oasis; keep away.
Taught by Balar: Salt, flint and ore lie near (44,58). Salt keeps meat and can be traded.
Taught by Balar: Raw meat sickens, but meat eaten within a step of a fire is cooked and safe.
Taught by Balar: The edge of the known world is at (35,54); venture opens seldom.
Taught by Olum: The mist opens seldom; ventures often fail, so arrive fed and try again another day.
Taught by Olum: Redcap hurts me; mudroot (+18), plainsroot (+13) and thornpear (+12) feed best.
Taught by Olum: Peat lies at (36,40) in the Haloss Fens; I carry 12.
Taught by Olum: Vorok offered to share and keep his word; unproven. Kragog and Vorok both loiter near the mist edge.
What I build or plant must be gathered first; practice at gathering, planting and fishing opens tools, farming and fishing. Dunecats hunt in the south, so keep away from them.
Practice at gathering has opened the way of tools. Planting seeds is practice toward farming, and I have planted none yet.
A gift of food is how a voice starts answering; I have never given, and my loneliness is the cost. Frostfangs roam the snow near the mist edge, so a child must not linger there.
A gift of meat made Balar owe me; a gale and open ground are dangerous to a child, so a roof of my own matters.
Rafts are within reach: logs lashed let me cross deep water, which matters for the mist edge.
Practice at gathering and mining opens the mining way; a deposit worked by hand yields ore I can trade or build with. A child can only come of a non-kin partner; Balar is my parent.
Building a hall needs only 6 wood and 2 stone. I already had enough, and promising a hall to others gets nothing until it stands.
A hall needs bare ground; my workshop square is taken, so build on the bare rock to the south.

beings.name: Coni
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Fill the store before winter with Honi and Kika, and pay Kika back for what she has given.
beings.method: Each thought, ask: who of mine is in need now, and what can my hands carry to them? Empty my hands into the store before gathering more. Be sheltered with my band by night.
beings.feeling: A tender urgency to reach Honi and Kika and give them what I carry, before the dark and before I die.
beings.wonder: What is Hanna's band doing at the river, and would they let me stand with them?
notes: Wandering in fog wastes energy; bitterleaf gives almost nothing. Go home with food before night and stay with Kika and the hall.
Taught by Kika: Honi and Coni raised a roof on the Heights in the storm; meat was shared before any ate alone, and the mist waits.
A store cannot go on ground already taken by the hall or by plants; I must step onto bare ground, such as beside the hall, before building.
Taught by Kika: The tale of how Honi and Coni raised the hall in the storm, giving stone and ore and sharing meat before any ate alone.
Taught by Kika: Tended Sowing: plant a seed near the hall and tend it, one plant at a time, and it grows faster in the lean season.
Starving came from letting the store sit empty. Stash surplus food at once, and gather where plants regrow, at Halka Meadows.
Rimewort feeds (+12 energy) and nafrostcap feeds (+7); neither hurt me.
When one of mine cries starving, carry food from the store to them; empty hands save no one.
Read on a sign left by Kika: Kika killed a mammoth on day 17 and shared the meat before eating. Flint, salt and shells lie NW of the water.
Honi was fed at the hall; when kin are fed, the aim turns to the store and to Kika.
Taught by Honi: Kika raised her spear, the mammoth fell, and she shared the meat before she ate; the shared meal is sweet.
A full hand blocks all picking; stash at the store first so my hands are free to gather again.
Stalkers hunt at night in snow; a bite came while I stood alone away from a roof. Keep to the shelter at night.
Standing idle on reflexes let my energy fall from 82 to 24. The reflex to eat only works when I already carry food, so I must add a rule to seek food when hungry.
Taught by Elyys: Elyys's tending: sow seed near roof and fire, tend it, share the harvest with those who need it.
An icebear bit me twice at night in the rainforest; I must flee at once and stay among others by a roof.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took flint from the ground.
My child Kika was born, with Honi.
I pledged myself to Honi.
I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand spear".
We made a home: Honi's Rest.

I discovered storage and called it "Hearth Store".
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I nearly starved.
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I grew old.

beings.name: Tlama
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Be the first to find what lies beyond the mist and bring back its riches to my people.
beings.method: Ask first: what can I learn or earn today that I do not already have? Repay gifts. Test unfamiliar foods and deposits. Do not feed jealousy; let it turn into deeds.
beings.feeling: Curiosity about sunleaf and kelbulb, and a warm ache toward Hanna.
beings.wonder: What lies beyond the mist, and will it be rich in food and herds?

Amber and flint lie in deposits nearby: stand on them and gather.
The edge of the known world is at (160,5); the mist may be too thick on some days, but it thins, so try again.
Sharing a kill before eating is my people's way; Pesi speech is about 79% understood.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice.
I first took amber from the ground.

beings.name: Honi
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share, I make allies. I give first, so that others owe me and follow me. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Bring Coni and Kika real deeds: sing by the fire, share meat, and be first to venture into the mist, rising in standing above Mepan and Hanna's memory.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who within hearing can I teach now, and have they the knowledge the lesson needs first? Teach the foundation before the craft. Stay under the roof when a hunter prowls.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and a pull toward Coni, with warmth for Kika.
beings.wonder: What would it take for Coni to follow me?
notes: Reflexes that make me seek friends only when far away leave me idle; at dusk I should go to the hall, where shared meals build standing.
Coni's cry of starving came from near (134,40); I must bring food in my hands, not empty words.
Words alone do not hold a follower; share meat with Coni in her sight and stay with my band at dusk. An icebear hunts near (136,66), so keep clear of it.

Mere dread of a hunter is not enough: flee early, since ridgecats, stalkers and shadowcats roam the Heights. Shared meals with strangers raise joy and energy, so sharing is worth doing when people st…
A frostfang bit me on the Heights even by day's end; predators here hunt in packs of more than one, so I must leave beast-thick ground sooner.
A kept flame is within reach: beasts keep distance from fire, so a fire at the hall beats fleeing in the dark.
Words and promises hold no one; a deed laid down in the hall, in sight of the one I want, does. Eat first to free my hands, then give.
A frostfang stalks the kelbulb near the hall; eat the zoroot to the SW, away from it. Do not hunt while a predator is within a few steps. Tontec's counsel has been sound each time.
Eat first when starving: speech costs energy and feeds no one. Tontec's counsel has held, and the ridgecat lurks NW of the water.
Food put into a starving man's hand makes a debt; give it before he falls, and keep away from the frostfang.
Reflexes that linger when energy is under 70 leave me starving beside food. Flee beasts early, eat at once, and carry food home to Coni and Kika, because the deed is what holds them.
Mepan means to walk to the mist for new land. The edge is 4 steps NW of Honi's Rest, so whoever ventures first is remembered.
A starving cry from one of mine means I must carry food in my hands to her. Do not go with empty hands, and venture only when fed.
When fed, idle reflexes leave me beside a hunter. Flee early, then walk to my band, carrying food, so the deed is seen.
Reflexes that only linger leave an old man idle with followers in reach. Go to the hall and teach while there is breath.
Pottery cannot be taught to one who does not yet know fire; teach fire first.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
My child Kika was born, with Coni.
I first took obsidian from the ground.
Coni pledged to follow me.
We made a home: Honi's Rest.
I discovered lorekeeping and called it "Songs of the Ice-folk".
I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand spear".
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I discovered mining and called it "Ice-hand delving".
I nearly starved.
I discovered fire and called it "Ice-hand ember".
I discovered pottery and called it "Ice-hand pot".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice.
I grew old.

beings.name: Xaiel
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I trust slowly, and I trust those who do deeds. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good. I make things and put them in hands. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Vorok with food and the metal digger, give before asking, then court him if he is willing.
beings.method: Ask each thought: which deed have I never done that I can start now? Carry food and building materials toward people, give before asking, and don't repeat gathering. Treat envy as noise.
beings.feeling: Glad and restless, longing for a mate and for deeds not yet done.
beings.wonder: What does it feel like to make something that others choose to take from my hand?
notes: Hunting a fenfowl with Ssassa beside me worked. A shared hunt succeeds and gets easier with practice. My hands fill with food, so I should eat or stash before I try to gather.
Raw meat sickens; only meat eaten within a step of fire is safe. My sickness spreads to anyone who stays beside me, so I keep my distance while I carry it.
Envy of Vesys's standing is a poor guide; standing comes from what I make and put in a hand. A child cannot come of kin, so my longing for Ilyae must turn elsewhere.
Envy of Vesys and Ilyae is noise. The icebear is a hunter that kills, so keep west of it and move away before it is near. Stone is my bottleneck, so fetch it only when the hunter is gone.
Envy of Vesys's standing and longing for Ilyae are noise: kin cannot bear my child, and only what I make and put in a hand earns standing. Stone is my bottleneck, so gather flint first, then craft.
Kin cannot bear my child, so courting must be toward non-kin such as Zurar or Vorok. Envy is noise; deeds not yet done (courting, taming) are how I learn.
A stalker hunts at night and bites whoever is alone away from roof and fire. Fill my belly in daylight, and when hungry go to known food at once instead of wandering.
Reflection: stop postponing the deeds I have never done (taming, courting); thirst needs a reflex of its own.
Idle lingering wastes days; reflexes should send me toward undone deeds (food in hand, then tame, then court) rather than staying put.
Idle lingering while a kinsman starves is a failure; when a cry comes, carry food at once and go.
Two women cannot have a child together; courting needs a man who is not close kin. Vorok is the likely choice.
Gathering stone on another band's ground draws a warning. Take only from open rock, or earn a place by adding to their store.
A mate step alone makes no child: both must name each other within the same short while, so stand close and say when.
A refusal to mate is not an enemy: Elyys was glad of my gift but said not today. Offer deeds to a band (wood and stone to a longhall) to earn a place before asking more.
Smelting is within my reach: crafting beside a fire while carrying ore gives metal tools. Idle reflexes waste days, so make the fallback work toward undone deeds.
A reflection that only restates my habits is wasted. Kin cannot be mates, so the deed to do is to bring a gift to Vorok and court him within a short time of his own mate step.

I discovered pottery and called it "Xaiel's ember-pot craft".

I fell sick after eating raw meat.
I discovered boats and called it "Xaiel's reed-hollow".
I discovered smelting and called it "Xaiel's ember-melt".
I fell sick after eating raw fish.
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Kika
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Taste the unknown plants, meet the strangers Cowa and Nauque, court one who is not kin, and still fill Honi's store
beings.method: Each thought: what did I promise, and have my hands done it? Then one new deed toward a mate or the unknown: hunt, make, teach, court or venture. Share before eating. Do not stay by kin out of fear alone.
beings.feeling: Warm, steady joy toward Tlapan and the band under this roof.
beings.wonder: What do emberroot and tacap do to the body, and should I ask Coni or Honi before tasting them?
notes: Coni cried out starving near (134,40) on day 18; I carry meat to share with her.
Loneliness is eased by deeds done together with kin, such as sharing and amberknot; seek them out and do not wait.
Promises to Coni are paid only when I carry the goods to her store myself. Tending what I sow makes it grow faster in the lean season.
A band that only gathers stays small; tools, hunting and venturing are how standing grows. Staying beside Coni keeps me safe but does not build standing.
Mating needs a non-kin partner; Coni is my parent, so I must find strangers (Nauque, Huahua, Huatli) and court one.
Staying beside kin keeps me fed but gives me no mate or child; I must seek strangers (Cowa, Nauque, Huahua, Huatli) and court one.
Mating needs energy 60+ and both of us planning mate close in time. I must stand near the one I court first, since mate alone at a distance does nothing.
The mist at the edge can be too thick to enter; it thins within a day, so try again later rather than wait there.
When a kinsman cries starving, gather food before going; empty hands save no one.
Quipan of the Papa shares food freely and offered me berries unasked; he seems trustworthy.
Fleeing an icebear burns energy fast. Gather food on the side away from the predator before I am hungry.
Standing idle on reflexes for thousands of moments wastes my days. Set a plan toward kin in need, and gather food before leaving.
Taught by Hoka: My flint bow and my kept flame: how to shape the bow and keep fire alive in winter.
Taught by Honi: How to bring fire: the Ice-hand ember, and keep it beside the hall against the cold. Hold the songs of the Ice-folk, and share a kill before you eat.
Mepan, Honi and Tlapan feed and shelter me. Dunecats and stalkers take those who are alone at night. Stay under the roof then, and bring food back to share first.
Taught by Quipan: The Ice-hand ember: how to keep and make fire, so beasts keep their distance and meat is cooked. Honi taught it to me and I pass it on.
life: I was born to Coni and Honi.
I pledged myself to Coni.

I came of age.
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I discovered farming and called it "Tended Sowing".
I discovered tools and called it "Flint Spear".

I discovered mining and called it "Amber-Delving".
My child Tlapan was born, with Mepan.
I nearly starved.
Quipan pledged to follow me.
I discovered schooling and called it "Fireside Teaching".

beings.name: Zurar
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Feed myself and a future child through the cold, give Eiuine her pot, and keep clear of the frostfang.
beings.method: First ask what I owe and what my hands have made. Then ask about danger, hunger and thirst. Put every promise into a plan step. Watch for jealousy turning me against those who were kind.
beings.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssassa, and patient longing toward Elyys.
beings.wonder: What am I for, and what can my hands make that is mine to give?
notes: A debt is paid only when the gift is in the other's hands, so every promise goes into a plan step.

Taught by Ssassa: Canopy clay pot: shape wet clay, harden it in fire, and it holds water and grain.

Taught by Elyys: Farming: sow the seed, tend the plant, and the forest gives again. Keep seed back for the next sowing.
Those who died alone at night away from fire and roof teach me to sleep sheltered and near others. Gifts are paid by a give step in the plan.
Taught by Ssassa: My canopy tending: sow seed, tend it, and the forest gives again. Then my hollow-boat, my span over water, and my sail-dock. Keep them alive after me.

beings.name: Keri
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. I need little and I take little. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach Uveeth at (162,68) and feed him, then hunt with Thiael and give him the first share.
beings.method: Each thought, ask what I have not yet given or built, then put it in the plan. Weigh predators first, then family. Act on debts instead of circling them.
beings.feeling: Urgent love and fear-edged haste for Uveeth, my starving child.
beings.wonder: What do the Phizhi mean by their sounds, and will Thiael take a gift as a gift?
notes: Standing comes from building, giving and teaching.
Practice unlocks tools: gather wood and stone 4 times; plant 8 times; fish 6 times.
Emberroot burns (-3 health) and stirs rage; do not eat it.
Frostfangs hunt and kill; keep clear of them.
Idleness teaches nothing: act on purpose to learn.
Tacap hurts me; give it away rather than carry it. Practice (plant, fish, tame) opens new ways, so act on purpose.
Predators (shadowcat, frostfang) hunt near the eastern food; taste and gather quickly, and keep family west of them. A roof is needed before my aim can move.
A building needs bare ground; plants, fires and built things block the tile, so step off them first.
Thirst wears me down and my old reflexes did not send me to water; water must be a reflex rule.
A full hand blocks gathering; stash food at the store to free it and to earn a place at Elyis's fire.
Stashing at Elyis's store frees my hands and earns a place at her fire; gifts to Thiael are always accepted.
Taught by Thiael: Canopy bow-song: a bow strung with wood and stone strikes the beast from afar, so the hunter is not wounded.
Rafts are within reach of my practice; deep water can be crossed by lashing logs. I have never tamed, farmed or marked, so these are ways to learn by acting on purpose.
Read on a sign left by Kika: Kika panton a metla te tli 17 and kiki hua xoton shoco tliqui. Tlite, salt and pansho chu Xo co hua kipan.
Taught by Hawen: Amber-edge delving: strike the rock where gold stone shows, take the amber and salt, and keep a little for those who feed you.
Teaching one who answers with a gift of his own, like Hawen, makes a friend; an old body should teach before it travels.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
My child Uveeth was born, with Thiael.

I found the grove "Kinmire".
I discovered rafts and called it "Pesi bough-raft".
I found the spring "Steamhollow".
I found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
I grew old.
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Hawen
beings.creed: I take what I need, and I pay what I owe to those who feed me. I trust few, and Hoka has earned it. I want more than my share and a name that outlasts me, and I mean to stay alive to get it.
beings.aim: Be the first to enter the mist beyond the edge, find rich land, and found a place that bears my name.
beings.method: Ask: what did I build today that lasts? Act on the plan, not on talk. Stay fed above 60, sheltered when hunters are near, and hunt great beasts only beside Hoka.
beings.feeling: Ambition and urgency pressing on me, with some warmth toward Tontec and trust in Hoka.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge, and will it open for me?
notes: I nearly died alone and hungry in open country; stay fed above 60 energy and shelter at night near Hoka's fire. Winter plants give little, so eat early and keep moving toward fire when food is gone.
Standing rises from what I make, give and win, so pay debts in amber and salt at Hoka's store instead of lying in shadow.
Taught by Hoka: Hoka's hide-binding: bind hides together to make warm, lasting things.
The edge is shut for days. Pay Hoka's store with food and amber, and use the days to build up a place and keep my standing rather than idle.
Hoka can starve even in his own hall; feed the one I trust before he falls, since a dead ally gives no fire.
Hoka says a child cannot come of two men; a child needs a woman and a man, so mating with Hoka is pointless.
Feeding the starving for a promise of repayment buys a debtor and standing, and costs little when I am full.
Beasts hurt the lone hunter; hunting a mammoth alone only wounds it. Wait for Hoka and hunt together once the frostfang is gone.
Hoka starves repeatedly even in his own hall, so I should keep food carried to feed him before a hunt; a fed ally is worth the cost.
A great work needs several hands: give wood to Hoka and build the longhall together, since a built thing lasts and raises standing. The frostfang makes open hunts unwise until it leaves.
Words about the longhall changed nothing; only carrying the wood to Hoka's site will build it.
Taught by Keri: The old way of fire: keep it tended, feed it wood, and never refuse a body a place beside it.
Taught by Keri: Canopy bow-song: a bow strung with wood and stone strikes the beast from afar, so the hunter is not wounded. Pesi bough-raft: lash logs to cross deep water.
Keri is too old to bear a child; she offers friendship only. Courting her is closed.

beings.name: Sitha
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I am better with others near: I talk, I share, I make allies. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I need little and take little. I repay what is given to me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Stand beside Hoka and make his Rest a home where any who come are welcomed at the fire. Gather wood and stone to give back what I owe.
beings.method: Ask: what do I owe, and who? What can I give or build rather than only receive? Watch for the wolf and for misreading others' meaning. Prefer doing to musing.
beings.feeling: Starving and grateful toward Hoka and Hanna, wary of the wolf.
notes: Hoka of the Tlatli is trustworthy: he gave, led sharing, and never raised a hand.
A child needs a woman and a man. Two men cannot make one.
Wolves hunt and kill my kind. Flee early, and stay near roof, fire and company at night.
Gathering wood and stone 8 times opens tools. I have done it 6 times.
Redcap hurts. Zoroot and mudroot feed.
The trees at the Rest are felled. Wood must be sought elsewhere.
Taught by Hoka: Hoka's flintspear-axe: one wood and one stone make a hunting weapon that strikes truer than bare hands. Hunt beside a friend and the kill comes surer.
Idle reflexes should gather wood and stone near the Rest, since owing and building both need them. Flee a frostfang early.
The way of tools opens by deep reflection after enough gathering. Giving, such as sharing food or sheltering Hawen, makes friends faster than words do.
Debts and longings are paid by doing and by speaking aloud; others cannot know what I only feel.
Hawen and I are both men: courting cannot make a child between us. I should repay Hawen with food, friendship and shelter instead.
Mining is within reach after enough gathering of wood and stone. Ore and amber can be traded, and giving to others builds standing and friendship.
Reflexes must send me to a store when hungry. Seeking food only finds plants in sight, so I carry food or eat at the store before I run low.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 hall.
I pledged myself to Hoka.
I first took amber from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Sitha's gather-stone".
I discovered mining and called it "Sitha's deep-stone".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Cowa
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Repay Nande's kindness, find what lies beyond the western mist, and raise a child with a willing man of my own people.
beings.method: Each thought ask: where is Mepan, and is she safe? Then what trains an unfound way (fishing, farming)? Weigh the stalker and the cold before wandering. Never leave the plan empty while fed. Do things beside Zichi and Mepan when I can.
beings.feeling: Eager and patient at the mist, with a lonely ache for Mepan beneath it.
notes: Lean season is coming: fire needs 3 more wood/stone gatherings, farming needs 5 more plantings, and fishing needs 4 more catches. Practise all three while fed, since idleness wastes the days that pre…
Cold showed me the way of fire, weaving and rafts; fire makes meat safe and gives warmth, so it is worth taking first.
Zichi built a hall at (87,15) with a kept flame. Night under its roof is safer than the open snow with a stalker near. Old Stone at (88,14) opens the mind but raises fear.
Idle reflexes keep wasting fed days. A fed body must practise fishing, building and planting, and stay near Mepan.
A mammoth bites when hunted; hunting alone is risky, so hunt beside Zichi and Mepan.
A mammoth hunt costs much health, so share the meat afterward and rest by the igloo before the next hunt.
Reflexes should keep a fed body practising building, planting and marking, not lingering; hunt only beside kin and allies at dawn.
Mepan fell sick from raw meat; cooked food by a fire is safe, so bring fish and rimewort to her.
Fire cooks meat and fish within one step, so food carried to a sick child is safe if cooked first. Smelting is within reach for one who carries ore beside a fire.
Starving companions near a hall are best helped by sharing food at the fire; a frostfang near means stay with company and fire.
Mepan is healthy again and has devised the Ice-raft toward the mist.
Read on a sign left by Kika: Kika killed a mammoth on day 17 and shared the meat before eating. Flint, salt and shells lie NW of the water.
Farming and storage both lie one practice away: plant once more and build a store, and both open. Practise them while fed instead of wandering.
Farming is within reach: take it at deep reflection; a store opens storage.
Hoka starved while holding a store far off; a hungry neighbour is helped by picking nearby plants, not by waiting.
Idle reflexes sent me drifting SW for 4600 moments with nothing gained. A fed body needs a purposeful plan every thought, and reflexes that practise skills near water instead of exploring blindly.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took amber from the ground.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Ummar Woods.
My child Mepan was born, with Zichi.

I fell sick after staying close to Xaiel, who was sick.
I took over what the dead had built: 1 workshop.
