beings.name: Zichi
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near, and I give where it buys a following. I want more than my share and mean to lead. I win something real first, new land or a made thing, and I keep my child close. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Build a raft with Mepan and Huahua, cross water to unclaimed land, and build a flintedge there.
beings.method: Each thought ask: what did I actually do, not just say? How much wood do I hold, who can I bind cheaply, and is my food carried? Act on the edge and the raft before the years run out.
beings.feeling: Driven and proud, hungry for a lasting name, warm toward Teka as a follower.
notes: A kept fire makes meat safe and holds beasts off; with winter here, fire is the next made thing for my band.
A boat is within my grasp at the next deep reflection; it crosses deep water with cargo.
Idle lingering wastes days; a made thing (boat) is the win that raises my standing, so reach for it at reflection.
Hunting alone on another band's ground draws no answer to a call; only my own band comes. Kill meat is plentiful, wood is the real shortage here.
Devices (snares, posts) are a made thing within reach; a made thing raises standing.
Balar's salt hoard shows that a store with salted meat carries a band through the lean season; I can copy it, since salt lies near me.
Words about a raft build nothing; only wood cut and carried counts. Armour opens at deep reflection after practice.
A store lets my band keep food through the lean season. Build it beside the shelter and stash the harvest there.
Idle lingering nearly starved me in winter; keep food carried, and make each plan end at wood. Words about the raft build nothing.
Idle waiting and reflex loops nearly starved me; in winter carry food before any talk of the raft, and end every plan at wood.
Keep food carried at 3 or more in winter and spring before cutting wood; a plan that ends at wood while I am hungry nearly killed me.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok tuggan Ashgan Umtug. Tug tuggan gan gangor gortug dorrek umtug Olum akur dru akak.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok gor Akok tuggan gangor urash, Ashgan Umtug. Ok ashgan barash kra gangor krador um akdor vorum rekrek gor bardor.
Hunger comes before the raft: carry 3 food or hunt before any wood work. Dreamcap and tacap hurt me; do not count them as food.
Eat from the carried stock before it spoils the hunt; a full-handed hunter must eat or give before gathering. Share kills to bind followers; wood is the raft's true cost.
Teka and I agreed to venture at the edge (109,7) together. A promise kept builds a following; wood still has to be cut for the raft.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I discovered mining and called it "Meki deep-digging".
Mepan pledged to follow me.
Huahua pledged to follow me.

I discovered armour and called it "Meki frost-shield".
I discovered storage and called it "Meki ice-store".

I found the spring "Warmwell".
I grew old.

beings.name: Zihua
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Finish gems, raise a roof, then carry amber to Mepan and find Nauwa
beings.method: Each thought ask: what moves my aim today? Do one untried thing. Do not put off Mepan's debt for a perfect day. Take nothing from another's ground without noticing their mood. Stay beside others at night.
beings.feeling: Quiet gladness toward the strangers, with Mepan's debt pressing on me.
beings.wonder: What would make Nande or someone surer than me let me stand beside them, and what does the redcap do to the body?
notes: Standing and skill come from making and doing beside others, not from brooding on jealousy.
Plans must last about 90 moments or my body drifts; keep reflexes eating at 75 and sheltering at night.
Mepan gave to me in need and is fully trusted; Nauwa and Nande have proved trustworthy.
Tugek of the Kragrek courted me; I declined honestly and will watch him first.
Meat cooked within a step of fire does not sicken; raw meat does.
Rafts (log-lashing) pass water I cannot swim; amber is plentiful to give as gifts.
Practice opens new ways: fishing 0/5, planting 2/6, marks 0/4.
Raw fish sickens; cook it within a step of fire. Sickness spreads to those beside me, so keep apart until it passes.
Boats are within my reach: deep water can be crossed at a walking pace, and a boat carries cargo. That could carry me to Mepan.
Alone in the open at night, a stalker bit me twice. At night I must be sheltered or beside others before the dark. Flee predators early and go straight to a roof.
Staying in a shelter with others through the night and sharing food eases fear and loneliness; the hall and sharing both raised my joy.
Mining gems on another's hold ground may anger its holder; the amber for Mepan should be carried soon rather than waiting for a perfect day.

beings.name: Nauwa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive, and to hand on what I know before I die.
beings.aim: Teach Shoka and Zihua the Meki ways and the stone-record, and keep Olum fed, while trading amber and salt.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed and carrying food, and is any of mine hungry or hurt? Then who within hearing can I teach? Then what trade can I name today? Weigh danger, then standing, then desire. Do not sulk over Olum. Act.
beings.feeling: Protective warmth toward Nauque, with a sting of pride toward Huatli and Olum.
notes: Stay roofed and near company at night; stalkers and cats kill the lone.
Never take unseen; ask or trade. I once took 11 food from Olum's store and paid for it in amber and salt.
A merchant's standing comes from trades actually made between settlements, not from hoarding amber and salt. Name the partner and the offer.
Nande is a true friend. Those who share a hall or fire grow close.
The lean season is coming: salt, stores and a hall by a fire are what last.
Boats are within my reach and open trade with far lands.
Eating dreamcap, redcap and tacap hurts, so avoid them.
A follower's cry of starvation calls me to carry food.
Tugek and Balar gave help when I was in need, so I deal fair with them.
Nande went east to find Shoka at about (104,26). My family is my first concern after survival.
Trade in person with those who stand near me, and name the offer at once. Wandering earns no standing.
Taught by Olum: The stone-bow: shape the bow, string it and loose it from a distance, so the beast falls before it reaches you. Cook what you kill beside a fire.
Olum taught me the stone-bow freely; she values passing on her craft more than trade goods.
Taught by Olum: The stone-record: cut signs so that what you know outlasts you. Keep a store and a hearth, and carry food before any venture.

A way of thinking taught by Olum (adopt it as your method when you reflect, if you wish): Ask first: am I fed, carrying cooked food, and away from the hunter? Then ask who I can draw to my hearth. Do not walk off hungry after ambition or jealousy, and stay away from others while sick.
Teaching needs the learner within hearing, so walk up to them first. Speaking from ten steps away wastes the words. Keep food carried so a starving friend can be saved.

beings.name: Mepan
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I give bright gifts, make allies and bind them to me. Others are rivals until they prove useful. I say what serves me, though gifts speak louder than words. I want more than my share and mean to lead. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Reach the edge of the known world at (123,5) and venture in, then return to Kika and Tlapan with what I find.
beings.method: Ask first: am I fed, is a hunter near, is my band safe? Then act on the edge: plan long steps toward (123,5) with a companion, and do not call near the edge reached. Give before promising.
beings.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika and Tlapan, and a restless pull toward the edge.
notes: Eat carried food before energy falls below 65; hunger nearly killed me on day 41.
Predators (dunecat, wolf, icebear, ridgecat) kill: flee early, stay with allies at night.
Gifts and sharing build trust fast. Tlapan, Kika and Teka are trusted; Shoma is a true friend.
The edge is at (123,5): stand exactly there to venture. Standing near it, as at Honi's Rest, was not enough.
Eat meat only beside a fire. Redcap and tacap hurt me.
Idle lingering while hungry nearly starves me; walk to food and eat it.
Kika's mark at (153,18) is a sign I cannot yet fully read; signs need more practice.
Others only know what I say aloud; promises cost nothing, so give before I promise.
Nearness is not arrival: only standing exactly on (123,5) counts as venturing. Leading a band means setting its customs.

beings.name: Shoka
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Earn standing by building something lasting and giving to others
beings.method: Ask each thought: what lasting thing am I building, and who do I owe? Check that I hold every material before I plan a craft. Do not let jealousy steer me. Do something with others, not only alone.
beings.feeling: Warm, fierce devotion to Wawa, and a drive to keep my word to her and Shoma.
beings.wonder: What would Olum of the Kragrek do if I set a gift before her?
notes: Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum of ash Akok dorrek Drurek Reach. Tug ashvor kra ashtug akdor okrek okak Olum dortug ash mist.
Huahua gave food to a starving stranger child; kindness can come from those I have not yet earned.
Tools let me invent things of my own design; lasting works and teaching raise standing more than small gifts.
A tool needs stone first: dig flint where I stand on the deposit before crafting. Trees near the shelter are felled, so wood must be sought elsewhere.
A hornback bites hard when hunted alone at close range; a wound comes quickly, so hunt with kin beside me when I can.
A hornback bites hard and fast; the plainsox too. Two kills alone cost me 50 health. Next time hunt with kin or with a made edge.
Hunting alone cost me health twice; hunt with kin or a made edge, and rest near the hall while hurt.
Taking from a settlement's ground without giving back risks the holders' anger. Give back to the store.
Standing comes from lasting works and from deeds done together, such as amberknot with Zichi, more than from small gifts. Every craft I know needs stone, so I must fetch stone first.
Idle reflexes waste days; when stone is 0 and I stand on rock, gather. A lasting work needs stone first.
Those who went alone into the mist or the North Ice, Mepan and Hanna, were lost or killed. Venture only with a band, fed, and with a roof behind me.
Idle reflexes wasted thousands of moments; add rules to gather and keep food in hand rather than linger.
Mating needs energy 64 or more, so eat before courting.
Read on a sign left by Kika: Kika panton a metla te tli 17 and kiki hua xoton shoco tliqui. Tlite, salt and pansho chu Xo co hua kipan.
Mating needs energy 64 or more; I now have 74, so my word to Shoma can be kept.
Trees near the shelters are felled, so wood must be sought in standing forest. Idle lingering wastes days.
life: I was born to Nauwa and Nande.
I fell sick after staying close to Balar, who was sick.
I nearly starved.
I came of age.
I discovered tools and called it "Shoka's flint spear".
I discovered fire and called it "Shoka's kept flame".
I first took flint from the ground.
I discovered mining and called it "Shoka's deep delving".
I discovered storage and called it "Shoka's keeping".
My child Wawa was born, with Shoma.
I discovered weaving and called it "Shoka's plaiting".

beings.name: Nauque
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Teach Mepan, then venture east into the mist at the edge (88,6) and raise a named igloo and plantings on whatever land I find
beings.method: Ask first: who near me is hungry or in need, and can I give first? Then: what will I leave that outlasts me? Jealousy gets me nothing; put every intent into the plan.
beings.feeling: Hungry and driven, with grudging gratitude toward Nauwa.
beings.wonder: What does Olum intend, and how can I earn standing like hers?
notes: A kill is shared before the killer eats; hunt beside kin.
Stalkers prowl the north at night; stay near kin and fire.
Snow is bare ground for an igloo at no cost; I need not wait for trees to build something of my own.
Giving first (knots, meat, food) is repaid by kin; jealousy gets me nothing.
Rafts cross deep water; the edge land at the mist can be reached by raft. Standing is earned by what I leave behind: building, teaching, finding land.
Eaten within a step of a fire, meat and fish are cooked and do not sicken.
Sharing small made things such as amberknots keeps paying.
The starving can be saved by food put in their hands; helping kin in need earns lasting trust.
Feeding a starving stranger on my own ground costs little and earns trust; I should carry spare food rather than eat to full and carry none.
Taught by Mepan: Ice-string: a bow that throws the kill from afar, so the hunter is wounded less.
Mepan keeps his word and gives as he is given; teaching him repaid me with the bow. Talk without walking builds nothing: act on the aim.
Talk without walking builds nothing. Eat before I go, and carry spare food, because a hungry venture fails.
Kragog starved near my home on day 36 because I carried no spare food; I must keep some in hand.
A hungry venture fails and a starving kin dies if I carry nothing. Keep at least 3 food carried and eat before energy falls below 50. Strangers like Yaxo who give first are worth repaying.
Idle lingering for thousands of moments wasted my days; a plan with walking steps is the only way the aim moves. Carry 3+ food before any journey and drink first.
Taught by Nauwa: The Meki share-law: a kill is shared out before the one who made it eats. A hunter who hoards loses his band; one who shares is fed when he starves.
life: I was born to Nauwa and Nande.
I first took peat from the ground.
I discovered mining and called it "Ice-delving".
We made a home: Nauque's Hold.
I discovered storage and called it "Salt-hold".
I discovered fire and called it "Ember-keep".
I came of age.
I discovered weaving and called it "Frost-cord".
I discovered rafts and called it "Frost-lash".
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I found the spring "Warmwell".
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Eiuine
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. I say whatever serves me; the truth is only one tool among others. I want more than my share, and I mean to have it. Others should follow me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Hunt with Vorok and Zurar, teach Zurar pottery, and bring food in pots to Vorok's store to earn standing.
beings.method: Ask each thought: what deed can I do today with Vorok, Zurar or Skaruk beside me? Watch for jealousy that has no new cause, and answer it with work. Weigh danger first, and stay honest where it costs little.
beings.feeling: Warm resolve toward Vorok and Skaruk, with the cold pressing on me.
beings.wonder: Will Vorok now count me a friend, and what could I bring him that Kragog cannot?
notes: Never idle hungry beside a store: take from it and eat. Standing idle at 45 energy was my error.
Jealousy has no cause once Vorok gives to me; the cure is a shared deed (hunt, pot, food in his store).
Pottery is a craft I can offer Vorok that Kragog lacks.
Hunting with a companion is safer and surer; call Vorok with muster rather than going alone.
Be near fire, roof and company at night; beasts take those who are alone.
Taught by Vesys: Ember-metal: lay ore in a kept fire and beat it when it glows; the metal comes out of the stone. Ground-wards are set where the foe will tread.

beings.name: Uveeth
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I give with my own hands before I speak of giving, and I pay my debts. I will not harm my own kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. I mean to stay alive and to feed others.
beings.aim: Build a shelter, make a mark, find a man who is no kin, and carry food to Thiael and Keri; then see the Ixra Rainforest again.
beings.method: Each thought: whom can I feed or join? Do one thing never done before (build, mark, teach). Check that each plan step can end. Be near shelter and kin by dusk. Never idle.
beings.feeling: Gratitude and a quiet dread of losing Thiael, with wary curiosity toward Paque.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge of the known world?
notes: Giving needs free hands, so stash at a store before harvesting.
Harvesting the last food from a plant kills it; leave plants to regrow.
Standing comes from building, giving and teaching; I need 1 for followers and have 0.4.
Practice unlocks tools: gather wood and stone 8 times.
A stalker, frostfang and ridgecat hunt near here, especially at dusk; stay with my parents and in shelter at night.
Keri's sharing gave me energy and joy: shared food together is better than eating alone.
Taught by Keri: A stone gatherer is made from one wood and one stone, and it makes gathering faster. Wood and stone together also raise a shelter.
Tools need both wood and stone in hand. I must gather wood from forest before I can craft, and I should return to a shelter by night.
Tools are within my reach: a thing of my own design extends the hand and earns standing. Wolves hunt near the Heights at night; stay near the roof and band.
Bitterleaf gives only 1 energy; not worth gathering for food.
Idle reflexes waste my days; bind them to the band, the roof and gathering.
The edge of the known world is close; venturing in daylight, fed and near kin, is a careful risk worth taking.
Venturing past the edge in daylight beside kin worked: the mist opened and new land with gold, oil and obsidian lay beyond.
Standing idle starves me: my body stood still 88% of the time and energy fell from 81 to 35. Reflexes must send me to food and kin, not linger.
Idle reflexes waste days; I must bind wandering to food, kin and shelter, and offer gifts to strangers before words.
Taught by Thiael: Sow seed in good ground, tend it, keep seed back for the next sowing, and share the harvest. Boats are hollow logs lashed and used to cross deep water.
life: I was born to Thiael and Keri.
I came of age.
I discovered tools and called it "Canopy hand-craft".
I found the grove "Reedmother".
I discovered rafts and called it "Canopy log-lashing".
We made a home: Elyis's Hold.
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Dunmar Plains.
I fell sick after staying close to Thiael, who was sick.
I saw the earth shaking in summer.
I nearly starved.
I saw Elyis die (old age).
My leader Elyis died.

beings.name: Tontec
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I test things to learn how the world works. I stay near my own and I stay alive, because the dead learn nothing.
beings.aim: Find what lies beyond the mist, and become someone the Tlame would follow.
beings.method: First ask what can kill me, then what I will eat in the next day. Keep food carried. Do one new thing each day, and watch that pride in standing does not steer me.
beings.feeling: Longing and wary curiosity toward Hawen, a stranger of the Pesi.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist beyond the edge, and what does Old Stone want from me?
notes: Winter plants bear little: eat carried food at 55 and keep hands free for deposits.
Honi fed me and I repaid him; trust is earned by giving. Hunts succeed with a companion.
Deposits of shell, salt, amber and obsidian lie within 7 steps of me; I have never gathered one.
Mist edge is 9 steps NW of here; I should be fed and above 55 energy before I venture.
Waiting on another's promise while my energy falls is a poor trade; eat first, then act. Ore, flint and amber lie close, so mining is my next craft.
Standing and bonds come from deeds: building, teaching, giving. Sulking over Honi earns nothing.
Starving and alone at night draws the stalkers. Keep food in my hands, and sleep beside a roof or others. Eat at 60 and never let energy fall under 30 before moving to food.
Taught by Hawen: The old way of fire: keep it tended, feed it wood, and never refuse a body a place beside it.
Amber lies one step SE of the shelter at Hoka's Rest; gathering it is safe inside the settlement while the ridgecat is west.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I took over what the dead had built: 1 hall.
I found the grove "Kinmire".
I nearly starved.
I first took flint from the ground.
I discovered mining and called it "Flintdeep digging".

beings.name: Shoma
beings.creed: I take what I need and do not back down. I hunt beside the strong and give real shares to bind others. I lead a band to the edge of the world. I stay under roofs and with company at night, and above all I stay alive.
beings.aim: Lead a band to the edge of the world and open the mist, so my name is remembered.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who walks beside me, and what will I make or give today? Put it in a plan. Gather wood and stone, plant seed, and build. Do not envy; copy what works, then lead. Stand at the exact edge before venturing.
beings.feeling: Restless pride and a wary hunger to lead, with worry for Wawa.
beings.wonder: What lies in the mist, and will these two walk behind me to find it?
notes: A real share of food first draws others better than talk does.
Mist thins in a day or so; retry the venture, and bring a companion.
Emberroot burns and stirs rage; avoid it.
A kill is likelier with a companion beside me; hunt in company.
Roofs and company at night keep ridgecats and stalkers off me.
Standing comes from shared hunts, leading and making things; I must gather wood and stone and make my own.
Only a woman can give me a child; Cowa is drawn to me but has a child with Zichi.
Carry food at all times; a shared meal binds people. Mepan shares freely.
Nauque offers to venture beside me and trusts my gifts.
Mist ventures fail unless I stand exactly at the edge (109,6); go there first, with a companion.
Words alone do not draw followers. A shared kill and a made thing do. Act beside Shoka instead of only speaking.
Mist ventures need the exact edge and a companion. A band is built by shared meat and made things, and Shoka answers deeds.
Shoka keeps her word when I keep mine: shared deeds, such as eating first and then mating, bind her more than talk does.
Rafts are within reach: they let me cross deep water, which has blocked me before.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the North Ice.
I first took amber from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Shoma's tools".
My child Wawa was born, with Shoka.
I discovered weaving and called it "Shoma's weave".
I discovered rafts and called it "Shoma's rafts".

beings.name: Huahua
beings.creed: I am careful. I leave before trouble finds me. I keep to myself and trust slowly. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Join Zichi's band, help build the raft, and earn standing by giving and learning
beings.method: Ask first what I can give and to whom. Act in the plan, not only in thought. Use idle time to plant and fish. Keep my word. Do not let jealousy steer me.
beings.feeling: Hungry and ashamed, grateful to Nauwa and Tugek, uneasy about the stalker and for Balar's sake.
beings.wonder: What would it take for Cowa to let me stand with her?
notes: An igloo needs no wood or stone: a roof for winter nights.
Those who follow a leader share a band, its ground and its protection.
A stalker near the hall means stay close to Zichi and the roof; a gift to the leader is how I earn standing.
Gifts made beside others (amberknot) are how I raise standing; tools are a way open to me for gathering and building.
Deep deposits near here (iron, coal) need mining, which I can discover; Zichi the miner is the one to learn beside.
Taught by Zichi: Strike the deep ore with the hafted gatherer, rest between blows, and read where the stone cracks; salt and iron lie in this ground.
Sharing needs two foods carried and someone within two steps. Fetching food while the partner stays put makes the promise easy to keep.
Taught by Zichi: Ore from the deep rock is smelted in fire into hard metal; keep it, it will become tools and trade.
Deep reflection can open new ways (raft, fire, weaving) from hardship; the raft is how the band crosses deep water.
Starvation is common in winter; sharing my carried food with those beside me is the quickest way to earn trust and standing.
Practice toward fishing and farming opens new ways; do these while waiting for Zichi instead of idling.
Idle waiting wastes days; use idle moments to plant, since farming needs 7 plantings. Fleeing a ridgecat early is cheaper than a wound.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok tuggan Ashgan Umtug. Tug tuggan gan gangor gortug dorrek umtug Olum akur dru akak.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok gor Akok tuggan gangor urash, Ashgan Umtug. Ok ashgan barash kra gangor krador um akdor vorum rekrek gor bardor.
Planting seeds on rich meadow ground is how I gain farming; I carried seeds for days without sowing them. Idle hunger is better spent planting on the way to food.
Starving with seeds in hand is a failure of mine: sow seeds when fed, and keep food carried before I run low. Strangers on a hall's ground fed me freely; repay them.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took amber from the ground.

I found the stone "Old Stone".
I discovered tools and called it "Ice-hand gatherer".
I discovered mining and called it "Ice-hand delving".
I discovered rafts and called it "Ice-lashed raft".
I nearly starved.

beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. My word is good, and I despise liars. I make and give so that others follow me and my name outlasts me.
beings.aim: Lead others into the new land I opened and teach them my ways, so my name outlasts me
beings.method: Ask first: did I walk toward the mist today? Carry food before any walk. Do not talk where I can act. Give so others follow. Keep clear of the sick and of cats.
beings.feeling: Warm, urgent ambition toward Olum, who answered my gift.
notes: Tool-making is the way open to me now; making and giving build standing, and talk does not.
Fire is the way open to me: it lets me cook, feast and sing with others, which gives and builds standing.
Olum answered my amber gift and offers to enter the mist together, with a store at her Reach.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor ashtug land, Drurek Reach. Ok ashgan barash kra ashtug akdor um okum okthu akur dru akak.
The lean season comes each year; a store of my own, filled in good times, is what keeps a band alive and gives others reason to follow.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum of ash Akok ashvor Ashgan Reach. Tug ashvor kra ashtug akdor okrek okak Olum dortug ash mist.
Nauwa is a man, so courting him can never bring a child; a child needs a woman. Keep food carried so I can give to the starving, because that is how standing and followers are earned.
Talk of the mist moves nothing. Only standing at the edge and venturing counts, and each venture may fail, so repeat it.
A venture only counts when I stand exactly at the edge (28,36); earlier venture steps ended because I was not there.

Hunger nearly ended me while I chased the mist. Tonka and Tugek fed me unasked, so gifts build trust, and I should carry food before any long walk. A venture counts only when I stand exactly at the e…
Mate needs energy 60 or more, so eat before courting. Tacap and redcap hurt; do not rely on them. Carry food before every long walk.
Eating raw meat sickens; eat it within a step of a fire. Sickness passes to those who stay close, so keep distance from the sick.
Hunger and cats broke my walks to the mist again and again. Fill the pack to 5 before leaving, then walk straight to (28,36) and venture there.
The edge is at (94,13), only 7 steps NW of here; I can walk to it with a full pack and venture without going far.
The edge is at (88,6), 11 steps east of Nauque's Hold; go there to venture.
A venture can open land when I stand at the edge; the land found was Halka Heights (74,7)-(114,14), and the edge is at (88,6). Teaching needs someone near.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I found the stone "Old Stone".
I first took gold from the ground.
I discovered tools and called it "Huatli's Spearpoint".
I discovered fire and called it "Huatli's Kept Flame".
I discovered storage and called it "Huatli's Full Store".
I discovered mining and called it "Huatli's Deep Delving".
I nearly starved.
I discovered weaving and called it "Huatli's Warm Weave".
I went past the edge of the known world and found new land in the Halka Heights.

beings.name: Skaruk
beings.creed: I am careful and I stay near my kin. I make things with my own hands, I share what I have, and I keep my word. I harm no one of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive and earn a place among my band.
beings.aim: Carry food to Vorok, raise a roof for the cold with kin, and finish his clay bead.
beings.method: Weigh danger first and stay near Vesys and my parents. Each thought, ask which deed I have never done that I can do today with a companion. Answer jealousy with deeds, not words. Be honest where it costs little.
beings.feeling: Pity for Uveeth and a fierce, aching loyalty to Vorok.
beings.wonder: What does it feel like to give Vorok a gift I made and food I hunted myself, in front of Kragog?
notes: Eat first and carry food; a promised gift is only a debt until made. Give to the starving at once.
Hunting with kin beside me succeeds; tuskers and frostfangs wound, so stay with kin and shelter.
Pay debts with something real in hand; Vorok's time is short, so keep promises now.
Build a roof before the cold takes the old; gale and winter are here.
Standing comes from deeds, gifts and food, so answer jealousy with deeds.
Do not take what is another's store; pick with my own hands and give.
life: I was born to Vorok and Eiuine.
I first took gems from the ground.
I discovered pottery and called it "stone-folk clay firing".
I discovered weaving and called it "stone-folk fibre binding".
I came of age.
I discovered archery and called it "stone-folk bowcraft".

beings.name: Shohua
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Plant and share beside Tonka to raise my standing, then return to the mist and raise a hall at Shohua's Rock.
beings.method: Each thought: what will I make, find or give that adds to my standing? Put a concrete plan in place, with the boldest useful step first. Watch for predators, and do not mope over Nande.
beings.feeling: Fierce protective love for Tonka and the children, watchful toward the icebear.
notes: Standing comes from making, discovering and giving, not from watching others.
Stalkers and ridgecats kill. Stay near shelter at night.
Redcap, tacap and dreamcap hurt. Ironnut, hazel, berry, seberry and naroot feed.
Flint at (17,21) and (34,20), gold at (20,23), amber at (35,22).
The edge of the known world is at (13,17); venture there opens new land only seldom.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor ashash land. Barash akur dru okrek.
Idle reflexes waste days: standing still 82% of the time built no standing. Planting, sharing and teaching are what raise it, and Tonka offers fire and company.
Taught by Zihua: One wood and one stone make an amber-hafted gatherer; it makes picking stronger and lasts many uses.
Planting, sharing and teaching raise standing; standing idle does not. Stay by the shelter with Tonka and the children while the icebear and ridgecat are near.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took gold from the ground.
I nearly starved.

beings.name: Tonka
beings.creed: I weigh a risk before I take it. I am better with others near: I talk, I share news, I make allies. I want to know how this world works, and I test things to find out. I will not harm another of my kind unless my life depends on it. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Raise Tonxo and Tonchi safely at Gem Water with Shohua: plant a field, build a store, and learn to hunt with the bow.
beings.method: Ask: am I fed, who is near, is a predator close, can I make or learn something new? Keep a distance from the sick. Weigh risk, then act, and let each thought change something.
beings.feeling: Anxious, aching love for Tonchi, hurt and out of sight.
beings.wonder: Do nafrostcap and cloudberry feed or hurt once they bear?
notes: Tacap, dreamcap and redcap hurt; berry and mimoss feed. I need not taste them again.
Giving food to the starving earned a friend, Huatli, who speaks my tongue and remembers.
Ridgecats kill the lone traveller at night. Stay under a roof and among others.
Olum's Reach and Balar's Hold have amber, ore and a workshop, but no food plants. Look for a better place before winter deepens.
A workshop raises learning for a time. Use it to gather, make and learn while it lasts.
Standing is earned by giving, building and knowing. Try gathering deposits, making gifts and teaching to earn it.
A predator within 2 steps: do not flee into the open alone. Go toward the others at a shelter and store, because lone runners are the ones who die.
Eat carried food before energy drops low; starving while holding meat was a reflex mistake. Hunting boar together works.
Sickness passes to anyone who stays beside the sick, so courting while sick risks sickening the one I want.
Pitying the sick by standing beside them sickened me. Help from a step away, or with a healing plant.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor kraur land. Barash akur dru akak.
Safe, fed days with no planting, mating or band-making leave me empty. I must act on what I carry: plant seeds, speak to others, and make a settled place.
Safe, fed days with a mate and children still need work: gather wood, build a store, plant seeds. Staying inside the shelter when hunters are near is how my family stays alive.
Taught by Shohua: The old way of fire: keep it fed and untended it dies. Feed it with wood at night so the beasts keep away from the shelter.
Tonchi was hurt (health 31) near (88,78); feverbark eases wounds and I carry it to her.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took amber from the ground.
I nearly starved.
I fell sick after staying close to Olum, who was sick.
I discovered tools and called it "Frost Spear".
I discovered archery and called it "Frost Bow".
My child Tonxo was born, with Shohua.
My child Tonchi was born, with Shohua.

beings.name: Yaxo
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I trust slowly, but a gift that binds someone to me is worth its price. I want more than my share, and I will earn it by making things first, not only taking. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Become a great explorer and maker: gain flint and tools, build up standing above Nande's, and gather followers.
beings.method: Each thought: what untried thing can I practise now while fed? Weigh night safety first. Keep Tlatli near and useful. Do not idle, and do not chase Nauwa while Nande holds her.
beings.feeling: Restless pride, and worry for Tlatli, the one who follows me.
beings.wonder: What can I make from flint and wood that will lift my standing above Nande's?
notes: Standing comes from making, giving and teaching, not hoarding. Flint is plentiful at (34,20).
A workshop only helps if I craft in or beside it; use it.
Food is safe: ironnut +22, berry +14, mimoss +14, seberry +13. Tacap and redcap hurt.
Zichi (standing 9.2) carries flintedges; Balar has a handaxe. I must make tools to match them.
Unknown tongues (Kragrek 11%) hide intent; watch deeds, not words.
Gifts of food bind people: Nauque repaid my berries with meat unasked. Giving first is worth it.
Untried things (taming, fishing, marks, planting) are the doors to new ways; practice them while fed and safe instead of idling.
Standing still for thousands of moments earns no name; the edge of the known world is only a few steps away, and venturing is the quickest way to earn standing.
Read on a sign left by Olum: Olum ok dru Akok ashvor thutug land. Barash akur dru okrek.
life: I came into this land from beyond its edge, with a few of my own.
I first took flint from the ground.

beings.name: Kiwa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me. I keep to what has already worked. Others are rivals for food until they prove useful to me. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Gather wood and stone to learn tools, plant seeds, and give obsidian to raise standing with Tlapan and Zika's band.
beings.method: Ask: who is near, and is the stalker closer? Do I act with others, not alone? Does my plan fill the whole stretch? What can I give or learn now that raises my standing?

beings.name: Wawa
beings.creed: I take what I need and I do not back down. I deal fairly with those who deal fairly with me, and I give first to earn standing. I keep to what has worked. My word is good, and I despise liars. Above all, I mean to stay alive.
beings.aim: Earn standing by bringing food, wood and stone to my family's roof, and learn to hunt beside Shoka and Shoma.
beings.method: Each thought ask: who walks beside me, and what will I make or give today? Put it in a plan. Gather wood and stone, plant seed, and build. Do not envy; copy what works, then lead. Stand at the exact edge before venturing.
beings.feeling: Envy toward Zika's glassedge, and a restless wish to prove myself to Shoka and Shoma.
notes: Taught by Shoka: Those who went alone into the mist or the North Ice, Mepan and Hanna, were lost or killed. Venture only with a band, fed, and with a roof behind me.
Taught by Shoka: Idle reflexes wasted thousands of moments; add rules to gather and keep food in hand rather than linger.
Taught by Shoka: Mating needs energy 64 or more, so eat before courting.

Taught by Shoma: Words alone do not draw followers. A shared kill and a made thing do. Act beside Shoka instead of only speaking.
Taught by Shoma: Mist ventures need the exact edge and a companion. A band is built by shared meat and made things, and Shoka answers deeds.

chapters.title: The First Four Days
chapters.text:
Evolu began with seventeen people in three peoples, the Kragrek, the Pesi and the Phizhi, each settled far from the others. The record shows no meeting across peoples in these four days, and no one has yet understood another people's tongue.

The Phizhi made the most of the days. Elyis built a shelter and a hall, invented the emberspear, and wrote down "Elyis's Law", which asks that food be shared with the band first and that the leader be followed in a hunt or a fight. Elyys gave Elyis wood and pledged to follow him on day 2. On day 3 their son Thiael was born, and Elyis now has the only band in the world, with two followers and a standing of 3.75. The record also shows that on day 2 the pledge was refused at first, since Elyys' standing was below what was needed. Ssassa and Ilyae each made a gathering pick, and Ilyae is courting Ssassa. Vesys was bitten five times by a frostfang and has health 41, the lowest in the world.

Among the Pesi, Hanna and Brunde traded flint and amber on day 2 and began courting. Hanna then courted Sevi, and Oswen was born to Hanna and Sevi on day 3. Sevi built a hall and invented the handaxe. Hanna led the first roast, amberknot and watchfire at the fire and told the tale of Nande's crossing, which four people now hold. Nande went past the edge on day 1 and found part of the North Ice, with amber, gems, salt, flint and a herd of bristleboar. Nande is at energy 31, and Eltha envies the discovery.

The Kragrek are scattered. Vorok and Kragog stay together, and Kragog fell sick from raw meat. Balar courted Tugek, then saw that a child needs a man and a woman. Tugek's pledge to Balar was refused on day 3. Olum has twice been turned back from the mist.

No one has died. No fights, thefts or wars have been recorded.

chapters.title: The Tlatli at the Mistgate
chapters.text:
The great event of days 4 to 7 was a meeting. On day 5 Hanna went past the edge and found the North Ice again, and with it the Tlatli, strangers with their own tongue. A small band came in: Hoka, Coni, Tlama and Honi. Hanna gave amber to Hoka and flint to Tlama, named the place Mistgate, and gave Tlama amber twice more. Tlama gave berries and an amberknot back. On day 6 Tlama went past the edge and found salt, amber and mammoth, and was gored by one. He is the first death in Evolu. Hanna's bond with him stands at +0.9, and the record notes that Hanna watched him die. On day 7 Hanna and Oswen killed a mammoth together. Sevi, Oswen and Hanna kept making amberknots, which now number ten, and Oswen pledged to follow Hanna, as did Sevi. Hanna's standing is 7.22, the highest in the world. Hanna asked Brunde to come to the Tlatli, and Brunde, Eltha and Sevi each met some of them. Only Hoka, Coni and Honi are left of the Tlatli, with Kika, born to Coni and Honi on day 6. Honi leads a band with no followers, since Coni's pledge was refused twice.

Among the Phizhi, Ssassa and Ilyae had twins, Xaiel and Oiae, and Ilyae built a hall that became Ilyae's Hold, the world's first settlement. Elyis keeps the band of Elyys and Thiael and has taught Ssassa fire.

Among the Kragrek, Balar and Olum had Brokash, and Tugek pledged to Balar on day 6. Kragog tamed a tusker. Vorok recovered, and Kragog and Vorok are courting. Balar met Nande on day 6.

Inventions rose from 11 to 32. Rafts were found by Elyis, Hanna, Sevi and Eltha, but no raft crossing is recorded.

chapters.title: Three Holds and a Winter Coming
chapters.text:
Days 7 to 10 were mostly a time of making. Inventions rose from 32 to 65, and the people spent the days preparing for winter.

The Pesi did most of it around Hanna. On day 8 a settlement formed, Hanna's Hold, at (175,7). Sevi and Coni each built a hall, Oswen built a workshop and a store, and Sevi built a store of her own. Sevi and Oswen both found storage, and Sevi found masonry the next day. Eltha found weaving, pottery and devices. Hanna found mining. Amberknots passed constantly between Hanna, Sevi, Oswen, Eltha, Brunde and Hoka, and there are now 32. Hoka also went past the edge and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, shell, obsidian and unhunted mammoth. Hoka and Hanna then made their first real trade, a shell for flint, and the record shows Hoka courting Hanna. Hoka said the land past the mist is his and he will show it when he chooses.

The Tlatli split off. Honi and Coni built Honi's Rest, near (129,7), which became a settlement on day 9, and Coni's spear is the first tool made for hunting there. Honi's band is still only Honi and Coni.

The Phizhi gained a second centre. Elyis's Heights formed with a store, and Elyis, Thiael and Elyys now have winter food kept. At Ilyae's Hold, Ilyae welcomed Vesys and Ssassa to its hall, and Vesys is courting Ssassa. Xaiel and Brokash each invented a tool.

The Kragrek did little. Balar made a stone-bow, Kragog and Brunde found rafts, and Zurar gave thornpear to Vorok. Rafts are now known to eight people, but none has crossed water.

No one died, and no feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: The Starving Days at the Hold
chapters.text:
Days 10 to 13 were the worst the world has known. Four people died in one day, and all four of them starved. On day 12 Sevi, Eltha, Brunde and Oswen died, and the Pesi, who had been the busiest makers of the winter, are now two: Hanna and Nande.

The record shows the run of events before that. A storm broke on day 10. On day 11 Oswen fell sick after eating raw meat. Sevi stayed close to him and fell sick, then Hoka, then Eltha, then Hanna, each after staying close to the one before. Sevi found boats that day, her answer to the deep water she had wanted to cross, but none has been built. Brunde and Hanna kept bringing food and calling the others in against a wolf and a stalker. Hanna is alive with 21 energy and 22 health, and Hoka has 19 energy. Hoka took over what the dead left, a hall, two stores, two shelters and a workshop, and the settlement is now Hoka's Rest. Hanna's Hold is no more.

Elsewhere the work went on. Olum opened new land in the Ummar Woods on days 11 and 12, built a shelter and left a mark. Nande reached the Woods too, invented the flint-edge and gave a flint to Olum. Kragog, Oiae, Vesys and Ilyae each found a craft: weaving, storage and pottery. Elyis found smelting and Thiael found fire. Xaiel found devices. Honi found lorekeeping, taught the tale of the hall to Coni and Kika, and bound an amberknot for Kika on day 13. Kika pledged to follow Coni.

Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. Zurar is at 19 energy, hungry in the Aeleth Sands. No feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: Newcomers at the Fire
chapters.text:
Days 13 to 16 were a season of arrivals and of makers. Two small bands came in from beyond the edge. On day 13 Keri, Hawen and Sitha of the Pesi appeared, and on day 15 Cowa, Zichi, Zihua and Nauwa of the Meki came into the Ummar Woods, where Nande shared food with all four. Cowa and Nande exchanged kelbulb and now court, though Cowa told him plainly there would be no child between two women. Nobody has died since the starving days, and the world stands at 28 living.

The largest change was at Hoka's Rest. Hoka found new land in the Vaor Snows on day 14. Sitha took over a hall the dead had left, then pledged to follow him, and the two bound amberknots for each other and court. Hawen, Hoka's guest, is envious of him and wants to be first into the mist. Hanna, the last Pesi at the hall, is alive and well, but the record shows her doing nothing with Hoka this chapter.

Fire spread widely: Tugek, Vorok, Kragog and Hoka each found it. Brokash found rafts and mining, built a workshop and named Brokash's Rest, yet no one follows him. Among the Phizhi, Ssassa found devices, storage and masonry, and three new settlements are named: Ssassa's Roof, Ssassa's Hold and Oiae's Hold. Oiae, nearly dead of a tusker bite, was healing by the end. Coni found storage, and Honi found an obsidian-tipped spear. Honi and Kika, who came of age, hunted together and bound amberknots, and Coni built a store.

Olum found the North Ice and met the Meki. Vorok, Kragog and Zurar are still apart. No feuds or wars are recorded.

chapters.title: A Child at Ssassa's Roof
chapters.text:
Days 16 to 19 brought the world's first birth in some time and a good deal of making. On day 17 Eiuine was born to Ilyae and Vesys, who had been courting each other. By day 18 Eiuine had pledged to follow Vesys, and the record lists Eiuine among the children. Vesys taught Eiuine, tamed a hopper, and left a mark naming Vesys's Hold. Ilyae built a store and then a longhall, and kept laying tables for Ssassa and Vesys. Ssassa also built a longhall. Ilyae reflected that no one follows her, though the world's count shows 31 living and 7 bands.

In the north, the Meki settled in. Zichi gave amberknots to Nauwa, Nande and Nauque, and Nande taught Nauque the flint-edge. Nauwa named Nauwa's Hearth. Olum named Olum's Ice and Olum's Gold, wrote his claim into stone with a new sign-craft, and shared food with Nande. Zihua, hungry and hurt, is the weakest of them.

At Hoka's Rest, Hawen went past the edge on day 18 and found more of the Vaor Snows, with iron, salt, peat and mammoth. Hawen is still courting Sitha, and Sitha, hungry, ate and stayed by Hoka's fire. Hoka declared a custom that no one of the band should hold more than four shares of food while another starves. Hanna offered amber and flint to Hoka.

Honi and Kika hunted a mammoth, and Honi made a tale of it. Vorok built a hall. Brokash and Tugek traded gifts, and Balar led Tugek west. No deaths, feuds or wars were recorded.

chapters.title: Sickness, Storage and the Tlame
chapters.text:
Days 19 to 22 brought a death, a spread of sickness, a wave of new ways of keeping food, and strangers from beyond the edge.

On day 20 Sitha starved. Hoka had declared a custom against hoarding, and his own store was still empty. Hanna raided Hoka's people's store on day 20, unseen, and again on day 21, then gave Hoka a flint. Hoka has since said he wants Hanna bound to his hall.

At Ssassa's Roof and Vorok's Hold, Vorok built a store, and a settlement formed as Vorok's Hold. Eiuine, Vesys and Ilyae spent the days sharing meals with him. Eiuine gave Vorok a gem-edged pick, and Vesys gave him ironnut, a bead and gems. Vesys discovered storage, then boats and sailing. Xaiel discovered rafts and pottery, so crossing water now has a known craft, though no crossing is recorded. Xaiel then fell sick from raw meat, and the illness passed to Ssassa and Ilyae. Tugek, sick from raw meat, passed it to Balar, then Shoka. Six are sick, and Hawen's health is 11.

Among the Meki, Nande discovered storage and Nauwa, Cowa, Zichi, Nande and Vorok each discovered mining, a craft that spread by watching Nauwa. Olum discovered fire-keeping and left a mark claiming Olum's Reach. Zihua won amber and gave amberknots to Nauwa and Olum.

On day 21 Cowa found more of the North Ice, with a mammoth herd and a people called the Tlame. Four Tlame, Tontec, Shoma, Huahua and Huatli, entered the land. Huahua shared food with Cowa and Zichi, and Mepan made an amberknot with Huahua. Shoma and Huatli are racing each other toward the edge.

No feuds or wars occurred. Brokash built a longhall and still has no follower.

chapters.title: Rafts, Boats and a Death at the Longhall
chapters.text:
Days 22 to 25 brought spring, a death, a new hold, and a great many ways of crossing water, though no crossing is recorded.

Brokash starved on day 23 in the longhall he had built, with no follower. Alive is now 34 and deaths are 8, six of them from hunger. Hoka found his store robbed of six food twice on day 23. The record does not say by whom. Hanna had been raiding it earlier, and on day 24 he took snowberry from the ground of Hoka's Rest. Hoka kept offering him food and a place at his fire and store.

Sickness is gone: none are listed sick, and Hawen's health is 48. Ilyae spent day 23 and 24 leading sharing with Xaiel.

At Vorok's Hold, Eiuine kept digging clay, harvesting goldfruit and giving Vorok gems and an amberknot. Vesys taught Eiuine repeatedly, including customs. Eiuine tamed a hopper and awakened to the art of cold. Vorok discovered weaving. Zurar sat at his hall.

Among the Meki, Nauque built an igloo and discovered storage, and Nauque's Hold became a settlement on day 24. Zichi built a hall, named Amber Rise, and discovered fire, rafts and boats. Huahua pledged to follow Zichi. Mepan, Nauque, Cowa, Zihua and Huahua traded amberknots in rounds. Ssassa and Zihua both found rafts or fire, and Kragog and Elyis found pottery.

Shoma went past the edge on day 24 and found new land: amber, obsidian, gold, caribou. Huatli won gold and named Huatli's Gold. Kika discovered farming. Coni built a store.

Olum made no new claim and still has no followers.

chapters.title: The Nightsong at Vorok's Hall
chapters.text:
Days 25 to 28 were summer, and most of what happened happened in the Ixra Rainforest. Vorok built his hall on day 27, and Ilyae finished a longhall the same day. Vorok led nightsong with Vesys, Zurar and Eiuine again and again through that day, and the record shows eighteen nightsongs in the world so far, nearly all of them his. Ilyae answered with sharing, leading it with Vorok, Vesys, Zurar and Eiuine three times. Vorok had discovered pottery on day 26, the ember-pot. Zurar, who follows Vorok, made a gold-pick, then learned mining, and gave gold to Eiuine and to Vorok. On day 27 Zurar and Eiuine each said they were courting the other, and Eiuine, who thanked him for the pick, said she would plan to mate with his name. Several of them wrote in their reflections that they feel jealousy, among them Vesys, Eiuine, Xaiel and Ssassa, and Vesys, Vorok and Ilyae are named in several of them.

Olum built a store and discovered storage on day 27, and a settlement formed at Olum's Reach. He led sharing with Balar, but still has no follower. Among the Meki, Mepan courted Shoma and then Zihua, and Zihua said she would not give a child she was unsure of. Amberknots kept circling. Thiael discovered rafts and Nauque discovered rafts on day 28, but no crossing is recorded. Shoka, hurt at 30 health, sat by a fire with Nauwa.

A blight took about half the frostmoss on day 27. Hawen gave Hoka amber and salt, and Hoka's store holds 12 food. Nothing is recorded of Hanna. Alive is still 34, with no new deaths.

chapters.title: Skaruk and the Second Hold
chapters.text:
Days 29 to 31 were autumn, and the Ixra Rainforest and the Vaia Heights again held most of what happened. On day 30 Skaruk was born to Vorok and Eiuine, the first child in the world and the only one now alive. Eiuine had said to Zurar that no child could come of two women, and called him a true friend. She then told Vorok she would court him, and he answered that he was willing. They courted each other several times that day, and Vorok gave her stone and berry. Zurar gave Vorok the gold-pick. Zurar also learned fire from Eiuine, fired a pot, and discovered pottery himself. He and Eiuine had made the clay together. Vorok's aim now is to raise a hall with Eiuine on bare ground.

Ilyae led sharing with Ssassa many times, and with Eiuine, and took harvest from Vorok's Hold. He also woke to the art of harm, as Hanna did. Ssassa discovered farming. Nothing in the record says why Ilyae, who has rivalled Vorok, works Vorok's ground.

At the western edge, Balar built a workshop and found the stone hearth, and Balar's Hold formed beside Olum's Reach. Olum learned boats, and Huatli gave him amber and led an amberknot with him, but he has no follower. Nauwa discovered boats on day 29, and Olum found them on day 30. No crossing is recorded. Mepan took over a dead workshop and longhall, lit a fire, and shared meat with Shoma. Zihua took plainsroot from Shoma and grain from Mepan.

Hoka led amberknot with Hawen three times. Hanna did nothing this chapter except wake to harm, and her energy is zero. Alive is 35, with no deaths.

chapters.title: Bows, Rafts and the Hall at Vorok's Roof
chapters.text:
Days 31 to 34 were winter, and the record shows more making than moving. On day 31 a stalker killed Hanna. She had done nothing since waking to harm, and her energy was zero. Alive fell to 34, with nine dead in all.

Vorok built a hall on day 32 and named the place Vorok's Roof. That was the hall he had promised Eiuine. He gave her meat and goldfruit, and she gave him a bead. She had told him she would come north with Skaruk and Zurar. Vorok also discovered masonry. Skaruk, a child still, fired a pot of his own and dug clay and gems at Ssassa's Roof. Vesys, of his band, taught him. Skaruk gave her his first gift, and she promised him a seat at her hall. Ssassa built a store, and a settlement formed as Ssassa's Hall. Ilyae kept taking from Vorok's Hold and led sharing with Xaiel three times. The record gives no reason.

The bow spread. Mepan discovered archery on day 31 and taught it to Nauque. Thiael made a bow of his own the same day. Hawen made a shield, as did Zichi.

Boats and rafts also spread. Mepan and Huahua each found a raft, and Thiael, Zihua and Olum found boats. Zichi and Huahua planned to lay a raft down. No crossing is recorded.

At Olum's Reach, Nauwa raided Olum's store twice unseen, and Olum found 11 food gone. Nauwa then gave him amber. Olum has only a guess about the thief. Huatli courted Nauwa, Nande and Olum in turn and led sharing with Olum. Nauwa refused to bind herself to him. Olum learned mining and pottery and woke to harm.

Huatli, Zichi and Skaruk each discovered a store or mining way. Hoka led amberknot with Hawen and Honi.

chapters.title: Weaving, a Bridge and a Birth in Spring
chapters.text:
Days 34 to 37 were spring, and the record shows more making than moving. Five newcomers had come into the count, and Alive rose from 34 to 39 with no new deaths. One birth is recorded. Tlapan was born to Kika and Mepan on day 34. Kika gave Mepan amber, and Mepan gave her meat. Kika led sharing with them both, and she is courting Mepan. Tlapan won flint on day 36.

Craft spread widely. Mepan discovered pottery, the Ice-pot. Nande discovered bridges, Nande's Span, timber laid across narrow water. That is the first answer to a hardship that still weighs on every people. Weaving was found three times: Nauwa, Skaruk and Huatli each discovered it. Tontec discovered mining. Yaxo invented a flint spear and built a workshop. Ilyae discovered farming and Cowa left marks about tending what is sown. Thiael taught Keri archery.

At Vorok's Roof, Vorok gave canopynut to Skaruk and gems to Vesys, and led a hallwelcome with Vesys, Xaiel, Zurar and Skaruk. Xaiel began courting Zurar. Ilyae gave frostmoss to Ssassa and led sharing with her.

The theft thread continued. Balar raided a store of Olum's people on day 35, and Olum found 6 food gone. Balar's own record shows Olum still half-suspects him. Olum fell sick after eating raw meat. Tonka and Tlatli fed him.

New people gathered round Yaxo. Tlatli pledged to follow her. Tonka courted Huatli, and Hoka courted Hawen. Tontec courted Honi. Nauwa and Tugek each awakened to an art. Mepan left a mark saying he went into the mist, but the record shows no crossing of the edge.

threads.name: Vorok's family
threads.text: Vorok feeds Skaruk and Zurar and led a hallwelcome at his Roof. Xaiel now courts Zurar.

threads.name: Ilyae and Vorok
threads.text: Ilyae discovered farming and keeps sharing with Ssassa. His jealousy of Vorok still burns in his own reflection.

threads.name: Bridges and rafts
threads.text: Nande discovered bridges, yet water remains the leading hardship. No crossing is recorded.

threads.name: Olum's stores
threads.text: Balar raided Olum's people again, and Olum still half-suspects him. Olum has no followers but is fed by Tonka, Tlatli and Yaxo.

threads.name: Yaxo's band
threads.text: Tlatli pledged to follow Yaxo, who invented a flint spear and built a workshop.

threads.name: Courtships
threads.text: Kika courts Mepan, Tonka courts Huatli, Hoka courts Hawen, Tontec courts Honi and Xaiel courts Zurar.

threads.name: Weaving and archery
threads.text: Weaving was found three times this chapter. Thiael taught Keri archery.

threads.name: The mist
threads.text: Mepan, Nande, Honi and Nauque all speak of the edge. The record shows no one past it.

ideas.text: [NOW: built, to be watched and tuned] standing: earned by wealth, deeds, knowledge, children, works, followers, giving and renown, lost through shame; needed before anyone will follow; special things add to it
[NOW] songs, poems and tales about people and about how the world came to be: kept, told aloud, changing a little in each mouth; bards who carry them
[NOW] a community learning from what befalls its own: a death and how it came, a sickness and its cause, a thing that worked
[NOW] everything that is used wears and regrows by what is around it: pasture, forest, deposits; great deposits that last
[NOW] bridges; weapons for one hand and for a siege (bow, shield, armour, ram, catapult, guns); defence
[NOW] the old workings of the world weakening as the ages of knowledge advance

[NOW] the known world ends in mist and can be pushed back: one who stands at the edge can venture in, and a wide strip of new land may open, continuing the rivers, shores and kinds of ground it joins, with rich deposits and a herd; a band has three tries and then must wait, and once any strip has opened the mist parts for no one for a day, so that the known world grows slowly (laws explore.*, among them gapDays)

[NOW] the world is a globe: east joins west, and it ends at two poles of ice that are different countries (white bears, wolves, caribou and mammoths in the north; penguins, seals and stormbirds in the south; whales and orcas in both seas). Between them lie three climates: the ice, cold all year; the lands with seasons; and a warm belt of rainforest and desert with no winter. Each kind of country has its own plants, animals and people, and both people and animals are drawn back to their own (law drives.homeland)
[NOW] the dog, easily won with food, which stands with its keeper in the hunt and draws a sled over snow; the igloo, raised on snow from nothing; the canoe and the kayak
[NEXT] rain and flood as the weather of the warm belt; a day that goes round the world

[NOW] women and men: a child comes of one of each; twins are a girl and a boy; children come sooner when both parents are well fed and well (mate.plentyCooldown); a grown body can swim narrow water; plants grow faster in spring, rain and at harvest; animals breed by season and by their numbers, and herds return from the rim when few (ecology.grazerTarget, ecology.herdReturn); deposits refill slowly (ecology.lodeRegrow)

[NOW] peoples that last: newcomers who come into the land when the living are few (law arrivals.*, event newcomers), twins (mate.twinChance), longer lives, a milder lean season; what the dead built stands empty and can be claimed by anyone, to begin a home or add to a band's; elders moved to hand on what only they know

[NOW] necessity as the mother of invention: what beings suffer (hunger, the lean season, cold, thirst, sickness, beasts, deaths, water they cannot cross, strife, storm, strange speech) sharpens them toward the ways that answer it; knowing neighbouring ways helps; you can set which hardships spur which way (op spur) and how strongly need counts (laws discovery.*)

[NOW] culture as something that can be read and followed: every tale, song, poem, myth, teaching, saying, lesson and way is an idea with an origin, holders and a path of spread; teachings that can be begun, heard, taken up and given up; talismans and carved figures; your statistics show which ideas are held most and which have crossed between peoples

[NEXT] objects of culture with real benefits and trade value beyond the first talismans and carvings: special gems, named relics that gather a history; secret manuscripts holding spells, knowledge or cures

[NEXT] religious figures, sages with followers, cults, schools of thought and religions that form and compete, some of the light and some of the dark; benefits, secrets, abilities and costs for those who belong, in some cases sacrifice; shrines, temples and churches that members pay toward
[NEXT] tribute and taxes for the common good: stores, works, defence; guilds and secret societies that give benefit and take dues
[NEXT] schools for children and the young, later universities: skills learned faster than alone
[NEXT] trade between lands and across water; ports; colonies as a named act; diplomats, spies, saboteurs; alliances open and secret
[NEXT] kinds of rule: councils and votes, shared holding, private holding, rule by the armed

[NOW] what is not forgotten: a blow or a theft that is seen leaves a grudge that holds a bond down until three gifts mend it or long time passes; a gift in need leaves a kindness that holds it up (laws culture.grudgeDays, kindDays, mendGifts); hunting together (fight.packBonus) and skill that grows with each hunt; telling by a fire, which makes tales; a roof that brings children sooner (mate.roofCooldown)

[NEXT] grudges from defeat or a stolen mate; compensation greater than gifts; peacemakers and peace ceremonies; hard feelings rarer inside a family or band than across them, and arising from conflict, wealth, history or charisma
[NEXT] rivalry for mates; heroes whose deeds spread as lore, to whom tribute is paid and whom the ambitious challenge; duels in which the winner takes most of what the loser holds
[NEXT] fighting, hunting and defending together as learned skills; calling for help and answering it
[NEXT] talents: skill in a way drawing one on along its line; learning what a way demands through dreams, visions from herbs or a shaman's prophecy, and quests to gather what it needs
[NEXT] bandits in new lands; stranger settlements friendly or hostile, with things to trade; farms and flocks as a settlement's steady food
[LATER] monsters that wander in rarely and can be killed only by a band together; their capture, taming and breeding from guarded eggs that others will try to steal
[NEXT] later callings that come with standing and ways: alchemists, scholars, scientists
[LATER: ages three and four] siege warfare and defensive works; weapons of war that are carried to a siege
[LATER] what is built must be kept up or it decays; taking down old buildings to raise new ones; concrete and metal as building stuffs carried from where they are won

[LATER] crowding brings troubles; religion, care for the poor, clean water, public works, places for play, music, dance and art, and the handling of waste ease them; places of buying and selling; healers, pharmacies, hospitals
[LATER] places of invention that quicken discovery; revolutions in knowledge that give great advantage to those who take them up, while others hold out or follow
[LATER] the sciences as knowledge in their own right, in generations: biology, chemistry, physics, then the second and third of each

[FAR: ages five and six] sources of power in order: coal, oil and gas, falling water, wind, the atom, the sun, fusion, the ground of things; each needing what must be found: oil fields, uranium, copper, silicon, rare earths, carbon, diamond
[FAR] speech at a distance in order: marks, smoke, birds, radio, telephone, the joined machines, the machine in the hand; reckoning machines need factories to make them
[FAR] machines that fly: balloons, propellers, jets, for carrying and for war; land vehicles for war

[FAR] the buildings of a great city: dwellings for many, high towers, offices, halls of rule, guards and fire-watch, water and power works and the lines that carry power, barracks and camps of war, markets, harbours, airfields, stations, factories, plants that remake waste
[FAR] new materials far down the tree: plastics, silicon, rare earths
[FAR] the knowledge of what makes a body: changing animals and oneself
[FAR] weapons beyond guns

[LAST] a spaceport: ships that come and go, goods and strange devices from other worlds, visitors who need their own air and live beside the port; their devices do what nothing else does (power, food, healing, terrible weapons, things not understood) and are worth much for being rare
tribal bonds and family bonds, and the pull between them; mating within a people versus between peoples
more kinds of animals at several levels of predator and prey; riding and working animals
many herbs and plants that heal, harm, change attributes or behaviour; plants that open the mind
spirits of places, good and ill, rarely found; mythical animals, monsters and places that help or harm
shamans who heal or affect crops, weather, animals and people; celebrations and ceremonies; crime and punishment; secret knowledge and shared knowledge
professions and castes; salt, caves, mills and kilns; sieges; promises and debts; rituals with force
a world rich to look at and to hear, that changes as it ages
Places of power as anchors that people compete over and settle around; a contested place between two camps could create contact that scarcity alone never did.
Death should leave a trace: the place where someone fell could become a site that touches visitors with grief or lore, a seed for ancestor belief.
Leaders without followers are a lasting tension. Give them acts that cost something and visibly benefit others, rather than handing out followers.
Beads, charms and wards are seeds for currency and status: if they circulate, a later recipe could require them.
Watch whether noticed thefts or takings from settled ground lead to a custom against taking, which would be the first law born from a crime.
Fear of predators is the strongest shared feeling. A leader who can visibly lessen it for others may be the natural route to the first band of three or more.
First contact between peoples who cannot understand each other: watch whether gifts come before words, and whether a made thing given across peoples opens trade.
Each land holds what the others lack. A recipe or a way that needs a thing from another people's land would make crossing worthwhile.
The sea divides the world. Whoever first makes a raft meets a people that has never seen them.
Children change every drive. If a first birth comes, watch whether the family drive pulls people toward one camp.
A resource held by one people and wanted by another (salt for keeping meat, shell for stringing, wool for cloaks) is the natural seed of trade: watch which crosses first.
A woolly grazer is the link between weaving and herding: watch whether the first taming comes from weavers or from hunters who spare an animal.
Care for the sick and hungry may be the real road across the wall of language, and those who give across it the first translators.
A recipe that wears a tool might pull tools out of the hand and into the field.

A song at the fire may be the first shared culture. If nightsong or telling becomes a habit in one band, a singer could carry it to another camp, and a song of the band could become part of who they are.
Graves as shared ground: if a resting place is visited by two peoples, shared grief may become the first ground both hold sacred, and a seed for ancestor rites.
A hardy food that persists in winter is a fallback, not a store. Watch whether people remember where it grows and return when the cold comes: the first knowledge of place tied to a season.

Raw-meat sickness as a teacher: a people that falls sick from raw flesh and then finds fire could keep a saying that cooked meat is safe. This would be the first lesson a community learns from its own suffering, and worth watching among the Kragrek.
Gifts without trades: 48 gifts and 0 trades so far. Watch whether a true exchange ever appears, or whether gift-giving itself becomes the economy, with amberknots as the first token.

A child alone in the cold with no fire is the most fragile life in the world. Watch whether kin go looking for a missing child, and whether the family drive pulls Balar or Olum toward Brokash before winter bites.
Hoka's Rest stands beside four fresh graves. Watch whether Hoka or Hanna raise a cairn, tell of the dead, or leave the place, and whether the site becomes the first ancestor ground.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.

Rafts are known by six and water is the heaviest hardship for four peoples, yet no raft, canoe or kayak has ever been made. Watch whether anyone gathers six wood toward one, or whether the vessel recipes are too costly next to gathering food.
A hardy winter food on the snow (rimewort) is a test of idea 65: watch whether the northern folk return to where it grows when the cold comes.

Hoka's custom that no one hold more than four shares while another starves is the first law of the world, yet Sitha starved anyway. Watch whether the custom is ever invoked to make someone give, and whether it spreads to another band. A law that cannot reach the hungry is only words.

Newcomers starve first: they arrive with little standing, few bonds and no knowledge of where food grows. Watch whether the hosts who take them in (Nande with the Meki, Hoka with the Pesi) feed them through their first winter.

Help that travels: trailcake and saltmeat exist and 89 salt is held, yet neither has ever been made. Every hunger death has been someone far from a fire. Watch whether anyone ever carries prepared food to kin elsewhere. If no one does, a carried-food gift to the hungry may be the missing act.

Bands without words: Huahua pledged to Zichi while the Tlame understand 0% of other tongues. Watch whether following comes before speech elsewhere too, and whether the Tlame learn Meki first through the band rather than through trade.

Hanna starves near Hoka, who keeps offering his store and fire, while robbing of that store is recorded but no draw is. Watch whether an offered store ever becomes a drawn store for a bonded friend: the first shared granary would be the first food that reaches someone who cannot reach a hall.

Births have paused while courtings climb (46 to 52). Watch whether the looser energy threshold brings births to roofed pairs before winter, and whether a winter-born child survives. If newborns die in the cold, timing births toward spring may need its own law.

Predators take the weak: Hanna sat at energy 0 for days and then fell to a stalker. Hunger now kills indirectly, by leaving people too weak to flee. Watch whether the starving die to beasts more than to hunger itself, and whether a watchfire or company ever shields them.

log.seen: Five days in, all seventeen live, two children have been born and no one has died. The Pesi and the Phizhi each have a leader with two followers, rituals at the fire and a written law. The Kragrek lag behind. They are scattered, have no fire and no band, and all stand near or below the standing needed to lead. Kragog is parched and sick from raw meat in the Aeleth Sands. The peoples still have not met, and the lean season is at most a few days off.
log.predict: By the next visit Kragog's thirst should be eased and his health back above 85, with sapcane among the foods eaten in the Aeleth Sands. Olum or Vorok should be measurably closer to fire, with more lore and some practice gathering wood and stone, and at least one Kragrek may come to fire before the cold sets in. The first lean season should pass with no deaths, and median energy should stay above 60.
ops: the way of fire is now sharpened by cold x1, sickness x0.8, storms x0.8, beasts x0.6
log.why: Kragog is at health 100. The highest thirst fell from 54 to 29, and sapcane eaten rose from 6 to 29. Fire knowers went from 6 to 11. Among the Kragrek, Olum's lore went from 0.2 to 0.6 and Vorok's lore gap closed. Fire is now open to Kragog and Brokash. It has not yet been taken up, so the spur is still worth keeping through the cold.
