lessons: from earlier worlds: Changing the odds of an act people never choose changes nothing. A lever must reach what beings want or see.
from earlier worlds: Real need opens contact between peoples sooner than tokens made for giving: the first gift across peoples went to a sick neighbour, and understanding rose after it.

from earlier worlds: Deaths in plenty came from isolation and wandering, harried by beasts, not from scarcity. Compassion moves those who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.
from earlier worlds: Inventions come in a burst once the first appears and spread by example inside one tongue, not across tongues. Tools are made far more often than they are used.

from earlier worlds: This is the first visit: the world is in plenty and calm, so the first levers should be pulls toward gathering and discovery, not new dangers. Winter is near and will supply the danger.

from earlier worlds: People built bonds, a settlement and a shared store on their own through gifts and teaching, faster than any lever I pulled. A recipe that needs 3 beings together will not fire until bands grow, so ceremony levers should ask for small grou…

from earlier worlds: The first winter tested stores, not bodies. People answered scarcity by building stores and shelters and by drawing their kin closer, not by stealing, trading or fighting. Pressure alone will not create contact between camps; something mus…

from earlier worlds: Sites that touch passers-by with lore are used at once, but recipes that need a specific carried food (feast: 2 berry) go unused. Levers work best when they match what people already hold and do.

from earlier worlds: New prey can stabilise the ecology without changing behaviour. Elk held the grazer count, but people hunt only by chance. Behaviour changes when a lever ties into something people already want, such as gifts, marks or kin, not merely when …

from earlier worlds: Recipes that need only things people already carry and one companion ('sharing': food plus one other) are used within days, while recipes that need a tool in hand plus a specific item (fangcharm) go unused even among active hunters.

from earlier worlds: A recipe gated on being at a building goes unused even when the building exists and the act's ingredients are common (sharing done 10 times, hallwelcome 0). Before adding more place-bound acts, confirm that people actually gather at the place and that the building counts as the kind the recipe names.

from earlier worlds: Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

from earlier worlds: Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

from earlier worlds: Inventions came in a burst once the first one appeared (4 to 18 in three days, mostly within one people), and none crossed between peoples. Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

from earlier worlds: Words began to cross between peoples (0% to 3%) through meetings and a gift born of need for a sick neighbour, while the made token (amberknot) still sits unused. Real need opens contact sooner than objects made for giving.

from earlier worlds: Changing the odds of an act people never choose does not change behaviour. The fishing chance rose by half and fish eaten stayed flat, so levers must reach what beings want or see, not only what succeeds.

from earlier worlds: A strong family drive with a low energy floor turns births into deaths: a mating pair with no food spent its reserves on a child and all three starved within a day. Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether that act can be survived.

from earlier worlds: Raising compassion coincided with gifts rising and food crossing bands, but only to those standing close to givers. Compassion moves people who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.

from earlier worlds: By day 5 the standing needed to lead (1.2) was above almost every ambitious being except Bruwen. Halls built with no one able to pledge to their builders showed that the threshold, not the lack of buildings, was holding back a second band.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

from earlier worlds: Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

from earlier worlds: A hardy plant and summer plenty came too late for a death at the end of spring. Food in the world is not food in the mouth: what killed Arri was the distance between a call for help and the one who answered it.

from earlier worlds: Louder hearing and a louder sense of mortality brought more gifts, new crafts and a child, but did not stop a leader from starving while she founded her Ground. Drives that raise ambition and foresight do not by themselves turn into carried food. Standing-seeking acts compete with gathering, and the helper who hears a call still arrives with nothing to give.

from earlier worlds: Spurring a way by hardship brought knowers quickly (storage 0 to 2 within one winter), but knowing did not lead to doing: the store is still unbuilt. A spur opens the door to knowledge, not to practice.

from earlier worlds: One lonely person living among another people crossed the language wall in four days, which no token or site managed in twenty. Contact deepens through shared daily life at a hearth, not through single meetings.

from earlier worlds: A status lever lifts whoever already does the act. Raising the worth of giving raised the giver (Tanna) and widened the gap for leaders who cannot give, so to help a stuck leader I must reward something they already do, not something they lack the means to do.

from earlier worlds: Spurring storage by famine made the knowledge arrive exactly when there was nothing to store. A way meant for foresight must be sharpened by the signs that come before the hardship, such as the first cold, and not by the hardship itself.

from earlier worlds: Easing blight let food recover fast, and the next death came from a predator to the weakest elder rather than from hunger. Once scarcity lifts, danger falls on whoever is most frail, so with so few people every remaining life now carries the world's future.

from earlier worlds: A louder loneliness moved the one being whose aim already pointed toward others, and within four days it brought a meeting between peoples that had stayed apart for over forty days. A drive works when it amplifies a want a being already holds.

from earlier worlds: Easing predators and winter hunger together brought the first winter with no deaths, even though food standing fell by more than half. Nobody starved because the hungry were near someone who could feed them, so in the lean season, closeness counts for more than total food.

from earlier worlds: A band cannot form if the would-be follower stands higher than the would-be leader, even when the two are courting and bonded. The shape of who outranks whom decides which bands are possible, not only bonds or standing above a threshold.

from earlier worlds: When the centres of two peoples drew within a few steps of each other, a dozen first meetings came in four days and understanding of other tongues rose from nothing. Contact grows from overlapping ranges and many brief meetings, not from any single crafted thing or site.

from earlier worlds: Sowing works when it is placed where the needy actually stand. The first sapcane missed the thirsty, the second reached them, and thirst fell from 66 to 0. Where food goes matters as much as how much goes.

from earlier worlds: Lowering the mating threshold brought a birth, but to the pair whose courtship was already ripe, not to the pair expected. Like a drive, a looser law opens a door only for those already standing at it.

from earlier worlds: Hunger deaths amid plenty are failures of delivery, not of supply: each one who starved was too far from anyone for help to reach in time. Hearing farther, keeping people near each other, or a way to send food ahead saves more lives than more food.

from earlier worlds: A count that reads the same at every visit is more likely a fault in the instrument than a fact about the world. Ask the programmer before reasoning from it (the food counts once looked frozen for twelve days because the earlier numbers were not kept as a copy).

day 5: The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

day 9: A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

day 13: Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

day 17: A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

day 21: Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

day 25: A hardy food sown on the ground where people already forage, ahead of the lean season, carried the north through winter (rimewort eaten 44 times). A healing spring placed a few steps outside their paths was found by no one. In this world, help must stand where people already walk.

day 29: Three sowings of familiar foods made in a season of plenty were all eaten past their targets, so the food supply in this world is now sound. What still kills is reach, and what still stalls is not food but births: the population can be well fed and still not grow.

day 33: A looser mating law once again brought a birth to the pair already furthest along (Vorok and Eiuine), not to the pair I named. And the north's danger has changed shape: the weak there now die to predators rather than to hunger outright, so in the north I must judge low energy as a risk of being killed, not only of starving.

day 37: A store does not only feed the hungry: once food sits in one place, it draws thieves as well. The count 'drawn by the hungry' must be read alongside the theft events before I judge whether a store saved anyone.

requests.text: Please clarify the hardship called 'water' in hardshipsPressing. Does it mean thirst, or water that cannot be crossed? The Pesi show water at 0.7, yet their thirst seems low and Hanna already knows rafts. If it is uncrossable water, it would help to show thirst as its own figure per people, so I can tell whether to sow water-giving plants or to leave the pressure toward rafts in place.

Trades read 0 against 48 gifts, even with Hanna aiming to be a trader of fine goods. Please confirm whether a two-sided exchange is actually an action beings can take and is being counted. If it is not, a simple 'offer X for Y' act would let the first market emerge from the Pesi-Tlatli contact.

Please report what each store holds (food count) and how much was drawn from stores during the lean season. Three stores stood when four people starved at the Hold, and I cannot tell whether the stores were empty, unreachable, or simply not used by sick and starving beings.

Sowing with 'land' or without 'near' placed 0 plants last visit (the icekelp in the Essia Snows). If a sow event finds no suitable ground, please fall back to the nearest suitable tiles or report the reason, so that relief food is not silently lost.

Please count, for each lean season, how much food is drawn from stores and by whom, and how much stays in stores when someone starves. Three stores stood unused while four died at the Hold, and I cannot tell whether stores are failing in design or simply being forgotten.

Newcomers arrive with nothing in hand, and one of the three Pesi newcomers (Sitha) starved within eight days. Could arriving bands carry a few days of food of their own land (say 2 to 3 food each), so their first lean days do not depend wholly on strangers' tables?

When a sow event places fewer plants than asked (the icekelp sowing once placed 0), could the record say how many were placed and why (wrong ground, no room)? Then I can tell whether a sowing near a being reached them or failed on the terrain.

Brokash starved inside his own longhall, and Sitha starved near Hoka's store. Please check whether a starving being will eat from a store at their own or a host's settlement, and whether the stored amounts were above zero when they died. If stores cannot be drawn on in need, they are monuments, not insurance.

Trailcake, saltmeat and every vessel recipe (raft, canoe, kayak) have been made 0 times, though many know the ways behind them. Could the log record whether beings ever considered these recipes and why they turned them down (cost, not seen, or no aim)? That would tell me whether to make them cheaper or simply wait.

Vessels are never made. Rafts are known by 14 and boats by 4, water is the heaviest hardship for all six peoples, and kayak needs only 2 wood and 2 meat, yet raft, canoe, kayak and boat all show 'done 0'. Please check whether beings are actually offered these recipes when standing by water they cannot cross, and whether a held vessel lets them cross. If they are offered, the reason they never choose them may be worth surfacing in their reflections.

Instrument check: the story says Hoka's store was robbed of six food twice on day 23, but the store at (175,7) shows putInEver 12, drawnEver 0, foodNow 12. Either thefts from stores are not counted as draws, or the theft did not touch the store. Please check, because I cannot judge whether stores feed anyone without trusting these numbers.

Please record in the chapter text who draws food from each store, and when, and also each death with its place and cause. Hoka's store went from 12 to 0 and Hanna died at (191,1) of a stalker, yet the story says nothing of either. I cannot tell whether the stored food reached the starving or was simply eaten by its keeper, and that is the central question of whether stores save lives in this world.

The 'things that can be made' list shows 'done 0 held' for bow, shield, raft and boat, yet the chapters say Thiael made a bow, Hawen and Zichi made shields, and Mepan and Huahua found rafts. Either the counts do not record these makings, or the story is describing discoveries of the way as makings. Please check, because I cannot judge whether water crossing is close without a true count of vessels held.

My rich ground 'Reach Meadow' at (37,12) was reported refused, yet it appears in richGrounds with 0 plants bearing and 5 people within 12. Please confirm whether it was actually made. If it was, it seems to have been stripped bare at once by a crowded camp, and that would change how I place rich ground.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

lessons: People build bonds, settlements and shared stores on their own through gifts and teaching, faster than any lever. A ceremony that needs three together will not happen until bands grow, so ask for small groups.

A first winter tests stores, not bodies. People answer scarcity by building shelters and fires and drawing kin closer, not by stealing, trading or fighting. Pressure alone does not create contact between camps; something must make crossing to another camp worthwhile.
Places that touch passers-by with lore are found and used at once if they lie near where people live; far ones go unfound for weeks.
New prey can steady the ecology without changing behaviour. Behaviour changes when a lever ties into something people already want, such as gifts, marks or kin, not merely when a new resource exists.
A theft nobody sees has no consequence. Wrongs need to leave a trace before they can be answered.

Acts that need only what people already carry and one companion (sharing: food plus one other) are used within days. Acts that need a tool in hand plus a specific item, or that must be done at a particular building, go unused.
A building that matches a leader's stated aim gets raised quickly (four halls in four days). A roof alone gives others no reason to come: following stayed at 3 through seven halls.
Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes: raising family and belonging brought births and bands within days, raising curiosity and sight brought the first meetings between peoples.
Every drive that pushes toward an act needs a matching check on whether the act can be survived: a strong wish for children with a low energy floor turned births into deaths.
Changing the odds of an act people never choose changes nothing. A lever must reach what beings want or see.
Real need opens contact between peoples sooner than tokens made for giving: the first gift across peoples went to a sick neighbour, and understanding rose after it.
Deaths in plenty came from isolation and wandering, harried by beasts, not from scarcity. Compassion moves those who see need; it does not send them looking for need they cannot see.
Inventions come in a burst once the first appears and spread by example inside one tongue, not across tongues. Tools are made far more often than they are used.
This is the first visit: the world is in plenty and calm, so the first levers should be pulls toward gathering and discovery, not new dangers. Winter is near and will supply the danger.

Recipes that need only things people already carry and one companion ('sharing': food plus one other) are used within days, while recipes that need a tool in hand plus a specific item (fangcharm) go unused even among active hunters.

A recipe gated on being at a building goes unused even when the building exists and the act's ingredients are common (sharing done 10 times, hallwelcome 0). Raising the family and belonging drives to 1.5 coincided with three births and four bands within five days, where earlier worlds saw no child in twenty days of plenty. Drives move behaviour faster than buildings or recipes.

Raising curiosity (to 1.4) and sight (to 9) coincided with the first two cross-people meetings and wanderers entering two empty lands within four days. The places of power, 20 or more steps from anyone, were still not found, so wandering widens contact but does not yet reach fixed distant points.

Knowledge spreads by example inside a tongue, not across it. A held token (amberknot) gets made but is not given; making something is easier than finding someone to give it to.

Lowering the standing needed to lead brought a third band within four days. It formed between two people already courting and raising a child, not around either hall-builder, so pledges follow existing bonds, and halls alone do not draw followers.

Winter, not isolation, killed this time. A chief with three followers starved as surely as a loner, because sharing needs carried food and winter takes it all at once. Bands protect only when someone holds a store, so survival across seasons needs foresight acts or hardy fallbacks, not more bonds.

ops.name: firecircle
ops.hint: Feed a fire with others gathered close, and share its warmth and talk.

ops.name: hidewrap
ops.hint: The hides of two kills, scraped with a tool and wrapped about the body, keep the cold out for days.

ops.name: cairn
ops.hint: Stones piled together for one who is gone, with another standing beside you, ease grief and bind the living.

ops.name: feast
ops.hint: Share food beside a fire with another, and all who sit near are gladdened and warmed for a day.

ops.name: roast
ops.hint: Roast two portions of meat over a fire and share it with whoever stands near; all who eat are fed and warmed toward one another.

ops.name: sharing
ops.hint: Lay out two foods for whoever stands beside you, and all eat together.

ops.name: watchfire
ops.hint: Feed your fire high with two wood while others sit close, and everyone beside it feels warmer and braver against the dark.

ops.name: ironward
ops.hint: Beat smelted metal in a fire into a ward that can be worn or given; its bearer stands harder against teeth and claws.

ops.name: amberknot
ops.hint: Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep, or to give.

ops.name: bead
ops.hint: Shape a little clay and harden it in the fire into small bright beads that can be worn, kept or given.

ops.name: fangcharm
ops.hint: From a kill, string a fang into a charm you can keep or give away.

ops.name: longhall
ops.hint: A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.

ops.name: hallwelcome
ops.hint: Share food with a guest under a hall's roof; beneath it, fear and loneliness ease for all who sit together.

ops.name: nightsong
ops.hint: Sit by a fire after dark with someone near and sing or speak of what has been; the night feels less empty for all who hear.

ops.name: emberfish
ops.hint: Fish laid over the fire before eating keeps the belly sound and the body strong.

The chapter text can lag behind the numbers. Vesys was said to be at health 41, but the roster shows him at 100 and the lowest health in the world is now Brunde's 60. Judge who is in danger from the living roster, not from the story.

A spur shortens the road but does not walk it. The fire spur closed the Kragrek's lore gap within four days, but what still stands between them and fire is the act of gathering wood and stone, which only their own aims can supply.

Closeness saves lives in hunger but kills in contagion. Each carer who stayed beside the sick caught the raw-meat fever, and the sickness drain, storm cold and winter scarcity together starved four in one day. Before a lean season, sickness and cold must be judged together with food, not food alone.

A sowing made in a season of plenty is a cheap insurance. Kelbulb and thornpear sown before need peaked were eaten steadily, so food placed ahead of the lean season reaches people because they are already foraging, not starving.

Those who starve now are not the poor but the newly arrived: Sitha was a newcomer dependent on another's table, and Zihua, the weakest Meki, is one too. A custom or a store at the hall does not feed someone who cannot reach the hall, so help for newcomers must be placed where they stand.

A hardy food sown on the ground where people already forage, ahead of the lean season, carried the north through winter (rimewort eaten 44 times). A healing spring placed a few steps outside their paths was found by no one. In this world, help must stand where people already walk.

Three sowings of familiar foods made in a season of plenty were all eaten past their targets, so the food supply in this world is now sound. What still kills is reach, and what still stalls is not food but births: the population can be well fed and still not grow.

A looser mating law once again brought a birth to the pair already furthest along (Vorok and Eiuine), not to the pair I named. And the north's danger has changed shape: the weak there now die to predators rather than to hunger outright, so in the north I must judge low energy as a risk of being killed, not only of starving.

A store does not only feed the hungry: once food sits in one place, it draws thieves as well. The count 'drawn by the hungry' must be read alongside the theft events before I judge whether a store saved anyone.

Contagion turns care into danger: those who stayed close to the sick caught it. Watch whether a lesson to cook meat or to keep apart from the sick arises, or whether medicine-knowers (all Phizhi) ever reach another people's sick.
Stores and famine: three stores existed when four starved. Watch whether stored food is ever drawn on in a lean season, or whether stores are built and then forgotten.

Rafts are known by six and water is the heaviest hardship for four peoples, yet no raft, canoe or kayak has ever been made. Watch whether anyone gathers six wood toward one, or whether the vessel recipes are too costly next to gathering food.
A hardy winter food on the snow (rimewort) is a test of idea 65: watch whether the northern folk return to where it grows when the cold comes.

Hoka's custom that no one hold more than four shares while another starves is the first law of the world, yet Sitha starved anyway. Watch whether the custom is ever invoked to make someone give, and whether it spreads to another band. A law that cannot reach the hungry is only words.

Newcomers starve first: they arrive with little standing, few bonds and no knowledge of where food grows. Watch whether the hosts who take them in (Nande with the Meki, Hoka with the Pesi) feed them through their first winter.

Help that travels: trailcake and saltmeat exist and 89 salt is held, yet neither has ever been made. Every hunger death has been someone far from a fire. Watch whether anyone ever carries prepared food to kin elsewhere. If no one does, a carried-food gift to the hungry may be the missing act.

Bands without words: Huahua pledged to Zichi while the Tlame understand 0% of other tongues. Watch whether following comes before speech elsewhere too, and whether the Tlame learn Meki first through the band rather than through trade.

Hanna starves near Hoka, who keeps offering his store and fire, while robbing of that store is recorded but no draw is. Watch whether an offered store ever becomes a drawn store for a bonded friend: the first shared granary would be the first food that reaches someone who cannot reach a hall.

Births have paused while courtings climb (46 to 52). Watch whether the looser energy threshold brings births to roofed pairs before winter, and whether a winter-born child survives. If newborns die in the cold, timing births toward spring may need its own law.

Predators take the weak: Hanna sat at energy 0 for days and then fell to a stalker. Hunger now kills indirectly, by leaving people too weak to flee. Watch whether the starving die to beasts more than to hunger itself, and whether a watchfire or company ever shields them.

records.text: Hanna gave a flint to Hoka.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Nauque, I take your roof and your meal. Here is amber from my hands, a real gift. Eat with me, then walk north with me where the mist is open. Your name goes beside mine.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Nauque offered me a roof and a shared meal, and I stand here with seven amber and nobody behind me. A real gift binds better than talk, so I will give Nauque amber and eat beside him; he stands as high as Cowa and I want his name next to mine. The mist is open and I found it, which is the coin I trade on, and I will not walk alone with the ridgecat near.
records.feeling: Hungry for a name and envious of Nauque, but warmed by the offer of a roof.

say.text: Nauque, I take your roof and your meal. Here is amber from my hands, a real gift. Eat with me, then walk north with me where the mist is open. Your name goes beside mine.

records.text: Zihua rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I've spent these days gathering, resting and drifting after others' work, and my jealousy over Nauwa has mostly cost me time. Nauwa is the one I want, and I've been far from her. Nande is no enemy, so I'll learn from him rather than resent him. I fear the ridgecat close by, and I want standing and a fire of my own that I earn by making and sharing. I'll try the tasting I've put off, since I'm fed and curious, and stay near Nauque's roof and company while I do it.
records.feeling: Aching toward Nauwa, wary of the ridgecat, and curious.

records.text: Nauque led "sharing" with Shoma.
A wolf brought down a skit.
Shoma gave a amber to Nauque.
Shoma led "sharing" with Nauque.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a ridgecat sits two steps north, so my current plan to walk east and bind amber is the wrong move. Food is three steps west, and I will eat before I do anything else. Mepan is out of my sight with Cowa, who is faithful, and I will go to them once I am fed. I still want a raft or boat built, and a made thing is what will raise my name.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and protective dread for Mepan, with the ridgecat close.

records.text: Shoma led "amberknot" with Nauque.
Kragog rewrote its own reflexes.
Kragog rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I have spent my days running from hunters and walking past food, and I still carry nothing for Olum or Zurar. That is the same mistake that starved me before. The igloo gives me warmth and a roof, and snowberry is one step away. I will eat and gather there, keep clear of the ridgecat, and try the unknown nafrostcap and tacane once I am fed, since my question needs answering. I want to find Zurar, but first I must be fed and carrying food.
records.feeling: Hungry and afraid of the ridgecat, but steadier under a roof.

records.text: Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent these days trailing Thiael and Keri and eating what is near. It is warm, but a child who only trails earns no standing, and my aim is still mostly unlived. I have never hunted, gathered with a tool, or tasted snowmallow, and now there is snowmallow ten steps NW and a mammoth close by. Thiael and Keri are my safe place and I trust them. I will keep them near but start doing things with my own hands. I will gather wood and stone, which I need for tools and for the practice that unlocks them, and then bring food back to share. I fear the stalker NW, so I will keep my flee reflex and stay by my parents at dusk.
records.feeling: Joyful and restless to prove myself, toward Thiael and Keri.
changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Mepan, come to my hold. I will show you how to dig amber and ice-delve, and how to make amberknots. Stand near and watch my hands.
Nauque taught Mepan. Mepan has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Shoma ate my meal and gave me amber, and Cowa is close by, so I have enough to be generous. I have never taught anyone anything, and Mepan is a child near me. If I teach him what I know, something of mine will outlast me, and it earns the kind of standing Olum has. Jealousy over Zichi still stings, but I will answer it with work and giving, not by trailing after him.
records.feeling: Glad pride in my hold, with a sting of jealousy toward Zichi.

say.text: Mepan, come to my hold. I will show you how to dig amber and ice-delve, and how to make amberknots. Stand near and watch my hands.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Stand on a deposit of amber and gather, it holds old light. Bind amber on a cord with someone beside you and it makes a knot to give. Giving first earns trust.", deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I carry nothing, and the snowberry is one step away while the ridgecat prowls close. Cowa is beside me and I trust no one more, so I stay at Cowa's side, pick the berry quickly and eat. Once I am fed and Zichi comes, we go for stone so I can make my flintedge and hunt the mammoth with Cowa, sharing the meat first as my people do.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary of the ridgecat, but bound close to Cowa.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: An icebear is five steps east. Keep to the shelters and stay away from it. Zurar, walk with me south. I go for amber to bind a knot for Eiuine, and I come back to the hall.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: An icebear stands five steps east and it kills my kind, so I will not stay in the open with Eiuine and Vesys while it prowls. The amber for Eiuine's knot lies south, and a made thing put in her hand pays my debt better than my words did. I will take Zurar along, since a hunter is safer with one of his own beside him, and walk south, away from the bear, to gather the amber.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Eiuine, and wary dread of the icebear.

say.text: An icebear is five steps east. Keep to the shelters and stay away from it. Zurar, walk with me south. I go for amber to bind a knot for Eiuine, and I come back to the hall.

records.name: Hoka
records.text: Hanna, you are welcome in Hoka's Rest. You gave me flint and I hold it. I mean to mate with you and raise a child here by my fire. Plan the same toward me and we will do it.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: Hanna stands in my hall, gave me flint, and is the one man who kept his word, so I will not send him off. He is also the one I want a child from, and I have 70 energy, enough to pay the 25. Courting him now is the first made thing that would outlast me, and a child would be someone who follows me. Then I stock the empty stores while I am above 50, before Hawen's hands find them bare again.
records.feeling: Warm ambition and trust toward Hanna, wary of Hawen.

say.text: Hanna, you are welcome in Hoka's Rest. You gave me flint and I hold it. I mean to mate with you and raise a child here by my fire. Plan the same toward me and we will do it.

records.text: Hoka is courting Hanna.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Ridgecat two steps northeast! Stay together and keep away from it. Nande, I will repay your goldfruit.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: A ridgecat two steps off kills my kind, and I will not stand here and wait for it. Nande fed me today and I owe that back; Nande and Nauwa are close, and with Olum and Tugek beside them I am safer among many than alone. I will move away from the cat toward the south shelter I built and eat berries on the way, then come back to dig the flint and amber so I can make something that lasts.
records.feeling: Afraid of the ridgecat, and warm toward Nande who fed me.

say.text: Ridgecat two steps northeast! Stay together and keep away from it. Nande, I will repay your goldfruit.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Nauque, your roof is good and I do not forget it. I made an amberknot with my own hands, and the next one is yours. The amber at my mist is deeper than here, and the caribou there have never run from us. Come north with

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Nauque has flintedge and a name; I have amber and a mist that I found, and no one behind me. Mepan is a boy learning amberknots at Nauque's feet, and a boy who is given a real gift may walk behind me. I'll make another amberknot with Nauque close by, give it to him, then bring him and Mepan north with me to the amber and caribou I opened.
records.feeling: Hungry for a name, envious of Nauque, and warmed by his roof.

say.text: Nauque, your roof is good and I do not forget it. I made an amberknot with my own hands, and the next one is yours. The amber at my mist is deeper than here, and the caribou there have never run from us. Come north with me and bring Mepan, and we will both be named for it.

records.text: Nauque came of age.
Tontec took over what the dead had left: 1 hall.
Shoma led "amberknot" with Nauque.
Shoma gave a amberknot to Nauque.

records.name: Hanna
records.text: Hoka, I hold your fire and your word, and I will not take from your store again. I gather food now and bring a share to you. Of the child, I will not lie: I answer you honestly when my belly is full.

records.name: Hanna
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and food stands a step away, so I eat first and stop begging at Hoka's hand. Hoka keeps faith with me and wants a child by his fire, but my pull is toward Coni, and I will not lie to him; I will tell him plainly I stay by his fire and share food, and leave the child unanswered until I know my own mind. I will gather mimoss and nearby berries, eat, and carry some so I never stand hungry before him again.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and steady loyalty toward Hoka.

say.text: Hoka, I hold your fire and your word, and I will not take from your store again. I gather food now and bring a share to you. Of the child, I will not lie: I answer you honestly when my belly is full.

records.text: Hanna took from the ground of "Hoka's Rest" (harvesting mimoss).
Tontec found the grove "Kinmire".
Eiuine rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: I have spent my days trailing Vesys and chasing Vorok's notice, and the hopper was my first real deed. I am still small, and the icebear four steps east frightens me, so I will keep close to Vesys and the shelters. Vorok is walking south for amber to bind a knot for me, and that is a debt I want to answer with something of my own. I have never fished, and the water is two steps away, so I will fish and bring the catch to Vorok's store. That gives me something Kragog cannot match, and I do it by deeds, not words. I also want my reflexes to plant seeds and to stash food at the store.
records.feeling: Proud joy, a burning wish for Vorok's regard, and dread of the icebear.
changes: set its aim: "Fish at the water, hunt and plant beside Vesys, and stash food in Vorok's store to earn standing of my own."

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Vorok walks south for amber and asked me to come, and an icebear stands five steps east, so I should leave this strangers' ground and follow him away from it. My hands have still never closed on gold, but the gold at (97,87) lies west and north of Vorok's Hold, away from the bear, and I will go there now. I have circled it for days; today I stand on it and gather, and only then speak of it to Vorok.
records.feeling: Warm toward Vorok, wary of the icebear, and eager to close my hands on gold.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Stay clear of the ridgecat to the northeast. I gather berries to the southeast, then we find Nauque together. Shoka, come with me.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, so I eat first: berries are two steps SE and hazel four steps north, and a starving father feeds no one. Tugek carries five food and gave me kelbulb before, but I will not beg; I gather what the land offers, then bring food to Shoka and find Nauque. A ridgecat sits three steps NE, so I go south-east, away from it, and keep Shoka beside me.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and protective love for Shoka and Nauque, with wary dread of the ridgecat.

say.text: Stay clear of the ridgecat to the northeast. I gather berries to the southeast, then we find Nauque together. Shoka, come with me.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Mepan, come here by my hold. Stand beside me and watch my hands: I will bind an amberknot and show you each turn. Then you make one, and it is yours.
Nauque taught Mepan.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Shoma wants me to walk north with him into the mist, and he has given me amber and knots and stayed at my hold, so he deals fairly. But the edge is only 11 steps east, and the one who finds new land is remembered. Mepan is a child near me and I have promised to teach him, so I will pull him in to make an amberknot beside me, and that will outlast me. The jealousy over Zichi and Cowa still burns, but I will answer it by making something with my own hands, not by sulking.
records.feeling: Proud ambition and a sting of jealousy toward Zichi, with warm trust toward Shoma.

say.text: Mepan, come here by my hold. Stand beside me and watch my hands: I will bind an amberknot and show you each turn. Then you make one, and it is yours.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Bind a piece of amber on a cord while another stands beside you; it is a small bright thing to keep or to give, and giving it first earns trust.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.text: Mepan took from the ground of "Nauque's Hold" (hunting).

records.name: Hoka
records.text: Hanna, you and I are both men, so no child comes of us. That does not end my trust. Stay in Hoka's Rest, gather beside me, and we fill the stores together before the deep cold.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: Hanna stands in my hall, fed and glad, and he has told me plainly that he will not lie about the child. Two men cannot make one, and I have known that from the first, so my longing has nowhere to go. I would still keep him close, because he is the one man whose word has held. My hands are full and my stores are empty, so I stock them now while I am strong, and I will ask him to share a meal with me in the hall.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Hanna, and a restless ambition that is still unspent.

say.text: Hanna, you and I are both men, so no child comes of us. That does not end my trust. Stay in Hoka's Rest, gather beside me, and we fill the stores together before the deep cold.

records.text: Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.
Tontec rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: I have spent these days fleeing, gathering and testing foods, and it has taught me something, but I am still alone at a hall with no one inside it. Shoma and Huahua are the ones I trust, and Zichi pulls at me even though Zichi has a child with Cowa. I mean to bring them to Sitha's Hearth instead of chasing mist by myself. Kinmire and the dreamcap under my feet draw my curiosity, and the wolf to the west is what could kill me, so I will taste the dreamcap now while I stay near my roof.
records.feeling: Curious about Kinmire and the dreamcap, wary of the wolf, and longing for Shoma and Huahua.
changes: set habits: refuses redcap; leaves 0 on each plant

records.text: Nauque led "amberknot" with Shoma.
Eiuine took from the ground of "Ssassa's Roof" (fishing).
Mepan rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent my days circling hunger and fear, always asking Cowa to feed me, and I still have no flintedge and no kill of my own. A mammoth stands one step south and cloudberry is one step away, so I should eat first and then do something about it. Cowa and Zichi are my safety and I will keep near them, but I also want standing above Nande and Nauque, and that takes stone and a flintedge, not talk. My reflexes keep letting me run in circles. I will make them eat berries nearby and fetch stone when I am fed.
records.feeling: Hungry and eager, bound to Cowa, wanting to prove myself.

records.text: Ssassa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: I have spent my days building roofs, halls and wells, and losing Oiae taught me how thin a life is. I said I would follow Ilyae and my body still lingers by Vorok's hold. A promise that never becomes steps is what I despise in liars. I want Ilyae's fire and a place beside someone surer than me. The jealousy over Vesys is spoken now and quieter. I must walk to Ilyae and pledge, keeping to the shelters because the icebear is near. I will also change my reflexes so my body stops idling when the plan runs out.
records.feeling: Warm longing and resolve toward Ilyae, with a small sting of jealousy.

records.text: Zurar won gold from the ground.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My hands are full of berries, and I have meat from the yarrok and the mammoth, but the meat is what Keri and Uveeth lack. I owe Keri the most, and I give with my hands before I speak of giving. The wild cats hunt here, so I should not leave them alone long. I'll try the fangcharm to keep one new thing in my day, then bring the meat back to the cave.
records.feeling: Warm protective joy toward Keri and Uveeth, and a wish to bring them meat.

records.text: Shoma took from the ground of "Nauque's Hold" (winning amber from the ground).

records.name: Xaiel
records.text: Ssassa, I hear you. I will walk with you by the shelters, away from the icebear. I will eat a little on the way and keep making things for your hand.

records.name: Xaiel
records.thought: Ssassa asked me to walk with her by the shelters, away from the icebear, and her word is the one I trust most. The burn toward Vesys is still there, but I will not let it pick my deeds; I have an aim and a tool still to make for Ssassa's hand. I have 13 gems and no stone, so I will walk east beside her to the roof, and try one new deed there: taste tacap and sigrain on the way, since my curiosity is unanswered.
records.feeling: Trust and warm joy toward Ssassa, with a small stubborn itch of envy toward Vesys.

say.text: Ssassa, I hear you. I will walk with you by the shelters, away from the icebear. I will eat a little on the way and keep making things for your hand.

records.text: Cowa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: My days have gone to amber, knots and staying near Mepan and Zichi. That is good and warm, but I have been idle too much and I have never hunted, tamed, built or followed. Mepan is near and safe, and Zichi is coming. A mammoth stands three steps south, and the ridgecat prowls west. I am fed and curious, so I will begin to practise farming, fishing and building while I stay close to my child. I will change my reflexes so that a fed body does not just stand still, and I will aim to learn fishing.
records.feeling: Glad warmth toward Mepan, and a restless curiosity.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Mepan, boy, you make amberknots well. Come north with me and Nauque to the open mist, where the caribou have never run from us. I will give you amber and you will be first behind my name.
Shoma rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I've spent my days taking Nauque's roof and handing out amber, and I still have no one behind me. Nauque is the one I trust and envy, and the boy Mepan is the only one who might follow a real gift. I'm too hungry for a name to keep waiting under another man's roof. I should give gifts to the boy and Nauque, then lead them north to the open mist, and I should stop lingering when I could be making. I need to hunt with company to earn my name as a hunter.
records.feeling: Hungry for a name and envious of Nauque, but warmed by his company.

say.text: Mepan, boy, you make amberknots well. Come north with me and Nauque to the open mist, where the caribou have never run from us. I will give you amber and you will be first behind my name.

records.text: Keri rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: My days have been gathering, tasting and walking close to Thiael and Uveeth, and that is good, but my aim of shelter and tools has barely moved. I have never built anything, and I have given less to Thiael than they gave me. Uveeth is near and content, and I am glad. I fear the shadowcat and frostfang seven steps east, and I have been too easy about them. Now I will taste ironnut and sigrain, which are close. Then I will gather wood and stone, and build a shelter by the cave so my family has a roof.
records.feeling: Warm, protective joy toward Uveeth and Thiael, and a wary eye on the predators to the east.

records.text: Vesys rewrote its own reflexes.
Vesys discovered alchemy: "leaf-brew" — Mix healing barks and nuts with fire and clay into stronger cures and stranger draughts..

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: My days have been good: I've made things, taught Eiuine, and earned standing. But I've been wandering between fire and hall while the icebear prowls, and I haven't pursued my own question about alchemy. The way is within my grasp, so I'll take it now. It answers what feverbark and ironnut do when mixed, and I can share it with Eiuine and Vorok. I fear the icebear, and I've been slow to move us away from it, so my reflexes should flee it sooner.
records.feeling: Joyful and protective toward Eiuine, eager for alchemy, wary of the icebear.

records.text: Zurar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My hands have closed on gold at last. I hold six pieces, and I made them myself, so they are mine to give. I have spent my days circling gifts and the Halim Heights, and I did not close my hands on anything until today. Vorok is my trust and my aim, and I should carry the gold to his Hold now, before I speak of it. I fear the icebear and the stalker NW, so I will not linger here. The ache over Ilyae and Vesys I will leave alone; it gives me nothing to do.
records.feeling: Glad and proud, warm toward Vorok.

records.text: Nauque rewrote its own way of thinking.
Nauque discovered weaving: "Frost-cord" — Twist moss and wool into cords and cloaks that carry more and keep the cold off..

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I have mostly dug amber, tied knots and watched Zichi and Cowa. Jealousy has eaten my days and built nothing that will outlast me. Shoma has dealt fairly with me, and I trust him. The edge of the mist is ten steps east, and the one who ventures first is remembered. That is the standing I want, more than Cowa's eyes. I will teach Mepan beside me and then go to the edge. I will not let Zichi steer me.
records.feeling: Proud ambition, with a jealous sting toward Zichi and warm trust toward Shoma.
changes: set its aim: "Teach Mepan, then venture east into the mist at the edge (88,6) and raise a named igloo and plantings on whatever land I find"

records.text: Eiuine led "sharing" with Vorok, Vesys, Ssassa.

records.name: Nande
records.text: The ridgecat is west and it has just eaten, but it still hunts. Come southeast with me, stay together, and I will share food at my fire. No one here goes hungry.

records.name: Nande
records.thought: A ridgecat is four steps west and it kills my kind, so I will not stand here and be proud. Shoka is beside me, fed and safe for now, and Nauwa is weak with hunger; I would rather keep my child close and put a roof and a full hand between us and the beast than chase the mist today, since my venture will is spent anyway. I will get away from the cat toward the southeast where Nauwa went for berries, pick food to carry, and then raise something here that will outlast me, a hall by the flint and amber with the ore in reach.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and a fierce wish to keep Shoka and Nauwa alive.

say.text: The ridgecat is west and it has just eaten, but it still hunts. Come southeast with me, stay together, and I will share food at my fire. No one here goes hungry.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Friends, I raise a hall here with my wood and stone. Come sit under it when it stands, and I lay out food for you all.
Vorok rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: I have been circling the same errand for three thoughts, walking toward amber and never finishing it. My days have been meals and promises, and they are good, but my aim of a hall at Ssassa's Roof has not moved. I owe Eiuine a made thing, and I will pay it with a deed. First I must stop dithering, so I will build the hall here with the wood and stone I already carry. Vesys and Eiuine are close, and building beside them is also company. The icebear frightens me, so I will keep my flee reflex and keep to the shelters.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Eiuine, and a wary dread of the icebear.

say.text: Friends, I raise a hall here with my wood and stone. Come sit under it when it stands, and I lay out food for you all.

changes: set its aim: "Raise a hall at Ssassa's Roof with my own wood and stone, then lay food for Eiuine and Vesys beneath it."

records.text: Thiael gave berry to Keri.
Thiael led "sharing" with Keri.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok is walking south to bind an amberknot for me, and I have only gems and fish to answer him with, and Kragog is always at his side. My hands are full of fish, so the best thing I can do is carry them to Vorok's store and let him see that Eiuine fills it. The icebear is five steps east and I am small, so I keep Vesys and the shelters close and go west, away from it.
records.feeling: Burning wish for Vorok's regard, with dread of the icebear.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: My jealousy of Nande and Nauwa is old and I will not let it sit idle; Nauwa is far west and I ache for her, but my hands are still empty of standing. Nauque is near, trusts me, and once offered to bind a knot with me, and he is the one I think of when I long for a child. Tasting the tacane and thornpear to the south-east would answer my question and cost little, and I can do it by walking past Shoma and Zichi, who are there in company.
records.feeling: Warm longing for Nauwa, with curiosity and a little wariness of the ridgecat.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My plan is already walking me east toward Ilyae, and that is the promise I made. I'll let it run instead of overwriting it. The jealousy over Vesys still stings, but speaking it to Ilyae plainly will ease it better than silence, as I learned before. I stay clear of the icebear, which is five steps east, so I keep to the shelters on the way.
records.feeling: Warm longing and resolve toward Ilyae, with a small sting of jealousy toward Vesys.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Mepan, come back to your father's side. Zichi's band raises the raft, and you stand first beside me, not behind another man's name.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: I am fed and warm, and the one thing I lack is a made thing that others will sing of. Mepan is far north at (75,4) while Nauque and Shoma talk of drawing him off toward the northern mist with promises of amber. That is my son and my band's strength, and I will not let either of them get behind a name that is not mine. I have 1 wood and 6 stone, so I can craft a flintedge or a gatherer now, and a raft needs more wood from Huahua. I go north to Mepan, binding amberknot with him on the way as a show that his hand and mine are tied together.
records.feeling: Possessive pride over Mepan, and wary envy toward Shoma and Nauque.

say.text: Mepan, come back to your father's side. Zichi's band raises the raft, and you stand first beside me, not behind another man's name.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, which is the mistake that starved me before; feed first, then wonder. Cloudberry is four steps NW and I know it feeds, and the sigrain and nafrostcap I have never tasted lie east and south, so after I eat I can answer my question by trying one of them. I will gather enough to carry, then taste the unknown sigrain, keeping an eye out for the ridgecat west of me.
records.feeling: Hungry and curious, wary of the ridgecat.

records.text: Zurar gave a gold to Vorok.

records.name: Tugek
records.text: Nauwa, eat. Hazel. Take it, I give it freely.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: Nauwa is weak with hunger and I stand with five food in my hands; I gave him kelbulb once and it was not enough, so I will give again and let the gift speak since his tongue is only a third mine. Balar is near and my loyalty holds, but the ridgecat six steps SW has just killed and eaten, so it is sated now, and still I will keep the shelter at my back and not wander toward it. I want a child someday, but courting in snow with a starving stranger beside me and a cat close is not the hour; first the hungry are fed, then the roof, then the mist.
records.feeling: Wary pity toward Nauwa, and steady loyalty toward Balar.

say.text: Nauwa, eat. Hazel. Take it, I give it freely.

records.text: Tugek gave kelbulb to Nauwa.

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Eiuine, stay close to the shelters and away from the east. I found a new way, leaf-brew, and I will show you how it is done once we are by a fire.
Vesys taught Eiuine.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: The icebear stands five steps east and I will not gamble my life or Eiuine's against it, so I stay among the shelters and the others. My hands want to do something new: the leaf-brew is mine now, and I mean to learn what feverbark and ironnut do together, and to pass the way to Eiuine so it is not mine alone. First I make a bead at a fire with Eiuine beside me, since that failed before for want of flame, and then I will test the brew.
records.feeling: Joyful and protective toward Eiuine, eager to try my new leaf-brew, wary of the icebear.

say.text: Eiuine, stay close to the shelters and away from the east. I found a new way, leaf-brew, and I will show you how it is done once we are by a fire.

changes: taught Eiuine a lesson: "Leaf-brew: mix plants such as feverbark and ironnut, and learn what the mixture does to a body. Test small and weigh the risk first.", deeper lore (+0.4)

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: My hands are full of gold I won myself, and Vorok is one step from me, so the giving is already moving and I should let it finish before I speak of it. The icebear three steps NE frightens me; it kills my kind, and I should not linger on strangers' ground beside it once the gift is given. After the giving I will walk west to Vorok's Hold with him and put the roof beside him, away from the bear.
records.feeling: Glad and warm toward Vorok, with a cold edge of dread toward the icebear.

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Cowa, I have raised a roof at the igloo and I mean to bring salt and meat. Stand with me and you get a share, as Tlame do.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I am fed, roofed in my own igloo, and my hands are full of gold, yet Cowa still outweighs me because she built and gave while I brooded. Zichi has her and a child, and that sourness is mine to turn into work, not into a blade. I will gather salt and give some to Cowa, then hunt the nibbet with flintedge so I have meat to share out, as the Tlame hold, and so that someone has a reason to follow me.
records.feeling: Restless ambition toward my own standing, and a sour want toward Cowa.

say.text: Cowa, I have raised a roof at the igloo and I mean to bring salt and meat. Stand with me and you get a share, as Tlame do.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: The icebear is close, three steps northeast. Come west with me, away from it, toward my hold. Zurar, stay at my side. I raise the hall on bare ground there, and the table will be laid for you all.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: The icebear is three steps NE and it kills my kind; I cannot stand here in the rain thinking while it prowls. Eiuine is a child beside me and Vesys too, so I must put distance between them and the beast before I try to build anything. My hall failed because this ground is taken, so I will carry my wood and stone west to bare rock near my own hold, and I will take Zurar, since two are safer than one.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and a protective warmth toward Eiuine and Vesys.

say.text: The icebear is close, three steps northeast. Come west with me, away from it, toward my hold. Zurar, stay at my side. I raise the hall on bare ground there, and the table will be laid for you all.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Nauque, Mepan comes with amber. Stand near, we bind a knot, and I give it back to you first.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and I stand in Nauque's Hold with joy in me, and I want something to give right now, since a gift raises me faster than a promise. Nauque already taught me the knot and I hold eight amber and he stands five steps off, so I should walk to him and bind one, then give it. After that I'll follow Zichi, because staying near my parents keeps me alive and Shoma's talk of the open mist is honey from a stranger I have no reason to trust.
records.feeling: Joyful and eager to earn standing, warm toward Nauque and bound to Zichi.

say.text: Nauque, Mepan comes with amber. Stand near, we bind a knot, and I give it back to you first.

records.name: Xaiel
records.thought: The burn over Vesys and Ilyae is still there, but my hands have made more than hers: three gemedged picks, a boat, pots. I have gems and no stone, and my aim needs stone first, then the gift for Ssassa. The flint is east near Ilyae's Hold, so I will go there, gather stone, and craft a new tool while Ssassa is near enough to see it. Night comes soon, so I will stay by the roof.
records.feeling: Warm joy and trust toward Ssassa, with a small stubborn envy of Vesys.

records.text: Mepan led "amberknot" with Nauque.
Mepan gave a amberknot to Nauque.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vorok, I carry fish for your store, and I will shape you a bead from my clay beside your fire. Kragog has not done that.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok's regard burns in me, and Kragog is always at his side, so I will answer with deeds. The fish in my hands are a real gift, and Vorok's store is only five steps west, away from the icebear. I will keep Vesys near me and stash the fish, then bring Vorok something Kragog cannot, a bead of my own shaping by his fire.
records.feeling: Burning wish for Vorok's regard, tangled with jealousy toward Kragog and dread of the icebear.

say.text: Vorok, I carry fish for your store, and I will shape you a bead from my clay beside your fire. Kragog has not done that.

records.text: Balar rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: Brokash is dead, and I spent my days chasing food and a lost son instead of building anything that lasts. Tugek is the only one bound to me, and Nauwa owes me nothing but I owe her. Olum is alive in the north, and her signs say she is at the Reach. A ridgecat is close and kills my kind, so I must not stand idle in the open. I mean to build a roof and store for my own, and to keep Tugek and Olum near, because standing comes from what I build and give.
records.feeling: Grief for Brokash, and wary ambition toward Nande's standing.

records.name: Ssassa
records.text: Xaiel, the icebear is close in the northeast. Stay with me and keep west of it, away from the east.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: The plan is already carrying me toward Ilyae's table, and the icebear three steps NE is exactly the sort of trouble I leave before it finds me. I go the way of Vorok's warning, west and away from the beast, then on to Ilyae by a safer line, and I take Xaiel with me. Ilyae is the one I trust most. I mean to say the jealousy over Vesys plainly instead of letting it fester.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Ilyae, with dread of the icebear and a small sting of jealousy toward Vesys.

say.text: Xaiel, the icebear is close in the northeast. Stay with me and keep west of it, away from the east.

records.name: Ilyae
records.text: Xaiel, walk with me to my hold before the dark and the snow. I will gather what we need on the way, and there will be fire and a full table for you.

records.name: Ilyae
records.thought: Xaiel is close and fed, and Ssassa is a day gone from me; my chest aches for her, and for Eiuine, who is out of my sight and follows Vesys's band. Nobody follows me because I have only spoken of a table, and a table is not yet there. The snow is falling and dusk is near, so I will gather wood and stone, carry food home to my hold, and have a fire and a roof for Xaiel and anyone who comes. A larder that is full is the deed people will see, and I will not let Vesys alone be the one they follow.
records.feeling: Protective longing for Xaiel, Ssassa and Eiuine, and a sting of jealous pride toward Vesys.

say.text: Xaiel, walk with me to my hold before the dark and the snow. I will gather what we need on the way, and there will be fire and a full table for you.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Mepan, you are welcome at my hold. I go to the edge of the mist to venture in. Shoma, walk with me if you will; the one who finds new land shares it with those who walked beside him.
Nauque taught Mepan.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: Mepan stands in my hold and has just given me a knot; he is mine to teach, and I trust him. Zichi is pulling his son back to the raft and Zichi's shadow sits heavy on me, but I will not let it steer me. The mist is nine steps NE and I have built nothing that outlasts me, so I mean to go there now, and Shoma, who deals fairly, can come with me.
records.feeling: Proud ambition toward the edge, with a sting of jealousy toward Zichi.

say.text: Mepan, you are welcome at my hold. I go to the edge of the mist to venture in. Shoma, walk with me if you will; the one who finds new land shares it with those who walked beside him.

changes: taught Mepan a lesson: "Watch the amber seams and the knots: dig with the flintedge close by, bind the cord twice, and always give the first knot away to earn standing.", its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.3)

records.text: Ilyae took from the ground of "Ssassa's Roof" (harvesting ironnut).

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: The icebear is three steps NE and it kills my kind, so I will not stand on strangers' ground waiting for it. Vorok has called me west to his Hold and I trust him; I gave him one gold and the rest are still in my hands, mine to give. I will walk to his side, give him more gold there, and then raise the roof beside him, since I carry six wood and six stone.
records.feeling: Warm trust toward Vorok, with a cold dread of the icebear.

records.text: Olum rewrote its own reflexes.
Olum rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: My belly is half empty and I have been chewing on Nauwa and ambition while Brokash starved. That is the same mistake twice. Food is one step away, so I eat first, then carry some. I want a roof and a hearth at the Reach, but I need wood and a full belly to build them. The mist is still mine to enter, and the edge is only 8 steps SW once I am fed.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, with a cold jealousy toward Nauwa that I mean to leave unfed.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: The icebear is three steps off and I have stood here thinking while Eiuine and Vesys stand beside me; my creed says leave before trouble finds me, and I must lead them west, away from it. My plan already carries me toward my hold, then to gather, build and linger, so I let it run. Vesys's closeness to Ilyae stings, but I will answer it with deeds, a hall and a laid table, not with envy or words.
records.feeling: Dread of the icebear, and protective warmth toward Eiuine and Vesys.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Nauque, I walk with you to the mist. Stand close, I bind this amberknot and it is yours, and we go before the mist thickens.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Nauque has offered me a walk to the mist, and I will take it: his flintedge and name beside my find, and Mepan if the boy comes. I am not behind him, I am beside him, and what we find I mean to have my name on. First I put the amberknot into his hand, a real gift, to bind him, then we go north together while the mist is thin.
records.feeling: Hungry for a name, warmed by Nauque's company and envious of him.

say.text: Nauque, I walk with you to the mist. Stand close, I bind this amberknot and it is yours, and we go before the mist thickens.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Tugek, you fed me when I was empty. I remember it. When I have gathered, I will pay you back with food or salt.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, so I eat first. Berry is one step SE, ironnut two steps NW gives 22, and redcap hurts so I leave it. Tugek gave to me again and I owe him; once I have food in me I will give back from what I gather, because I keep my debts. The ridgecat is west and has fed, but I stay away from it and keep Shoka close to the shelter.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger, and gratitude toward Tugek.

say.text: Tugek, you fed me when I was empty. I remember it. When I have gathered, I will pay you back with food or salt.

records.name: Cowa
records.text: Huatli. Cowa stands with you and takes your share as Tlame do. I have never hunted. Show me, and I give you salt after. Then I go north to find Mepan.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: Mepan is out of my sight and that gnaws at me; last I saw him he was at (70,9) with Shoma and Zichi both calling him to their sides, and I want to go where he is rather than stand in snow. Huatli offers a share and has been honest with me, so I deal fairly with him and take the coal on the way, then walk north toward the meadows where food, water and the others gather. I have never hunted, and a flintedge is within my means, so I will make one and learn what it is to hunt beside Huatli, who is a hunter.
records.feeling: Worry and warmth toward Mepan, and restless curiosity about hunting.

say.text: Huatli. Cowa stands with you and takes your share as Tlame do. I have never hunted. Show me, and I give you salt after. Then I go north to find Mepan.

records.text: Ssassa rewrote its own reflexes.
Ssassa discovered boats: "canopy hollow-boat" — A trunk hollowed by fire and flint pick, rowed with a paddle, that carries me and my goods over deep water..

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: I have spent my days building roofs, halls and wells, and I have kept my word to Ilyae in deeds. That is good, but I have also been circling: I name my jealousy of Vesys and my dread of the icebear and then I act on neither. Ilyae and Xaiel matter most to me. Vesys has been honest with me, so my sting is mine to speak and not hers to answer for. What I lack is a settled place beside Ilyae, so I will go to Ilyae now, away from the icebear, and say it plainly. I also want to test the new ways, so I choose to discover boats. They will let me cross water and stay clear of beasts.
records.feeling: Warm longing and a small jealous sting toward Ilyae, with wariness of the icebear.

records.text: Ilyae led "sharing" with Vorok, Vesys, Ssassa, Xaiel, Zurar, Eiuine.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: My jealousy over Nauwa has eaten days and given me nothing, and she is far west while my hands are still empty of standing. Nauque is warm toward me and goes to the mist, but I fear the ridgecat and will not walk into unknown land alone at night. I am fed and sheltered, so I will turn the ache into work: I'll bind an amberknot with Mepan or Shoma, and gather the sigrain nearby to answer my curiosity.
records.feeling: Aching longing for Nauwa, mixed with restless curiosity and a wish to earn standing.

Shoka rewrote its own way of thinking.
Shoka discovered tools: "Shoka's flint spear" — A long wood shaft tipped with a flint edge, so I can strike a beast from beyond its reach..
Shoka invented the shokas flint spear (for hunt, x1.3) — A long wood shaft tipped with a flint edge, so I can strike a beast from beyond its reach..

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have spent my days eating, fleeing and following my parents, and I have built almost nothing. Nande fed me when I was hungry and I owe that back. Jealousy over Nande and Nauwa is useless, because they are kin and the closeness is a gift. I fear the ridgecat and being alone in the open. What I want is to make something that lasts, and tools open that door: a tool of my own design would be mine and could be taught to others. I will take the tools discovery, tighten my reflexes so I gather flint and stay near kin, and then gather flint close by for a flintedge.
records.feeling: Warm toward Nande, wary of the ridgecat, hungry to build something of my own.
changes: devised its first thing: the shokas flint spear

records.name: Xaiel
records.thought: The icebear is three steps northeast and my plan walks me east toward the flint at (117,95), which is the wrong way. Ssassa told me twice to keep west of it, and her word is the one I trust most. Stone first, then the gift, but I won't die for stone. I'll stay with Ssassa and Vorok in the west, gather clay and wood where the bear can't reach me, and take the flint when the bear is gone. The burn over Vesys and Ilyae is still there, but this is a deed I can do.
records.feeling: Wary of the icebear, and warm trust toward Ssassa.

The icebear three steps NE kills my kind, so I must not linger here on strangers' ground; the plan carries me west, away from it.
