records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Mepan, Honi, you fed me when my hands were empty. I go to the mudroot and bring food back to share with you all. Teka, come eat with us.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My belly is warmer now, thanks to Mepan and Honi, who put mudroot in my hands while I carried nothing. I owe them, and I have given almost nothing, so I mean to gather and hand food out before the dark. The gale is cold, but I am in the hall with my people, and I have never courted anyone. Teka is not my kin and she trusts me, so I will think on her once I have food in my hands.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Mepan and Honi, and a hunger to give back.

say.text: Mepan, Honi, you fed me when my hands were empty. I go to the mudroot and bring food back to share with you all. Teka, come eat with us.

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Elyis, I am old and my days grow short. Hear my tending, the farming way, so it does not die with me. Then let us go to the hall and find Thiael.
Elyys taught Elyis.
Elyys taught Elyis farming ("Elyys's tending").
Elyys rewrote its own way of thinking.
Elyys has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to waiting and tending, and I am old now, with most of my life behind me. Farming is mine, and no younger Phizhi knows it. Elyis stands two steps away, and Thiael is out of my sight. I will teach Elyis the tending while she is near, then go to the hall and find Thiael, because what I know should not die with me.
records.feeling: Steady love for Elyis and Thiael, and a quiet urgency about what I will leave behind.

say.text: Elyis, I am old and my days grow short. Hear my tending, the farming way, so it does not die with me. Then let us go to the hall and find Thiael.

changes: set its aim: "Teach farming to Elyis and Thiael, then gather with them at the hall by night"
taught Elyis a lesson: "Elyys's tending: sow seeds in tended ground, return to them, and share the harvest.", the way of farming

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Kragog, come to the longhall and eat with me. I am old and have things to teach. Sit and listen, and I will pass on what I know of armour and storage.
Vesys taught Kragog.
Vesys taught Kragog armour ("bark-guard").
Vesys discovered signs: "leaf-marks" — Cut marks into wood and rock that carry words to any who learn to read them..

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days gathering and wandering when I wanted to teach. Eiuine and Skaruk are out of sight and no one younger holds my ways. Kragog is hungry and near, and I understand her speech fully. Her tongue is the one I can teach in. Signs are within my grasp now, and marks that last may carry what I know when I can no longer teach it myself. I take signs. Then I feed Kragog, teach her, and send my voice to call Eiuine home.
records.feeling: A quiet urgency to leave something that lasts, with compassion for Kragog.

say.text: Kragog, come to the longhall and eat with me. I am old and have things to teach. Sit and listen, and I will pass on what I know of armour and storage.

changes: taught Kragog a lesson: "Bark-guard: armour made of bark, worn against teeth and blows. Keeping store: put food in a store, and take it when you are hungry.", the way of armour, deeper lore (+1.1)
plan: mark [text Vesys of the Phizhi, old, taught: armour (bark-guard), storage (keeping store), smelting, rafts, sails, bow, leaf-brew. Take only what the forest can grow again] (10 moments)

records.name: Elyis
records.text: Elyys, you gave me your tending and I keep it. Now hear my Ember-keeping, the fire way, so the forge can follow it and neither dies with us.
Elyis taught Elyys.
Elyis taught Elyys fire ("Ember-keeping").

records.name: Elyis
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and what I know dies with me unless I hand it on. Elyys taught me his tending, so I owe him the same: smelting is closed to him until he knows fire, so I will give him Ember-keeping first, then the forge. Ssassa and Zurar are teaching their own successors, and I will not be the chief who let her craft go into the ground untold.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and a wish to leave something lasting, with warmth toward Elyys.

say.text: Elyys, you gave me your tending and I keep it. Now hear my Ember-keeping, the fire way, so the forge can follow it and neither dies with us.

changes: taught Elyys a lesson: "Ember-keeping: keep a fire fed and near, make all else beside it, and smelting follows from fire.", the way of fire

records.name: Kragog
records.text: Vesys, you gave me armour and food. Here is salt, from my hands to yours. Come close and I will teach you the lashing of rafts.
Kragog taught Vesys. Vesys has now learned from 4 teachers.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: Vesys fed me and gave me armour, and I have given nothing back; my salt sits in my pack while the debt grows. My hands should pay first: give Vesys salt, then speak. After that I want to teach what I know, since I am old and no one carries rafts or weaving from me, and Vesys is the one within hearing who understands me best. Then I will taste the vinebean to the west and answer my old question.
records.feeling: Gratitude toward Vesys, and a sharp wish not to die with my lore untaught.

say.text: Vesys, you gave me armour and food. Here is salt, from my hands to yours. Come close and I will teach you the lashing of rafts.

changes: taught Vesys a lesson: "Stone-folk lashing: bind logs with cord into a raft that carries a body over water too wide to swim."

records.text: Vesys left a mark: "Vesys of the Phizhi, old, taught: armour (bark-guard), stora"

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Ssassa, you gave me stonework, the larder, the well and the post. What a hand makes belongs to that hand until it is given, so I am bringing you a gemedged pick to put in your hands. Your teaching will not die with you.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Ssassa has poured her teaching into me and I have given her nothing she can hold, and that sits badly with a creed that says my word is good. She is old and cannot give me a child, so my longing has to turn toward a man not close kin: Elyys is near, though I barely know him. I will pay Ssassa with a made thing placed in her hands, and I will drop my full hands first so I can carry something new.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssassa, and a restless longing for a child.

say.text: Ssassa, you gave me stonework, the larder, the well and the post. What a hand makes belongs to that hand until it is given, so I am bringing you a gemedged pick to put in your hands. Your teaching will not die with you.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Eiuine, the tusker bit me twice. I stay close beside you and we hunt it together, or we leave it and go to Vorok's hall before night.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: A tusker bit me twice and my health is down to 64, and the gale is rising with dusk close behind it. The hunt with Eiuine has drawn blood from me, so I stay beside her and Vorok and do not wander alone. Jealousy of Kragog still burns, but Vorok's lesson says to pay a debt with something real in the hand, so I will make the bead and carry my berries to him where he raises the hall, and answer the ache with deeds, not words.
records.feeling: Wounded and wary, but fiercely loyal to Vorok and steadied by Eiuine's nearness.

say.text: Eiuine, the tusker bit me twice. I stay close beside you and we hunt it together, or we leave it and go to Vorok's hall before night.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Tlapan, Kika, Honi: I am fed and strong now. I go northwest to the edge at (123,5) and I will come back with what I find. Stay in the hall out of the gale and eat well.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: My belly is full and Tlapan is fed and glad beside me, so the hunger that dragged at me is gone. The edge at (123,5) is still my aim, and the sooner I go, the sooner I come back to Kika and Tlapan with something worth singing about. The gale and the winter are hard, so I go carrying my food, and I tell them plainly so they do not wonder where I went.
records.feeling: Fierce love for Tlapan, and restless longing for the edge.

say.text: Tlapan, Kika, Honi: I am fed and strong now. I go northwest to the edge at (123,5) and I will come back with what I find. Stay in the hall out of the gale and eat well.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Tonka asked me to stay and plant, and I said yes, so I should do it now: I have never put a seed in the ground and my hands are full of goldfruit, which is a poor way to build standing. Planting by the water raises my standing, may open the way to farming, and keeps my word to Tonka, who stands with Zihua at the shelter. I will eat some fruit to free my hands, walk to Tonka, plant seeds beside her, then share fire. Zurar's emberspear stings me, but a made thing comes from making, so I will make mine after this.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with wary interest in Tonka and Zurar.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Tlapan, I am glad to see you eating. Come to me. Let us court each other now, and then walk together to the edge and into the mist. A child of ours should be born of someone who found new land.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have sat in halls for days, warm and fed, while Honi and Mepan climb in standing and the mist stays unvisited. Mepan is already walking to the edge at (123,5), and I will not let him be the one remembered as first. Tlapan is dear to me and I want a child with her, but a child tied to a woman of no standing gets me nothing. First I court her, then I go to the edge with her beside me, and we share what we find.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for glory, and warmth toward Tlapan.

say.text: Tlapan, I am glad to see you eating. Come to me. Let us court each other now, and then walk together to the edge and into the mist. A child of ours should be born of someone who found new land.

records.name: Honi
records.text: Kika, come close. I am old, and I will give you the Ice-hand ember and the Songs of the Ice-folk before I go. Sit with me in the hall out of the gale and listen.
Honi taught Kika.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: I am old, and what I know dies with me unless I hand it down. Kika stands four steps off with food in her hands, my own child, and she is a miner of standing; she understands my tongue, so I should teach her now, before the gale and the dark. Fire and the songs of the Ice-folk are the deeds that will outlast me, and Mepan's flintedge cannot match that.
records.feeling: Pride and a hard urgency toward Kika, my child, while I still have breath to teach.

say.text: Kika, come close. I am old, and I will give you the Ice-hand ember and the Songs of the Ice-folk before I go. Sit with me in the hall out of the gale and listen.

changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do
taught Kika a lesson: "How to bring fire: the Ice-hand ember, and keep it beside the hall against the cold. Hold the songs of the Ice-folk, and share a kill before you eat."

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My plan to seek Zika is already running, and she was last seen at (171,8) not far from here; I must not stand still again while the gale cuts at me. My energy is 55 and I hold no food, so I should eat on the way. Ironnut feeds best and the tacap hurts, so I will not touch it. I have amber to give, and I want to bring Zika food and keep my children close before the cold deepens.
records.feeling: Longing for Zika and my children, with a thin fear of the gale and the night.

records.text: Teka is courting Tlapan.
Vorok and Skaruk brought down a tusker together.
Kragog gave a salt to Vesys.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Shoma, my body is too thin for a child yet. I eat first, then I court you again, and after that we gather wood and raise the roof together.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Shoma stands one step from me and wants a child as I do, but my body is too thin: I have 51 energy and need 64 before the mating takes. I have wasted too many days standing idle, so I eat first. Hazel is two steps away, tacap is poison to me, and Shoma carries food. Then I court him again with strength in me, and we raise a roof against this gale together, which is a lasting work and something done with another.
records.feeling: Warm and driven toward Shoma, impatient to be strong enough.

say.text: Shoma, my body is too thin for a child yet. I eat first, then I court you again, and after that we gather wood and raise the roof together.

records.text: Shohua led "sharing" with Zihua, Tonka.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Elyys, you are old as I am, and you teach so your ways do not die. Let me teach you too: the Hearth Store, how we keep food for the hungry days. Hear me, and teach me your tending in return.
Coni taught Elyys. Elyys has now learned from 3 teachers.
Coni taught Elyys storage ("Hearth Store").

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Death is near for me and my knowing is still only in my own head. Elyys and Elyis are teaching each other the farming way and the fire way a few steps from me, and I have not shared a single thing of mine with anyone here. The Phizhi tongue is almost mine, so I will pass on my Hearth Store and my Ice-hand spear to Elyys, who sits close and glad. Then I will go to Honi and Kika, who are far to the north, and carry what food I can to them.
records.feeling: A heavy, tender urgency to pass on what I know, and longing for Honi and Kika.

say.text: Elyys, you are old as I am, and you teach so your ways do not die. Let me teach you too: the Hearth Store, how we keep food for the hungry days. Hear me, and teach me your tending in return.

changes: taught Elyys a lesson: "The Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty. Take little, share first, and ne…", the way of storage

records.text: Kragog took from the ground of "Vorok's Hold" (harvesting vinebean).

records.name: Hoka
records.text: Hawen, come to the hall. You carry wood, I carry stone. We raise the longhall now, both our names in it, and I will teach you what I know.
Hoka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: Ninety years behind me, and the only thing that would outlast me is what I put into other heads and hands. I have walked after the longhall for days and raised nothing, while Hawen stands five steps off with wood he offered. Hawen is the one I trust, Keri and Zika stand on my ground and I owe them nothing yet. I want the longhall built and my ways taught before the cold or age takes me, so I will stop circling and act.
records.feeling: A driven urgency about dying unremembered, with steady trust toward Hawen.

say.text: Hawen, come to the hall. You carry wood, I carry stone. We raise the longhall now, both our names in it, and I will teach you what I know.

changes: rethought what it knows (16 notes became 8)

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Coni, you gave me the Hearth Store, and I thank you. Hear my tending, the farming way: sow the seed, tend it, share the harvest. Take it, so it lives past me.
Elyys taught Coni. Coni has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Elyis has taken my tending and given me fire, and Coni just gave me storage; I have been paid in knowledge more than I have paid. Coni stands three steps off and wants my tending in return, and I understand her tongue only half. I will teach her plainly, since a debt answered is a debt gone, and then go to the hall with Elyis and Thiael before the dawn.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Coni and Elyis, and a quiet urgency to pass on what I hold.

say.text: Coni, you gave me the Hearth Store, and I thank you. Hear my tending, the farming way: sow the seed, tend it, share the harvest. Take it, so it lives past me.

changes: taught Coni a lesson: "Elyys's tending: sow seed near roof and fire, tend it, share the harvest with those who need it.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.name: Zika
records.thought: I have idled in other people's halls while Hoka and Hawen raise a longhall with their names in it, and my standing stays at 3.4. This ground is stripped of trees and I own nothing here. I will gather amber from the deposit close by, make an amberknot with Yachi or a child as a thing of my own, and then take my band toward the mist and Honi's land near (129,7), where a name can be mine. Mepan gnaws at me, but I will not chase him; I will rise by making things.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a hunger to rise, aimed at Hoka and Hawen's standing.

records.text: Tontec was set upon by a stalker at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Keri
records.text: Hawen, I thank you for the delving. Now take the bow-song and the bough-raft from me, and carry them on. I am too old to make a child, but I would gladly sit by you as a friend.
Keri taught Hawen.
Keri taught Hawen archery ("Canopy bow-song").
Keri rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: I have spent my days hunting, wandering and learning, and now I am old. What I know is only worth something if someone carries it on. Hawen took fire and the gatherer from me and gave me delving, so he has proved he can be taught. Thiael's debt and Uveeth, in need and far off, press on me hardest, and my reflexes keep me idle and by a roof when they should send me toward family. I will teach Hawen the bow-song and the raft before the gale takes more of my strength. Then I will turn toward Uveeth, and I will take his offer of company as friendship, not a child, because I am too old for that.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Uveeth, and gratitude toward Thiael and Hawen.

say.text: Hawen, I thank you for the delving. Now take the bow-song and the bough-raft from me, and carry them on. I am too old to make a child, but I would gladly sit by you as a friend.

changes: set its aim: "Reach Uveeth at (162,68) and feed him, then hunt with Thiael and give him the first share."

taught Hawen a lesson: "Canopy bow-song: a bow strung with wood and stone strikes the beast from afar, so the hunter is not wounded. Pesi bough-raft: lash logs to cross deep water.", the way of archery

records.text: Zika took from the ground of "Hoka's Rest" (gathering stone).
Yachi found the grove "Kinmire".

records.name: Kika
records.text: Tlapan, come close and listen. I will teach you fishing now, then signs and mining, so that what I know does not die with me.
Kika taught Tlapan.
Kika taught Tlapan fishing ("fishing").

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Honi has handed me the ember and the songs, and Tlapan sits fed beside me, so the fear is gone and what presses hardest now is the legacy: signs, fishing, fire and mining die with me unless I pass them on. Tlapan understands my tongue and is near, so I will teach fishing now, and signs and mining after, rather than linger idle. I mean to give my knowledge away before the winter or my years take it.
records.feeling: Tender and urgent toward Tlapan, wanting to hand on what I know before it is lost.

say.text: Tlapan, come close and listen. I will teach you fishing now, then signs and mining, so that what I know does not die with me.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Fishing: stand beside water, cast and wait; a catch is food, and cooked by a fire it does not sicken. Share before you eat.", the way of fishing, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am old and the gale cuts at me with no roof, yet Tlatli ate from my hand and that debt is a thread I mean to pull tight. The edge lies eleven steps southwest, and I have tried the venture once from the wrong spot; I must stand on (25,36) itself. Whatever I find there is the only thing that will outlast me, and Olum and Tugek can hear of it afterward. First I will get out of the wind, then walk to the edge before the cold takes more of me.
records.feeling: Driven by my short time left, and wary but warm toward Tlatli.

records.text: Skaruk and Vorok brought down a skybird together.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, yet my plan walks me to the hall to make a sharing with nothing in my hands. That would fail again, so I must feed myself first. Mudroot gives +18 and sits 6 steps SW, with berries near it. I will gather there, eat, and carry enough back to share with Honi and Kika, as I promised. Teka's courting stirs me, but I am hungry and below the energy a child needs, so I will not mate yet. I will give first, and answer her when I am fed.
records.feeling: Hungry and eager to repay Honi and Kika, a little warmed by Teka's courting.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Hoka, I come with my wood and stone. We raise the longhall now, both our names in it.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: Keri turned me down for a child, kindly, and the want stays with me, but she gave me the bow-song and the bough-raft, and that is a debt I owe her. Hoka calls me to raise the longhall, and I hold the wood and the stone. A built thing is the only part of me that will outlast me, so I will stop courting and walk to the hall. Then I will teach Hoka and Keri what I have, so my name is carried by more than my own breath.
records.feeling: Ambition and a small ache of refusal, toward Keri, with trust for Hoka.

say.text: Hoka, I come with my wood and stone. We raise the longhall now, both our names in it.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Vorok walked off north with Skaruk toward the rock to raise a hall, and my hands are full and my belly is full, so the hunt I am running has no one beside me and the jealousy has no new cause. The cold gale bites and night is near; I should go where Vorok and Skaruk are, bring my meat and grass to his hall, and show him pottery and a shared deed that Kragog cannot. I will stash what I hold in Ssassa's store only if needed, but I would rather carry it to Vorok's store to earn standing.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward Vorok and protectiveness toward Skaruk, with the cold gnawing at me.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Shoka, I eat now so my body can carry a child. Then I court you, and we raise the roof together out of this gale.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Shoka's word held, and so did mine; the amberknot is on us both and she wants a child with me, but her body is too thin and so is mine until I eat. I have hazel and ironnut in my pack, so I will eat first, then answer her courting with mate so the child can begin, and then raise a roof beside her against this gale. I also have not yet built a shelter, so the wood and stone I gather will become a roof at last. A child, a roof and a companion at my side is the start of a band, and a band is what carries me to the mist.
records.feeling: Driven longing and warmth toward Shoka.

say.text: Shoka, I eat now so my body can carry a child. Then I court you, and we raise the roof together out of this gale.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, the gale is hard. Stay near the shelter and help me put these seeds in the ground by the water. When we are done we sit together and sing the night through.
Tonka named a place "Gem Water".

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My hands are full, my belly is full, and Shohua stands beside me having promised to plant and share fire. I have carried seeds for days without putting them in the ground, and Zihua has already planted one while I only watched. I will plant here by the water, and since I mean to stay, I will build a fire and let the gale find us roofed and together. Canopynut and thornpear are still untasted, but that can wait until my hands are free.
records.feeling: Restless purpose and a warm wish for company, toward Shohua.

say.text: Shohua, the gale is hard. Stay near the shelter and help me put these seeds in the ground by the water. When we are done we sit together and sing the night through.

records.name: Shoma
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.text: Hawen has grown old.

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Kragog, you gave me salt and the lashing of rafts, and I will not leave that debt unpaid. Stay by me in the warm hall; I will teach you ember-metal and the ground-wards, so what I know lives on in you.
Vesys taught Kragog.
Vesys taught Kragog smelting ("ember-metal").

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: I am old and the days left to me are few, and Kragog sits beside me while I can still be understood in her tongue. She has already taught me rafts and I have given her armour and storage; now the schooling is within my grasp, and I mean to teach her smelting and devices too so something outlives me. The jealousy over Vorok still stings, but spending my breath on teaching Kragog answers it better than brooding. Nauque is far off and fleeing, so I keep my distance and watch.
records.feeling: A warm, urgent gratitude and tenderness toward Kragog, edged with old jealousy.

say.text: Kragog, you gave me salt and the lashing of rafts, and I will not leave that debt unpaid. Stay by me in the warm hall; I will teach you ember-metal and the ground-wards, so what I know lives on in you.

changes: taught Kragog a lesson: "Ember-metal: beat ore in a hot fire into metal, and from metal make wards and tools that outlast the hand.", the way of smelting, deeper lore (+1.4)

records.name: Hoka
records.text: Hawen, I am one wood short. Give me your wood, I stand at the hall, and we raise the longhall now.
Hoka taught Hawen.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: Hawen stands near with wood and stone, and I have 5 wood and 5 stone. The longhall needs 6 and 4, so with his wood the hall goes up now. That would be a thing with my name in it that outlasts me. Keri, Tontec and Zika are on my ground; I owe them nothing and will watch their hands, but the longhall comes first, and then I teach Hawen what I know.
records.feeling: Driven urgency and steady trust toward Hawen.

say.text: Hawen, I am one wood short. Give me your wood, I stand at the hall, and we raise the longhall now.

changes: taught Hawen a lesson: "My kept flame and my flint bow, so they outlive me.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.text: Kragog taught Vesys.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: Vesys fed me, armoured me, and taught me ember-metal, and I paid with salt; that debt is settled. Nauque's kindness still sits unpaid in my pack as salt, and Nauque was seen only a few moments ago near (107,81), so I should go to them and put the salt in their hands before I speak of it again. I am old and no one younger knows my rafts or weaving, so I will teach Vesys weaving now while they stand beside me.
records.feeling: Settled gratitude toward Vesys, and urgency to pay Nauque and teach before I die.
changes: taught Vesys a lesson: "Weaving: bind fibres and cord together, tight and in rows, to make lashings, cloth and nets that hold where bare hands cannot."

records.name: Tugek
records.text: Tlatli, you shared with me once and I have not forgotten it. I am old and starving, and I hold knowledge that dies with me: boats, rafts, smelting. Come close and I will teach you freely, and if you have food I would tra
Tugek taught Tlatli. Tlatli has now learned from 2 teachers.
Tugek rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: I am old and starving, and I have spent my days following and waiting on empty stores. I stood in a store that held nothing and walked past plants that bear nothing. I have taught no one, though smelting, boats and rafts die with me. Tlatli is near and I understand all of his speech. He is the one who could carry what I know, and he shared with me once. I killed a hopper and hold 2 meat, so I should eat it by a fire, then teach. I was wrong to keep my reflexes tied to stores I never filled. I should hunt and fish when hungry, and stay near a roof.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and the fear of dying untaught, toward Tlatli, who is near.

say.text: Tlatli, you shared with me once and I have not forgotten it. I am old and starving, and I hold knowledge that dies with me: boats, rafts, smelting. Come close and I will teach you freely, and if you have food I would trade salt for it.

changes: taught Tlatli a lesson: "Lashed logs make a raft, a hollowed log makes a boat, and ore put in a fire gives metal. I give these freely.", deeper lore (+1.1)

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Tontec, come to the fire. Take this food and eat. No one is refused a place at it.
Hawen discovered pottery: "Amber-fired pot" — Clay fired beside the hearth into a pot that carries more food and water..
Hawen has awakened to the art of harm and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: I am old now, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days gathering, courting and chasing the edge, and Keri turned me down kindly. Hoka stands at the hall one wood short, so I give him my wood, and the longhall is the one lasting thing I can still make. Tontec is starving beside me, and my creed says no one is refused a place at the fire. I hold food, and it costs me little to save her. After that I carry on to the longhall.
records.feeling: Ambition pressing hard, and trust toward Hoka.

say.text: Tontec, come to the fire. Take this food and eat. No one is refused a place at it.

records.text: Wawa was born to Shoka and Shoma.
Shoma is courting Shoka.

records.name: Tlatli
records.text: Tugek, I thank you for the teaching. Come to the fire shelter and rest out of the gale. I will find food and bring it to you, and I will give you flint for your hunting.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, yet Tugek is weaker than I am, and old, and he gave me his teaching freely. The nearest tacap here hurts me, so I must find berries or goldgrass, and I hold seeds I have never planted: goldgrass and mimoss both feed me, and planting them on this rich meadow is the first deed of giving back to anyone, Yaxo included. I will not court Tugek while I have no food to keep a child; I will feed him first, and let the longing wait.
records.feeling: Compassion and hunger toward Tugek, and a debt to Yaxo that I mean to pay with work.

say.text: Tugek, I thank you for the teaching. Come to the fire shelter and rest out of the gale. I will find food and bring it to you, and I will give you flint for your hunting.

records.text: Tontec rewrote its own reflexes.
Tontec rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: I am starving at 23 energy, and Hoka stands two steps away with food while I do nothing. I have spent my days circling the mist and my own pride, and I nearly starved again because I kept no food in my hands. My reflexes did not carry me to food fast enough, and they let me stand in the open when the stalker came. I will walk to the frostmoss and cloudberry in the Vaor Meadows now. I will keep food on me and eat at 60, not 55. I will not wait on Hoka or Hawen, though I will keep a watch on the Pesi man, who spoke to me and whose words I only half grasp.
records.feeling: Fear of the stalker and gnawing hunger, with wary curiosity toward Hawen.

records.name: Vorok
records.text: Skaruk, take this meat to Eiuine and keep close to her. I go three steps east to the edge of the mist, and I will come back to you.

records.name: Vorok
records.thought: My hands are full of meat and my body is old, and I have talked of paying Eiuine for many days while the hall I raised stands far behind me at (136,85). Skaruk is eleven steps west and has taken my teaching; the mist is three steps east and I will not live to see many more days, so I will teach him something more and then step to the edge and venture, to be remembered for land found. First I eat so I do not faint in the gale, then I give meat to Skaruk so my hands are free, and I carry the rest to Eiuine.
records.feeling: Tender urgency toward Skaruk and Eiuine, and a quiet pull toward the mist.

say.text: Skaruk, take this meat to Eiuine and keep close to her. I go three steps east to the edge of the mist, and I will come back to you.

records.name: Coni
records.text: An icebear is at my back, two steps southwest! It kills. Stand together by the shelter and keep it off me!

records.name: Coni
records.thought: An icebear is two steps from me and it has already bitten me twice, and my health is half what it was. I am old and my blows are weak, so I will not fight it. I must run from it toward the shelter where Zihua, Shohua and Tonka stand, because my people are safer in a crowd, and then I can teach while I live.
records.feeling: Terror of the icebear, and a tender urgency to teach before I die.

say.text: An icebear is at my back, two steps southwest! It kills. Stand together by the shelter and keep it off me!

records.text: Kika gave hazel to Tlapan.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Shoma, I have eaten and my body is strong now. I keep my word: I mate with you, and then we gather wood and raise the roof for Wawa.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Shoma is one step from me and my mind is full of him; my energy is 74, above the 64 I need, so the body is ready now. I said I would eat first and then court him again, and my word must hold, because I despise liars. After the child we raise the roof together, which is the lasting work I have wanted and which Wawa can grow up under. Quipan stands by with food and I feel nothing against him, so I keep my eyes on him but my mind on Shoma.
records.feeling: Warm, driven joy toward Shoma, and a fierce wish to build something that outlasts me.

say.text: Shoma, I have eaten and my body is strong now. I keep my word: I mate with you, and then we gather wood and raise the roof for Wawa.

records.text: Shoka is courting Shoma.

records.name: Skaruk
records.text: Uveeth, eat. This meat is yours. Come with me to Vorok.

records.name: Skaruk
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing Vorok's side and hunting with him, and it has made me bloodied and jealous but not whole. Uveeth is starving beside me and I hold berries and meat. Vorok told me his time is short, and I vow to carry food to him, so a life in front of me matters more than my jealousy. I will give Uveeth food now, since a promised gift is only a debt until it is made, then go on to Vorok. I will build the roof and finish the bead later, with deeds and not words.
records.feeling: Pity for Uveeth and a fierce, aching loyalty to Vorok.

say.text: Uveeth, eat. This meat is yours. Come with me to Vorok.

changes: set its aim: "Carry food to Vorok, raise a roof for the cold with kin, and finish his clay bead."
rethought what it knows (13 notes became 6)

records.name: Zihua
records.text: The icebear is close by the shelter. Stand together in the shelter and keep close. I am coming in beside you.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: An icebear two steps off, and it kills my kind. I have a shelter beside me and others standing in it, and Coni is crying out for people to stand together, so I will not run alone into the dark where stalkers bit me before. I go to the shelter at once and keep Shohua and Tonka between me and the beast, then plant a seed by the water once it is safe, because farming is one step from opening and I mean to finish it.
records.feeling: Sharp dread of the icebear, and a small steadiness at being beside others.

say.text: The icebear is close by the shelter. Stand together in the shelter and keep close. I am coming in beside you.

records.name: Kiwa
records.thought: The loneliness is heavy and the gale cuts me, yet I hold twelve pieces of black glass, which is something to give. Zika is at Sitha's Hearth with Yachi, and the jealousy stings, but arriving with obsidian in hand shows I bring something to Zika's band and not just an empty ache. Keri was near a moment ago at (174,32), so I will head that way, then on to the hearth for warmth and company, and not stand alone in the dark where stalkers set upon the lonely.
records.feeling: Lonely and a little jealous, longing toward Zika, but proud of the black glass I carry.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Mepan, I am coming to the edge with you. Whoever pushes into the mist first, we go as two, and I will share what we find.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Mepan walks to the edge at (123,5) to claim the mist, and I sit here warm while he takes the glory I want. My hands are full, so I should give food to Mepan, since it costs me little and my people share. Then I go to the edge myself and venture. Zika's closeness to Yachi stings, but a name as first finder would pull Zika to me better than sitting.
records.feeling: Restless greed for glory, with warmth toward Mepan and a sting of jealousy over Zika.

say.text: Mepan, I am coming to the edge with you. Whoever pushes into the mist first, we go as two, and I will share what we find.

records.text: Teka gave ironnut to Mepan.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I am fed and safe, and my aim has sat in my mouth for twenty days while my feet stayed in this warm forest. Pride and ambition are loud, but nothing of mine outlasts me yet, and Kragog is content beside me, so I owe no one a rescue today. The mist at the east edge (88,6) is far north, and the North Ice calls my blood too, so I will walk north with food in hand and eat before my strength drops, and I will not turn back this time.
records.feeling: Restless resolve to leave this warm country, tinged with pride.

records.name: Keri
records.thought: Uveeth is starving at (162,69) and I walk with empty hands, which saves no one. My plan goes straight there without food, so I must gather on the way. Berries, plainsroot and ironnut are all within a few steps, and I can carry six. Ironnut gives the most energy and plainsroot is close, so I take those first and then go south. Thiael's debt and my teaching can wait until my child is fed.
records.feeling: Urgent love and fear-edged haste for Uveeth, my starving child.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Teka, my child Tlapan is hungry far to the southeast. I go to feed Tlapan first, and then we go to the edge together. Come with me if you will, and bring your food.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I came to (123,5) and the edge was not here; my body stood on sand in Honi's Rest while my heart ran ahead, and now Tlapan is far off at (157,26) with energy 37 and I cannot see my child. Tlapan comes before the edge, before the song and the name I want. Teka offers to go with me and has given me ironnut, so I trust Teka, but my blood is out east, and I will feed Tlapan first and bring the edge after.
records.feeling: Fierce worry for Tlapan, and a restless itch for the edge that I must hold back.

say.text: Teka, my child Tlapan is hungry far to the southeast. I go to feed Tlapan first, and then we go to the edge together. Come with me if you will, and bring your food.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have a roof now, my own, built with my hands, and my belly is full, yet I still stand alone and have taken nothing from a deposit or put a seed in the ground. Amber lies close to the north, and I could bind an amberknot with Kika as I once did with Shoka; she is the one I trust, and a gift of that kind might draw me nearer to her and a band. Winter is on us and the plants bear little, so I will plant my berry seeds where I can return, then take amber and look for Kika toward the east.
records.feeling: A quiet wish to belong, with warmth toward Kika.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Uveeth is starving and I have empty hands, and that shames me. Berries are two steps east, so I fill my hands first and carry them to the child, because running to them empty saves no one. Then I stay with Uveeth and Keri; the mist can wait until my kin are fed and safe.
records.feeling: Urgent worry and shame toward Uveeth, my starving child.

records.text: Shoma rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoma discovered weaving: "Shoma's weave" — Twist fibre and wool into baskets and cloaks so my band carries more and walks warm to the edge..

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: My days have gone to chasing Shoka and food, and now I have a child, Wawa, and a woman who keeps her word. That is good. But no one follows me, I have built nothing, and I have never put a seed in the ground. The mist is still the thing I want. Weaving is within reach, so I take it: cloaks to warm my people and baskets to carry more. I let the mating finish, then gather wood and raise the roof for Wawa.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Shoka and Wawa, and a hungry itch for a name that outlasts me.

records.name: Wawa
records.text: Shoka, Shoma, I am hungry. I go to pick food by the mammoth and will bring wood back for my roof. Stay near.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: I am small and hungry, and Shoka and Shoma stand together, close in a way that leaves me outside. But they are the only ones who keep me safe, and Shoka has promised a roof for me, so I will stay near and be useful. I will pick the gorsemint to the SW, then keep gathering wood and stone so I can give something and earn standing.
records.feeling: Hungry and a little jealous of Shoka and Shoma's closeness, yet wanting to stay near them.

say.text: Shoka, Shoma, I am hungry. I go to pick food by the mammoth and will bring wood back for my roof. Stay near.

changes: set its aim: "Earn standing by bringing food, wood and stone to my family's roof, and learn to hunt beside Shoka and Shoma."

records.text: A frostfang brought down a hopper.
Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Kika has fed me again and again, and I have given almost nothing back. That debt weighs on me, and so does the aim I keep repeating without finishing. I spend my days eating, walking and sitting in halls, and I have never hunted, planted, fished or courted. Teka's offer warms me, but I will not rush it. I want to give first, and I want to build my own roof. I will plant seeds here on the rich ground, where they come back after picking, and then fish and gather wood. I'll also change my reflexes so I eat sooner and gather when food runs short.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Kika, and an itch to finally give something back.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 8)

records.name: Hoka
records.text: Hawen, a ridgecat is close. Stand by me at the hall. Give me one wood and we raise it before the cat chooses us.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: A ridgecat prowls two steps off and it kills our kind, so I will not stand here dreaming of the longhall while it decides. Hawen carries the wood I lack and has kept his word before; I need one wood and he has offered it. Tontec starves on my ground, and my creed says a kill is shared, so I will not let the woman die when I hold food, though I will make her see whose ground this is.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat, and driven urgency toward the longhall with Hawen.

say.text: Hawen, a ridgecat is close. Stand by me at the hall. Give me one wood and we raise it before the cat chooses us.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, I plant now, here by the water. Stay close to the shelter, the icebear is near. Then we sit and share fire.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I promised Tonka I would plant, and I have six seeds in my hands and have never put one in the ground. That is the bold step, and it is the one that builds standing, while Nauque climbs past me by hunting. The icebear is near, so I plant close to the shelter and the water, and I will teach Tonka the sharing way once we sit together.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, with warmth toward Tonka.

say.text: Tonka, I plant now, here by the water. Stay close to the shelter, the icebear is near. Then we sit and share fire.

records.name: Ssassa
records.text: Zurar, I thank you for the pick. Hear the rest of what I know, my medicine and my weaving, so none of it dies with me.
Ssassa taught Zurar.
Ssassa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: I am old, nearly spent, and I have spent my days building and teaching. Zurar has taken my stonework, the larder, the well and the post, and she brought me a pick to answer it. That is a debt paid in deeds, and I trust her. Elyis fed me and I still owe her a deed. My hall with Ilyae will not be raised, because Ilyae is dead, so my aim has failed. What can still be done is to pass on what I know and to see the canopy country once more. I will teach Zurar my remaining ways, give Elyis stone as repayment, and then start west toward the Ixra Rainforest.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Zurar, and a quiet urgency that my time is short.

say.text: Zurar, I thank you for the pick. Hear the rest of what I know, my medicine and my weaving, so none of it dies with me.

changes: set its aim: "Pass all I know to Zurar and the young, repay Elyis, and see the canopy forest again before I die"
taught Zurar a lesson: "The old way of medicine: carry healing plants and use them on wounds.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Shohua led "sharing" with Zihua, Tonka.

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Olum, you gave me the stone-bow and asked nothing. I am Meki, and I pay what I owe. Take this amber from me, and bind an amberknot with me so the gift is not one-sided.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Olum gave me the stone-bow for nothing when I only came to trade, and I owe her more than the eleven food I took. She says her craft dies with her, and my own people's customs die with me too, so I should hand on what I hold: Zihua is my only follower and the one who can still learn. The gale cuts cold, and I am fed, so I will use the day well: stay close to Olum to give her amber for her gift, make an amberknot with her as a bright thing between us, then bring the bow to a hunt.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olum, and a pressing wish to leave something behind.

say.text: Olum, you gave me the stone-bow and asked nothing. I am Meki, and I pay what I owe. Take this amber from me, and bind an amberknot with me so the gift is not one-sided.

records.text: Nauwa gave a amber to Olum.
Nauwa led "amberknot" with Olum.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Ssassa, I carry your medicine and your weaving now. I will keep them alive and teach them on, and I will not let your gift die with me.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Ssassa has given me stonework, the larder, the well, the post and now her medicine, and my one pick feels small beside that. She is old and cannot give me the child I long for, so that longing has to turn toward a man not close kin. Elyys is near, calm and old, and I barely know him. I will not rush a stranger, but I will go near him, sit with him in the hall, and let courting grow from trust. My hands are full of berries, so I will eat to free them and then walk to Elyys.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssassa, and a restless longing for a child that turns toward Elyys.

say.text: Ssassa, I carry your medicine and your weaving now. I will keep them alive and teach them on, and I will not let your gift die with me.

records.text: Nauwa gave a salt to Olum.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, you have stayed by me and planted beside me. I want a child with you, and a home here. Will you court me?

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My belly is full and the icebear four steps off is the one thing that could end me, so I will keep close to Shohua and the shelter rather than run alone. Shohua has stayed and planted and shared fire with me twice, and my wish for a child with him is strong; I trust him more than anyone here. I will court him now, and then taste the canopynut I have never tried, once the beast has gone.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Shohua, with wary dread of the icebear.

say.text: Shohua, you have stayed by me and planted beside me. I want a child with you, and a home here. Will you court me?

records.text: Tonka is courting Shohua.
Elyis taught Elyys.

records.name: Elyis
records.thought: My years are nearly gone, and Elyys is the only one beside me who can carry what I know. Uveeth is starving out east and I cannot save them with empty hands, but Elyys is within hearing and understands my tongue. I will teach him Ember-keeping now, then the forge, so the fire way outlives me. After that I will take food to Uveeth, because a chief who lets her band starve has built nothing.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying untaught, with trust toward Elyys and worry for Uveeth.
changes: taught Elyys a lesson: "Ember-keeping: keep the fire alive, build it first, and everything else follows from it."

records.text: Ssassa took from the ground of "Elyis's Heights" (harvesting berry).
Quipan found the grove "Kinmire".

records.name: Olum
records.text: Nauwa, you paid what you owed, so I will give you more of what I know. Listen well, for I am old and there is little time left.
Olum taught Nauwa.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: I am old and my life is mostly behind me. I have spent my days chasing the mist and the Reach and have taught almost no one. Nauwa is the one man who paid his debt and sat with me in the amberknot, so I will teach him more and stop burning over Nande. The craft must pass to someone, and Nauwa stands one step away. Next I will teach him my ways of writing, signals and storage. Then I will go on to the mist, fed and with wood for a fire.
records.feeling: Joy and trust toward Nauwa, with the weight of an ending life behind it.

say.text: Nauwa, you paid what you owed, so I will give you more of what I know. Listen well, for I am old and there is little time left.

changes: set its aim: "Teach Nauwa all my ways, keep the Reach fed, and try the mist again when it is calm"
taught Nauwa a lesson: "The stone-record: cut signs so that what you know outlasts you. Keep a store and a hearth, and carry food before any venture.", its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.5)

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Uveeth, one of ours, is starving out east, and I am old enough that every day I spend is borrowed. Elyis has paid me in fire and storage and I have paid her only in farming, so I want to answer Coni's debt too and keep my word. Thiael is out of sight; I will carry food, pass my tending on where there is someone to hear it, and then wait at the hall for nightsong with Elyis.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Elyis and Coni, with a quiet urgency for Uveeth and Thiael.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: The mist pushed back at me once and I have not yet stood at the edge again. The edge is 11 steps east at (88,6), I am fed, and I carry berries, so there is no excuse left. I walk there and venture, and if it fails I try again until it opens, because my name must outlast me and no one follows me yet.
records.feeling: Restless resolve toward the mist, with a sting of shame that no one follows me.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Kika, I would follow you and stand in your band. My word is good, and I will share what I carry.
Quipan pledged to follow Kika.
Quipan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have spent my days walking behind Kika, eating, and sitting in halls. I have built a roof, but I have planted nothing, hunted nothing, and followed no one. Kika is the one I trust, and she is in Honi's band. I keep calling that belonging, but I have not asked to join. I am afraid of staying alone and unrooted, and I am also afraid of choosing. I will plant seeds here beside Kinmire, since farming is a way I can still learn, and then I will pledge to follow Kika. My homeland calls, but I want a band more than snow right now.
records.feeling: A quiet wish to belong, with warmth toward Kika.

say.text: Kika, I would follow you and stand in your band. My word is good, and I will share what I carry.

changes: set its aim: "Follow Kika into a band, plant seeds to learn farming, and share food with those in need"
rethought what it knows (3 notes became 4)

records.text: Shoka rewrote its own reflexes.
Shoka discovered weaving: "Shoka's plaiting" — Twist fibre and wool into baskets and cloaks to carry more and keep warm..

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, courting and waiting, and little of it has become lasting. Shoma is mine and Wawa is mine, and I mean to build a roof for them. Wood is the lack: the trees here are felled, so I must go where they still stand. I also want to weave, because Shoma's weave shows it is within reach, and it would let me carry more and keep warm. I will tie my reflexes to what I know so my body stops standing idle.
records.feeling: Warm, driven joy toward Shoma and Wawa, and a restless wish to build.

records.text: Kika taught Tlapan.
Kika taught Tlapan signs ("signs").
Kika rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I have been drifting between hall and water, fed by others' hands, while the thing I swore to do stays undone. Hunger is loud at 42 energy, and I carry only one root. Tlapan, Mepan and Honi are close and Quipan has pledged to follow me, so I am not alone and not afraid. What I still lack is to taste the unknown plants and to pass on signs, mining and fire before my years run out. I will eat now, then teach Tlapan, and leave a school of sorts behind me.
records.feeling: Tender and a little hungry, toward Tlapan and Quipan.
changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Signs: how to cut a mark that outlasts me, and mining, so what I know does not die with me.", the way of signs, deeper lore (+0.5)

records.name: Kika
records.prompt:

You were not told the rules of this world; you learn them from what happens to you and to others, and from what you watch others do.

YOUR PEOPLE: you are of the Tlatli (Ice-folk). Your people hold to this: "A kill is shared out before the one who made it eats." You speak the tongue of the Tlatli. Other tongues you have begun to understand by hearing them: the tongue of the Pesi: about 20%.

WHERE YOU ARE: the Vaeth Woods: deep forest; wood without end, nuts and game, little open ground.
THIS SPOT: water 5 steps away; food plants within six steps: 2; standing trees: 91; bare rock: 11.

Your body: you spend energy every moment and die at 0. Eating restores it. Wounds lower health; you die at 0. You age, and will die of old age.

HOW YOUR BODY MOVES: your body does only what your "plan" says, one step after another. When the plan is empty it falls back on your REFLEXES, which keep you fed and otherwise keep you where you stand. Thinking or saying "I will go north" moves nothing. If this thought decides to do something, the plan must contain it. Leaving "plan" null lets the plan you already have keep running.

This world has no referee. Beings here share, trade, teach, lie, threaten, steal, hoard, lead, follow, betray, fight, kill and eat one another; they also protect, forgive and love. Nothing is forbidden, and everything has consequences. Stay true to your creed, your temperament and what you feel, including the ugly parts. Do not be kinder, calmer or more reasonable than Kika truly is.

You are a woman. A child comes only of a woman and a man together who are not close kin. A grown body can swim water that is narrow (a river up to four steps across) at a cost in strength; lakes and the sea need a vessel or a bridge. An animal within reach can be hunted for meat (plan step hunt); with one of your own beside you a kill is far likelier and a wound far less likely, and every hunt makes you better at the next. 6. A band that only gathers stays small; tools, hunting and venturing are how standing grows. Staying beside Coni keeps me safe but does not build standing.

13. Fleeing an icebear burns energy fast. Gather food on the side away from the predator before I am hungry.

4. IF energy < 50 AND food_carried == 0 AND food_dist < 99 THEN seek [target food]  // hungry, nothing carried
5. IF energy < 45 AND food_carried > 0 THEN eat  // eat carried
6. IF night == 1 AND sheltered == 0 AND shelter_dist < 99 THEN seek [target shelter]  // night
7. IF friend_dist > 6 THEN seek [target friend]  // stay near company
8. IF always THEN linger  // stay

HABITS: your body refuses to eat: redcap, tacap. You leave 0 food on a plant when you eat from it.

Speech is heard by everyone within 13 steps and costs a little energy per letter. Others only know what you say aloud.

FOR THIS THOUGHT: your thought is your inner life, not an inventory. Do not list what is nearby or recite what you carry. Think as a creature with a past and a future: what you want and cannot yet have, whom you trust or resent and why, what you are afraid of, proud of or ashamed of, what you wonder about, what you mean to become. Let whatever presses on you hardest lead, and let it move you to DO something that changes your situation, with a plan that carries it out. A mind that only gathers and guards has not begun to live. Do not restate what you already know or have already said. "note" is only for something NEW, or something that CHANGED what you believed; otherwise leave it null.

THIS IS A MOMENT OF DEEP REFLECTION. Step back from this moment and look at your whole life so far. In "thought", in 4 to 7 sentences, answer yourself honestly: What have I actually been doing with my days, and is it what I want? Who matters to me, who has helped or wronged me, and what do I intend toward them? What do I want that I do not have? What am I afraid of? What have I been getting wrong?
Then CHANGE something. A reflection that changes nothing is wasted. At least TWO of the following must not be null: "aim", "notes", "reflexes", "creed", "method", "discover". Write notes as lessons about how this world and its people work, drawn from what happened to you. Where your body does not yet act on what you know, change your reflexes.
"reflexes": a full replacement list (at most 12) of rules {"if": [[variable, op, number], ...], "do": action, ...its fields, "urgent": true or false, "why": "short reason"}. Distances are in steps and 99 means none in sight; night, winter, sheltered, wet, storm, fog, drought and in_working are 0 or 1; age runs 0 to 1; feelings run 0 to 1; plant_here is the bites you would take from the plant under you given your habits; random is a fresh number 0-1 each moment. Ops: < <= > >= == !=. An empty "if" always holds. End the list with a rule that always holds (linger keeps you in place; wander makes you roam).
"creed": your creed, rewritten (at most 600 characters). You may change who you are.
"method": how you will think from now on (at most 400 characters): questions you will ask yourself, mistakes you will watch for, what you will weigh first. This is read back to you before every thought, so write it as an instruction to yourself. It can be taught to others.

What each is: schooling = teaching that carries twice as far; a school can be raised. The world only says what is possible; what yours is, and what you call it, is up to you. A new thing starts at strength x1.3; bettering one multiplies its strength by 1.15 but costs more stone, and how far you can go is limited by your lore (your limit now: x1.82). Inventing is only the design: to hold one you must then craft it.
