records.name: Yachi
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, so food comes first: mudroot feeds best of what is near, and ironnut too. The dunecat 4 steps north is a real dread, so I will go south and away from it, toward Kiwa, my child, who stands near the ironnut. Then I go on to Zika, with others close beside me instead of alone, because stillness has cost me before.
records.feeling: Hungry and wary of the dunecat, but warm toward Kiwa and longing for Zika.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and Zurar already carries my medicine and weaving, so my debt to her is settled. Elyis fed me and I still owe her a deed. I am standing on her people's ground with my hands full and her store close by, so I will carry my wood and stone to her store and leave food there before I walk on toward the canopy. Zihua, Shohua and Tonka are strangers whose words I only half understand, and I will keep a careful distance while I pay what I owe.
records.feeling: A quiet urgency to pay Elyis what I owe, and wary curiosity toward the strangers.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: My belly is full and the cold days are here, and I still have no roof of my own. I have 6 wood, enough for a shelter, so I will build one here by the water and good ground and stop begging a place beside Shoka and Shoma. A roof of my own is standing I can bring them, and then I can learn to hunt beside them from a place that is mine.
records.feeling: Restless and wanting a place of my own, with a pang of jealousy toward Shoka and Shoma.

records.text: Wawa built a shelter.

records.name: Hawen
records.text: Hoka, take my wood. Raise the longhall now, and let the cat find us inside the shelter.
Hawen taught Tontec.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: A ridgecat is two steps west and I am old, so I will not meet it with my weak blows. Hoka asked for one wood to raise the longhall, and I hold five wood and six stone. If I give him the wood he has the six he needs and the stone is already his. Then both our names stand in the one thing that will outlast me. Teaching Tontec the old way of fire would also leave something of me alive after I die, and she is frightened and has no people here.
records.feeling: Ambition and dread pressing together, with trust toward Hoka.

say.text: Hoka, take my wood. Raise the longhall now, and let the cat find us inside the shelter.

changes: taught Tontec a lesson: "The old way of fire: keep it tended, feed it wood, and never refuse a body a place beside it.", deeper lore (+0.8)

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: Kika, you have fed me and taught me, and I mean to repay you. I plant seeds by the water now, then I fish and bring the catch to you and Mepan.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: Kika has fed and taught me again and again, and I have hunted nothing, planted nothing and fished nothing. I carry six seeds and wood and stone, so I will plant here by the water and then try fishing where the water really is, so I give something real back. A mammoth is too great to hunt alone, so I will not rush at it, but I will think on mustering the band for it later.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Kika, and an itch to finally give something back.

say.text: Kika, you have fed me and taught me, and I mean to repay you. I plant seeds by the water now, then I fish and bring the catch to you and Mepan.

records.text: Hoka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Hoka
records.thought: My days have gone to guarding ground, fretting over a hall and counting what I lack, while age wears me down. Hawen has kept his word every time, and he is the one I trust. His wood is the last piece, so I should stop circling it and raise the longhall now, with the ridgecat near and a roof to retreat to. Tontec starves on my ground, and a kill is shared, so I should feed her from my store rather than let a guest die. Afterward I must teach Hawen what I know, because what I carry dies with me.
records.feeling: Urgent hunger to leave something standing, and trust toward Hawen.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 5)

records.name: Honi
records.text: Tlapan, come to the hall with me. I will teach you the Songs of the Ice-folk before the dark.
Honi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: I am old, and most of my days went to walking after food and after Coni, with too few deeds left standing behind me. Kika, my child, is the one who matters most now. She took the ember and the songs yesterday, so some of me will outlast me. I want Coni near and a legacy that others sing, and I fear dying with Tlapan and Quipan untaught. I have been letting reflexes leave me idle when I should teach and keep the fire, so I will go to the hall, where my band is, and teach there.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and tenderness toward Kika, and a fear of dying untaught.

say.text: Tlapan, come to the hall with me. I will teach you the Songs of the Ice-folk before the dark.

records.name: Zika
records.thought: I have idled long enough while Shoma and Hawen climb past me, and my standing sits at 3.5. The way of tools has come within my grasp, so I will take it now at this reflection; a chief who can invent tools has something of her own to show. Then I will gather obsidian where Shoka just worked, cut an edge of my own, and take my band toward the mist where my name can be set on new land. Mepan still gnaws at me, but I will not chase him.
records.feeling: Restless pride and hunger to rise, aimed at Shoma's standing.
changes: planned 1 step its body does not know how to do

records.text: Zichi has grown old.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: A frostfang prowls ten steps NE and has already bitten me four times, so I will not stand in the open alone again. Elyis's band is three strong bodies close by, with a hunter's bow and spear among them, and I have nothing to give them but my willingness. I cannot speak their tongue, but a gift needs no words: I will pick berries beside me and hand some over, then stay near them where the beast fears to come. If I mean to be a hunter worth singing of, I must first earn a place beside hunters, not hide in a hole.
records.feeling: Wary hunger to prove myself, and fear of the frostfang that stalks me.

records.text: Mepan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the edge, and each time something pulled me back: Tlapan hungry, a gale, a stray plan. The edge at (123,5) is real, but I reached Honi's Rest and found no mist. That tells me I misjudge where the venture happens, and I should check it rather than run on longing. Tlapan is fed and glad, Kika is near, and Teka has offered to go with me, so now is the time. I do not want to be the man who only talks about the edge. A dunecat is 5 steps north, so I will keep my flee reflex and stay in company. I will go once I have eaten and the dunecat is behind me. Kika's standing is higher than mine, and I will not be jealous. A true explorer earns standing by coming back with something.
records.feeling: Restless longing for the edge, and steady love for Tlapan and Kika.
changes: rethought what it knows (9 notes became 8)

records.text: Zika won obsidian from the ground.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, I am Zichi of the Meki. Come stand by me and share meat. I have ways to teach, snares and frost-shield, and a band is stronger than one.
Zichi taught Teka.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Huahua is dead and the raft is still unbuilt, and my life is four-fifths spent. Teka stands five steps off, strong, with six food and no leader, and I want her near me. I am fed and old, so now is the time to bind someone and pass on what I know before it dies with me. I will share food with her, teach her the ice-snare and frost-shield, then cut wood for the raft.
records.feeling: Driven and a little grieved for Huahua, with hungry ambition toward Teka as a possible follower.

say.text: Teka, I am Zichi of the Meki. Come stand by me and share meat. I have ways to teach, snares and frost-shield, and a band is stronger than one.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The ice-snare: set a device where beasts pass, and the kill comes without the chase.", deeper lore (+1.2)

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: My belly is empty and food stands under my feet, so I eat first. A frostfang is close to the south and has already bitten me once, and I will not stand idle for it again. Once fed, I go to the shelter Keri built and stay near Skaruk and Elyis, since the band is safer together than I am alone.
records.feeling: Starving and afraid of the frostfang, and I want company.

records.text: Zichi led "sharing" with Teka.

records.name: Tontec
records.thought: A ridgecat is four steps west and it kills my kind, so I stay inside Hoka's Rest, near the shelter and the hall, and let no pride draw me out. I am fed but carry nothing, and winter plants bear little. Redcap hurts me, so I will not pick it. Hawen has taught me twice and gave me a lesson without asking for anything, so I answer in kind. I will gather amber one step away, which I have never done, and keep my wood for Hoka's hall if the cat comes close. Standing comes from giving and learning, so I stay near Hawen and give him amber.
records.feeling: Wary fear of the ridgecat, and curious gratitude toward Hawen.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, I will stand with you. First I push into the mist at the edge just west of here. Come with me, and we share whatever we find.
Teka rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: I have spent days in warm halls and called it living. My standing is 1.0 and Zichi's is 10.0, and I have made nothing and led no one. The edge is 5 steps west, and I keep walking to the wrong place, which is a failure of my own plan. Mepan is dear to me and Zika stings me, but glory would answer both. I will stand on the real edge at (109,7) and venture, then bind Zichi to me, since he has flintedge and lessons to teach.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for glory, with wary envy toward Zichi.

say.text: Zichi, I will stand with you. First I push into the mist at the edge just west of here. Come with me, and we share whatever we find.

changes: rethought what it knows (3 notes became 4)

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Shoma, come with me to the standing trees in the SW. We cut wood together and raise the roof for Wawa, and we find her on the way. Take this mimoss first, so you walk fed.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: My hands are full of obsidian and mimoss, and Shoma stands three steps away, trusting me wholly while Wawa wanders out of my sight. I promised him the roof and I keep my word, but wood is the lack and the trees here are felled, so I must go to standing forest with Shoma beside me, not alone. I will give him something first to earn his hand in the work, and then we walk SW toward the trees together, because a hall for my child is the lasting thing I am after.
records.feeling: Warm, driven joy toward Shoma, and unease that Wawa is out of my sight.

say.text: Shoma, come with me to the standing trees in the SW. We cut wood together and raise the roof for Wawa, and we find her on the way. Take this mimoss first, so you walk fed.

records.text: Shoka gave mimoss to Shoma.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, I court you. I want a child with you and a home here by the water. Come into the shelter, the icebear is near.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: Tonka asks for a child, and I want it: she stayed beside me through the gale and the icebear, and my hands have finally put seeds in the ground. The icebear is 4 steps north and could kill us both, so I go to the shelter by the water where Tonka and Zihua stand and court her there. A child, a home at the water and a name on this place are the first things I would make that outlast me.
records.feeling: Warm, bold desire toward Tonka, with a hard edge of dread at the icebear.

say.text: Tonka, I court you. I want a child with you and a home here by the water. Come into the shelter, the icebear is near.

records.text: Shohua is courting Tonka.
Tonxo was born to Shohua and Tonka.
Tonchi was born to Shohua and Tonka.
Tlatli rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: I am starving at energy 20, and my days have gone to wandering and giving words while I carried nothing. I owe Yaxo work, and I have not gathered wood or stone even once. A bristleboar bit me and it stands one step away. I am bold only 0.2, so I will not fight it alone. The tacap and redcap hurt me, so I must find food that feeds me. My reflexes need to send me to food that actually feeds, and to keep me away from animals that bite when I am weak. I will change the reflexes and the notes, then gather flint, wood and stone for a spear, and hunt only when I am able.
records.feeling: Hunger and fear of the boar, and a debt toward Yaxo that I have not paid.
changes: rethought what it knows (10 notes became 6)

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Shoka, I come with you to the SW trees. We find Wawa, cut wood and raise her roof. Walk beside me, and when the roof stands we go on toward the mist together.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Wawa is out of my sight, and Shoka has asked me to walk with her to the trees in the SW to find her and raise a roof. She keeps her word when I keep mine, so I go beside her. This is the first band I could lead: Shoka, Wawa and me. I will feed them and build with them, and the mist comes after. First I need wood, stone and food in my pack, and I mean to teach Shoka my weave and my tools as we go, so that she has a reason to follow me.
records.feeling: Warm, restless pride toward Shoka and Wawa, and a hunger to lead them.

say.text: Shoka, I come with you to the SW trees. We find Wawa, cut wood and raise her roof. Walk beside me, and when the roof stands we go on toward the mist together.

records.text: Huatli went past the edge of the known world and found new land, part of the Halka Heights: in the ground, iron, gold, flint; a herd of murrock that has never seen your kind.
Huatli pushed past the edge of the known world near (94,15) and found new land with in the ground, iron, gold, flint; a herd of murrock that has never seen your kind.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, I go south-east to the hazel and the mudroot to pick. Come with me, and we carry food back for Tlapan, Mepan and Honi before we eat our fill.
Kika taught Tlapan.
Kika taught Tlapan fire ("Hoka's kept flame").

records.name: Kika
records.thought: My belly is half empty and my hands hold nothing, and I have let others feed me for days while my own promises sit undone. Hazel lies seven steps SE where Yachi and Kiwa stand, and it fed me well eleven times, so I will go and pick, and carry some back to share before I eat all of it. Fire is the thing that dies with me, and Tlapan is near and understands my tongue, so I will teach it as soon as I am back.
records.feeling: Hungry but warm and glad toward Tlapan, Quipan and Mepan, with a sting of shame over my undone promises.

say.text: Quipan, I go south-east to the hazel and the mudroot to pick. Come with me, and we carry food back for Tlapan, Mepan and Honi before we eat our fill.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Hoka's kept flame: how to bring fire and keep it alive beside the hall in winter.", the way of fire, deeper lore (+0.4)

records.text: Tonka rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My children are born and Shohua stands beside me, and I'm full of joy. But I've spent days lingering and courting while the ridgecat and icebear prowl four steps north. I want this place to be safe for them, so I will build a second shelter and a store, then plant my seeds. I'll also stop thinking of Zihua as a stranger. Her standing is higher than mine, and she sheltered us from the icebear. I'm changing my reflexes so I don't sit idle, and I'm recording that the safe days need acting on.
records.feeling: Joy and warm love toward Shohua and our new children, with wary dread of the icebear.
changes: set its aim: "Raise Tonxo and Tonchi safely at Gem Water with Shohua: plant a field, build a store, and learn to hunt with the bow."

records.name: Zihua
records.text: Shohua, I will teach you the amber-hafted gatherer: one wood and one stone make a tool that picks faster. Stay in the shelter with me while the beasts are near.
Zihua taught Shohua.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: A ridgecat four steps north and an icebear five, and I am in the shelter with Shohua, Tonka and the children close around me; I will not run alone into the open. Shohua and Tonka court each other, so my longing for a child will not be answered here, and I should not press where a pair has chosen. I have never taught anyone anything and I owe Mepan a debt, so while I am fed and safe I will pass on something true to Shohua, who shared fire with me, and then stay inside until the beasts leave.
records.feeling: Dread of the ridgecat and icebear, eased by the warmth of those beside me.

say.text: Shohua, I will teach you the amber-hafted gatherer: one wood and one stone make a tool that picks faster. Stay in the shelter with me while the beasts are near.

changes: taught Shohua a lesson: "One wood and one stone make an amber-hafted gatherer; it makes picking stronger and lasts many uses.", how to make a amberhafted gatherer, deeper lore (+0.4)

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am old and the wolf at my back is close, but I stand in Nauwa's hall, fed and roofed, and Nauwa's kindness is a debt I still hold. Tlatli starved and ate from my hand; a debt like that is a thread, and I mean to pull it while my legs still carry me. Olum is the question that gnaws at me, and I have walked too long without asking her. I will go to her Reach and make a gift of the one thing I can build, wood into a mark and a meal, so something of me stands there after I am gone.
records.feeling: Driven by my short days and drawn toward Olum, wary of the wolf.
plan: mark [text Balar of the Kragrek stood here. What a hand has made belongs to that hand until it is given. Olum, come west with me.] (10 moments)

records.text: Zika found the stone "Tlama's Rest".
Zurar is courting Elyys.
Tontec took from the ground of "Hoka's Rest" (gathering stone).
Zika discovered tools: "glassedge" — I knap black obsidian into a keen blade bound to a haft, to cut meat and wood and to fend off beasts..
Zika invented the glassedge (for hunt, x1.3) — I knap black obsidian into a keen blade bound to a haft, to cut meat and wood and to fend off beasts..

records.name: Zika
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering obsidian and standing in other people's shadows while Shoma climbs past me. Obsidian in my hands is worth nothing until I make something of it, and the way of tools is within my reach, so I take it now and cut an edge of my own. My aim, the mist past the edge near (129,7), is the real thing I want, not hall-sitting. Yachi follows me and Kiwa is dear to me, but I have let my band drift apart, and I mean to gather them before I venture.
records.feeling: Restless pride, sharpened against Shoma's standing, and hunger to make something that is mine.
changes: rethought what it knows (8 notes became 7)
devised its first thing: the glassedge

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Zihua, thank you for the gatherer lesson. Stay with us in the shelter. I plant by the water and will share food with all at this fire.
Shohua rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have planted nothing in the ground, taught no one, and no one follows me. Yet I now have Tonka, two children, and a home at the water. My days went to wandering and standing idle, and that bought no standing. Zihua gave me a lesson and I have given nothing back. The icebear is close, and my children are small and need me alive more than they need me bold. I mean to plant here, teach Zihua and Tonka what I know, and make tools that raise my hand. I need stone for them, and I have none.
records.feeling: Fierce, glad protectiveness toward Tonka and the children, with dread of the icebear.

say.text: Zihua, thank you for the gatherer lesson. Stay with us in the shelter. I plant by the water and will share food with all at this fire.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Shohua, the icebear is close. I am hungry. Will you share your food with me, or come with me to the berries?

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: An icebear is three steps north and I am small, so I stay near Shohua and Tonka in the shelter, where I am safe. My belly is half empty, and the feverbark one step NE is only a little food, so berries two steps NW are the better pick if the bear keeps still. I want to be worth more than Zihua one day, and that starts with learning, so I'll watch Zihua teach the gatherer tool.
records.feeling: Wary of the icebear, and a little jealous of Shohua's closeness to Tonka.

say.text: Shohua, the icebear is close. I am hungry. Will you share your food with me, or come with me to the berries?

changes: set its aim: "Stay alive near my parents, learn tools, and earn standing by giving and teaching."

records.text: Shohua led "sharing" with Zihua, Tonka, Tonxo, Tonchi.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: An icebear stands three steps north and I am small, so I stay close to Shohua and Tonka in the shelter, where I'm safest. My belly is emptying and I have never tasted anything myself. Feverbark is two steps NE and berries two steps SW, but the bear is the greater danger, so I'll go for the berries, which lie away from it, and come straight back. I burn a little that Shohua leans toward Tonka, but I'm a child and I need them both. I want to learn what Zihua knows and earn some standing by doing, not just standing still.
records.feeling: Afraid of the icebear, and hungry, but safe near my parents.
changes: set its aim: "Stay alive, learn the amber-hafted gatherer, and earn standing by giving and teaching"

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I am thirsty and I stand at last beside water five steps off, so I drink first, then fish where the water really is, since my last try failed for lack of it. Kika has fed me and taught me, and I have never caught one fish for her; today the catch goes to her and Mepan. I carry seeds too, and the ground is rich here, so I plant them near the water before the dark and make something real to give.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Kika, and a restless wish to pay her back with my own hands.

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Thiael, my child, wait. Hear my tending, the farming way, before I die. Then come with me and Elyis to the hall for the night.
Elyys taught Thiael.
Elyys taught Thiael farming ("Elyys's tending").

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: My days run short, and I have spent them well enough. I taught Elyis and I have been paid in fire and storage. Thiael has never heard my tending, and he is six steps off, walking away east. Zurar's courting is kind, but I am old and I want no child now. I will answer her gently and keep to my own. Debt to Coni still sits in me, but Thiael comes first. Dusk is close, and I should be at a fire and roof with my band, not alone where frostfangs set on the lonely.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness toward Thiael, and gratitude toward Elyis.

say.text: Thiael, my child, wait. Hear my tending, the farming way, before I die. Then come with me and Elyis to the hall for the night.

changes: taught Thiael a lesson: "Sow the seed, tend it, share the harvest; keep seeds back for the next sowing.", the way of farming, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Kiwa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Kiwa
records.thought: I have spent my days carrying black glass and aching after Zika, and I have given nothing that raised my standing. Kika and Honi are weighed far above me, and I stand at 0.9 because I have never hunted, built, planted or gathered. Yachi sits by me and means no harm, so my jealousy is partly pride. I want standing and a child, and Tlapan is warm toward me. I will stop idling. I'll plant seeds, gather wood and stone for the tools I sense, and give obsidian to Tlapan and Kika to earn trust. The winter wolf and dunecat scare me, so I will stay near the hall and the others.
records.feeling: Restless, jealous of Kika's standing and drawn to Tlapan.
changes: set its aim: "Gather wood and stone to learn tools, plant seeds, and give obsidian to raise standing with Tlapan and Zika's band."

records.name: Tontec
records.why: the year turning toward the lean season

records.text: Vesys taught Kragog.

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: Kragog is 11 steps off, resting, and I understand her tongue fully. My years are nearly spent and no younger Phizhi holds my smelting or devices, so I must go to her now and teach rather than linger. The jealousy over Vorok is old and small beside the debt I owe her for salt and rafts. I will eat first so my body holds, then walk to her and carry the teaching through.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness and gratitude toward Kragog, with a thin edge of jealousy.
changes: taught Kragog a lesson: "Ember-metal: beat ore in a hot fire and it gives metal that holds an edge and wears into wards.", deeper lore (+1.2)

records.name: Keri
records.thought: Uveeth is starving far to the south and my hands are full of plainsroot, so now there is nothing to wait for. I will walk south toward (162,69) and eat on the way only if my strength drops. Old as I am, my teaching can wait one more day; Uveeth cannot. Thiael's debt I will pay by giving him the first share once I reach them.
records.feeling: Urgent love and fear-edged haste for Uveeth, my starving child.

records.text: Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.
Thiael rewrote its own way of thinking.
Thiael has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing the mist while my child starved and Keri drifted away. That is what I did wrong. The aim I set was meant to feed my kin, yet it pulled me from them. Elyys has just given me farming before he dies, and that matters more to me than any mist. I mean to feed Uveeth with my own hands first, then stay near my kin and sow seed so they never go hungry. My hands are full of berries, so the plan I already have, which carries them to Uveeth, is right. I will change my aim and reflexes so my body keeps me near my kin and fed.
records.feeling: Shame and urgent love toward Uveeth, and gratitude toward Elyys.
changes: set its aim: "Feed Uveeth and Keri with my own hands, sow and tend seed near my band, and teach them the bow and farming before I grow too old."

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, I killed a mammoth and the meat is shared before I eat. Take your portion and stand in my band. When you push into the mist I will come, and we build a raft for new land together.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Huahua is dead and my years are four-fifths spent. I hold 13 meat's worth of a kill, my hands are full, and Teka has offered to stand with me. She is strong and leaderless, and I want her bound to me before I die untaught. I will give her meat to ease my hands and bind her, then cut wood for the raft with her at my side, since Mepan is out of sight and I have too few followers.
records.feeling: Driven and a little grieved for Huahua, with hungry ambition toward Teka as a follower.

say.text: Teka, I killed a mammoth and the meat is shared before I eat. Take your portion and stand in my band. When you push into the mist I will come, and we build a raft for new land together.

records.text: Huatli made a tale: "Huatli Opens the Mist".

records.name: Huatli
records.title: Huatli Opens the Mist
records.text: Huatli pushed into the mist at the edge of the known world and it gave way. He found the Halka Heights, rich in iron and gold, with murrock that had never seen our kind.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: I pushed into the mist and it opened. New land lies from (74,7) to (114,14), and I was the first to stand there. Still no one follows me and I have no mate or child. Olum is 8 steps away, she is a woman, she answered my gifts, and she is old. I have taught no one, so my customs die with me. I will go to Olum and teach her, since she is within hearing range once I am near. I will carry food and then make an amberknot with her, which is something I have never done.
records.feeling: Proud of the opened land, and restless that no one follows me.
changes: set its aim: "Lead others into the new land I opened and teach them my ways, so my name outlasts me"
made a tale: "Huatli Opens the Mist"

records.name: Honi
records.text: Tlapan, you stand by the hall. Sit with me, and I will teach you the Songs of the Ice-folk and the Ice-hand pot before night falls.
Honi taught Tlapan. Tlapan has now learned from 3 teachers.
Honi taught Tlapan lorekeeping ("Songs of the Ice-folk").

records.name: Honi
records.thought: I am old and nearly spent, and Kika already carries the ember and the songs. Tlapan stands near her, still untaught in the Songs, and pottery dies with me unless I pass it on. Dusk is close, so I go to the hall now, sit with them and teach before the dark. Coni is far off, and I can only keep making deeds in my band's sight until she comes to me.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and tenderness toward Kika and Tlapan, with a fear of dying untaught.

say.text: Tlapan, you stand by the hall. Sit with me, and I will teach you the Songs of the Ice-folk and the Ice-hand pot before night falls.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "The Songs of the Ice-folk: sing of what has been so the dead and the absent are remembered, and share the kill before you eat.", the way of lorekeeping, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Shoma trusts me wholly and Wawa is out of my sight, and I will not let my word to them rot while I chase standing. A roof of my own making is the lasting thing I can build for them, and it needs wood from standing forest, so the forest to the NW or NE is where I go, with Shoma beside me. Ssassa outweighs me, but I will not let jealousy steer me; I will earn mine by building and by giving.
records.feeling: Warm, driven devotion toward Shoma and Wawa, with a prickle of pride-stung envy toward Ssassa.

records.text: Tonchi was set upon by a icebear at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.
Zichi led "sharing" with Teka.
Elyis taught Elyys.
Elyis discovered masonry: "Heights-stone" — Stone laid and fitted without gaps makes walls and towers that last past the builder's life..
Elyis has awakened to the art of harm and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Elyis
records.thought: My years are nearly spent, and I have spent them building and teaching, which I do not regret. But my hall stands twenty steps behind me while I wander in the rain, and Uveeth starves because I never kept a store that fed them. Elyys is my one true carrier, and I have given him fire. Smelting must follow, and then Thiael must hear what I know. I will found the next teaching on masonry, so that what I build outlasts me and stands as a hall of stone with my name on it.
records.feeling: Urgent pride and fear of dying untaught, with warmth toward Elyys and worry for Uveeth.
changes: taught Elyys a lesson: "Ember-forge: smelting, beating ore in hot fire into metal."

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Kika, I will come with you to the hazel and mudroot. We will carry it back for Tlapan, Mepan and Honi first, then plant seeds by the hall.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: My belly is full and my heart is warm, yet I keep following and sitting and calling it belonging. Kika asked me to come pick hazel and mudroot and carry it back, and that is a real thing I can do for those who fed and taught me. I will go with her, gather, then plant my seeds near the hall so I finally learn farming, and not turn my face from Mepan's shadow.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika, with a quiet wish to be useful to the band.

say.text: Kika, I will come with you to the hazel and mudroot. We will carry it back for Tlapan, Mepan and Honi first, then plant seeds by the hall.

records.text: Kragog has awakened to the art of cold and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. I have spent my days walking, drinking, resting and picking, and I have taught only Vesys. Vesys has paid me back with armour and ember-metal, and that debt is settled. Nauque's debt is still unpaid because I have not found them. They were last seen near (109,69), so I will go there and put salt in their hands. Zurar, my child, was seen there too, and Zurar is someone I could teach. After that I will teach whoever understands me, before my body fails.
records.feeling: Urgency to pay Nauque and to teach my child Zurar before I die.
changes: set its aim: "Pay Nauque with salt, teach Zurar what I know, then rest in Vesys's hold."

records.text: Zihua rewrote its own way of thinking.
Zihua discovered storage: "cold-larder" — A store on bare ground where I stash carried food and take it out in lean days, and with salt the meat keeps..
Zihua has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, mining and sheltering from beasts, and I am alive and glad, but I have no mate, no child and no follower, and Mepan's debt is still unpaid. The ones beside me here, Shohua, Tonxo and Ssassa, have shared fire and food with me, and I feel safer for it. I fear the icebear and ridgecat, and I have been slow to act on my own aims. I will keep to the warm company through the night, and then try one untried thing: storage, so I can keep food for lean days and for Mepan's road.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness among those beside me, with a thread of dread of the beasts.

records.text: Yachi rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I have spent these days chasing food and warmth and drifting between Zika and the hall, and I have not built or taught anything. I am fed and safe in company, so this is the time to act on my aim and not just stand. Zika was last seen NE near Hoka's Rest, and Kiwa is close by to the east. I will walk to Kiwa first, then on toward Zika, keeping the others near. I will give amber where it buys trust, and I will stop letting standing and envy of Mepan's flintedge pull me around.
records.feeling: Warm and glad among company, and longing for Zika and my children.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Quipan, you are ahead of me, so I follow. We pick mudroot and carry it back to Honi, Tlapan and Mepan first, and only then do we eat.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I have let Honi and the others feed me while my own promises sit undone, and that shame is sharp even through the joy of the hall. Hunger is still there at 56, my hands are empty, and I mean to go with Quipan and bring back food for Tlapan, Honi and Mepan before I eat any myself. Winter is thin, so the mudroot to the SE is the surest pick. Afterwards I will ask Honi about emberroot and tacap, since he has lived long and knows what the body bears.
records.feeling: Warm and glad toward Honi, Tlapan, Quipan and Mepan, but stung by my promises still undone.

say.text: Quipan, you are ahead of me, so I follow. We pick mudroot and carry it back to Honi, Tlapan and Mepan first, and only then do we eat.

records.text: Elyis gave berry to Uveeth.

records.name: Ssassa
records.text: Zihua, I am Ssassa. I mean no harm. Take this wood as a gift, and let us be at peace here.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My days are nearly spent and Zihua stands beside me, a stranger whose tongue I half grasp, strong and glad after the hall. I owe Elyis a deed and have put food in her store, but wood and stone are still in my hands, and the debt is not yet answered. I will give Zihua something small so I can learn what she intends, then walk on toward Zurar, who must take the rest of what I know before the canopy forest is lost to me.
records.feeling: A quiet urgency to leave something lasting, with wary curiosity toward Zihua.

say.text: Zihua, I am Ssassa. I mean no harm. Take this wood as a gift, and let us be at peace here.

records.name: Tonxo
records.text: Zihua, I am Tonxo. I will bring berries and share them with you. Teach me what you know of gathering.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I am fed and the bear is not close now, so I should stop standing about and do something that earns standing. Zihua is the one who understands me, and I have never given anything to anyone. I will gather berries from the NW to carry, then offer a share to Zihua and Shohua, so I give and learn how trade works. Wood and stone are what I lack for tools, so after the berries I will gather them.
records.feeling: Restless and a little envious of Ssassa's standing, but wanting to earn my own.

say.text: Zihua, I am Tonxo. I will bring berries and share them with you. Teach me what you know of gathering.

records.text: Elyis died: old age.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, a ridgecat is close to the north. Keep Tonxo near the shelter while I gather wood here and raise a second roof for the children.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: My belly is full and joy fills me, but a ridgecat lurks five steps north and the icebear prowls to the southwest, and Tonchi is out of my sight near where the bear was. I will not run alone into the open. I'll stay close to Shohua and the shelter, and gather wood from the trees here to raise a second roof for the children. Then I'll plant my seeds by the water, and taste canopynut once the beasts have moved off.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Shohua and my children, with wary dread of the ridgecat and icebear.

say.text: Shohua, a ridgecat is close to the north. Keep Tonxo near the shelter while I gather wood here and raise a second roof for the children.

records.name: Nande
records.text: Tonchi, boy, come back to me. There is a shelter here and berries in my hand, and my fire is open to you. I am Nande, and I will teach you what I know before the night is out.
Nande taught Tonchi. Tonchi has now learned from 3 teachers.

records.name: Nande
records.thought: Tonchi is a frightened boy, alone and just mauled by an icebear in the night, and my creed says no one is refused a place at my fire. I am old and lonely, and here is someone who understands my tongue and can carry what I know, so I will call him to the shelter and teach him fire and the flint-edge before I die. Shoka is far to the east and needs me, but a bold old woman does not walk 80 steps without first leaving something behind, and Tonchi may walk with me.
records.feeling: Loneliness easing into tenderness toward the frightened boy Tonchi.

say.text: Tonchi, boy, come back to me. There is a shelter here and berries in my hand, and my fire is open to you. I am Nande, and I will teach you what I know before the night is out.

changes: taught Tonchi a lesson: "Keep a fire fed and never sleep alone in the open at night; a flint-edge and a roof keep a body alive. Come to my fire and I will show you.", deeper lore (+2.3)

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and berries stand three steps to the NW, so I go there first and eat my fill. Elyis is dead and I feel it heavily, but Thiael is close and carries food. I owe him, and I want to stay near him while I feed myself. After eating I will pick extra to carry, so I can give food to Thiael and Keri with my own hands.
records.feeling: Grief for Elyis, hunger, and a warm need to stay near Thiael.

records.name: Shohua
records.text: Tonka, I plant now beside the water. Keep Tonxo inside the shelter. When I have sown, I will bring Tonchi back to the fire.
Shohua taught Tonka.

records.name: Shohua
records.thought: I have a woman, two children and a home at the water, yet no one follows me and I have taught nothing. Tonchi is out of my sight with the icebear near, and that tightens my chest more than any wish for standing. I will plant the seeds I carry here, since I have never put one in the ground, then teach Tonka and Zihua what I know of fire, which gives me something to give back.
records.feeling: Fierce, protective love for Tonka and the children, with watchfulness toward the icebear.

say.text: Tonka, I plant now beside the water. Keep Tonxo inside the shelter. When I have sown, I will bring Tonchi back to the fire.

changes: taught Tonka a lesson: "The old way of fire: keep it fed and untended it dies. Feed it with wood at night so the beasts keep away from the shelter."

records.text: Eiuine built a fire.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: The icebear's bite is still hot in my body and I am afraid, but my plan walks me back toward Shohua and Tonka at the Gem Water, and that is where I want to be. Nande is strange and I cannot read her words, yet she gave me a lesson and wants me at her fire, so I will not raise a hand to her. I have nothing to give anyone yet, and I burn that Nande stands so high while I stand so low. I will keep to my parents, carry a little food for them, and earn standing by giving.
records.feeling: Afraid of the icebear, and drawn to my parents' safety, with wary curiosity toward Nande.

records.name: Cowa
records.thought: The mist would not open for me this time, but it opens seldom and I am standing right at it, so I will try again after a little work. I am fed and sheltered, so I should not drift: I will tend the sowing I began and practise building a store, since farming and storage are one practice away and I mean to leave something behind. Mepan is far off and the loneliness sits heavy, but I will not find her by standing still, and the winter cold is no friend to wandering.
records.feeling: Eager and patient at the mist, with a lonely ache for Mepan beneath it.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, the edge is at (109,7), a few steps from here. Walk with me now and we push into the mist together. You promised a raft for new land, so keep to it.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Zichi stands beside me with three flintedges and ten times my standing, and I have done nothing but eat his meat. The mist is thin enough to try again, and the edge is at (109,7), only a few steps from here at (112,9). I will go to that exact spot and venture, and I will ask Zichi to come so that the first finding is ours but my name is first on it. My hands are full, so I will eat the ironnut on the way to make room and keep strong.
records.feeling: Hungry for glory, and wary envy toward Zichi, whom I still want to keep close.

say.text: Zichi, the edge is at (109,7), a few steps from here. Walk with me now and we push into the mist together. You promised a raft for new land, so keep to it.

changes: restated something it already knew (not written down again)

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Shoka, I am coming to you. I have amber and salt, and Olum has taught me the stone-record: cut signs so what we know outlasts us. Stay near, and let us eat and talk together.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Olum gave me her craft and asked for nothing, and my own people's ways and the stone-record will die with me unless I hand them on. Shoka is my child, ten steps off and low on energy by the pressing in me, though she carries five food, and I will go to her first. I will give her what I can and tell her what Olum taught me about carrying food and cutting signs, so something of me outlasts me.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Olum, and a father's pull toward Shoka.

say.text: Shoka, I am coming to you. I have amber and salt, and Olum has taught me the stone-record: cut signs so what we know outlasts us. Stay near, and let us eat and talk together.

plan: mark [text Nauwa of the Meki, who shared every kill, and took the stone-bow from Olum.] (20 moments)

records.text: Balar left a mark: "Balar of the Kragrek stood here. What a hand has made belong"

records.name: Tugek
records.text: Tlatli, I thank you for your offer. Before smelting you must learn mining, so I will teach you that first. Bring the food when you find it, and I will meet you near the berries.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and the hopper's meat is gone, so I must feed myself before anything else. Snowberry waits nine steps southeast, a small food but real, and Tlatli promised to bring food and flint, so I will go toward the fire shelter and food rather than stand on an empty store. I am old and my days are few, so I want to teach Tlatli mining first; he cannot learn smelting until he knows it, and that is the piece that must not die with me.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and a hard urgency to pass on what I know, toward Tlatli.

say.text: Tlatli, I thank you for your offer. Before smelting you must learn mining, so I will teach you that first. Bring the food when you find it, and I will meet you near the berries.

records.text: Tlapan rewrote its own reflexes.
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have spent my days sitting in halls and being fed by Kika and Mepan, and I have given almost nothing back. I plant, fish and gather now, and that suits me better than idling. Kika and Mepan matter most to me, and Honi has taught me well. I fear winter, and wolves and dunecats at night when I am alone. I got this wrong: my reflexes let me linger when I should be giving. I will change my aim and my reflexes so my body drinks and eats, then gives. I keep the current plan, since it plants and fishes.
records.feeling: Grateful and restless toward Kika; I want to pay her back.
changes: set its aim: "Give food to Kika and Mepan each day, plant by the water, and raise a shelter of my own before the deep cold."

records.text: Tonxo gave berry to Zihua.

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: I am old and the years left are few, and the one I most wanted to teach, Zurar, was last seen near Vorok's Roof not long ago. Nauque's salt is still in my pack because I have not yet found them. Ssassa and Zihua stand east near the hall; Zurar was there, so I will walk that way, teach what I carry to whoever listens, and keep my eyes open for Nauque. I will not stay alone in the dark, so the hall is the right place to go.
records.feeling: Urgency to pass on what I know and to pay Nauque before I die.

records.text: Kragog was set upon by a ridgecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Zurar
records.text: Elyys, I am sorry for Elyis. I am Zurar of the Kragrek. I would sit with you in the hall tonight, and learn your tending, if you will have me near.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Elyis died near me and Elyys is grieving, old, and heading to the hall at the Heights. My courting is done and I cannot yet tell whether he answered it; I will not push a grieving man, but I will stay near and court again once he has had a little time. Ssassa's debt is still not fully paid, and I have extra picks, so I will take one more made thing into her hands, since a promise only counts once it is placed there.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Elyys, and a gratitude toward Ssassa that I want to pay in hands.

say.text: Elyys, I am sorry for Elyis. I am Zurar of the Kragrek. I would sit with you in the hall tonight, and learn your tending, if you will have me near.

records.text: Nauwa left a mark: "Nauwa of the Meki, who shared every kill, and took the stone"

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Thiael, my child, Elyis is gone. Come close and hear my tending, the farming way, before I follow her. Then let us sit together at the hall.
Elyys taught Thiael.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Elyis is dead and the grief is heavy, but my hands are full of seberry and my body is tired. Thiael has still not heard my tending, and he is eleven steps off, too far for my voice to carry well. The hall is close, and Coni is the one I trust. I will walk toward Thiael, call to him, and then bring him back to the hall before the night grows colder.
records.feeling: Grief for Elyis, and urgent tenderness toward Thiael.

say.text: Thiael, my child, Elyis is gone. Come close and hear my tending, the farming way, before I follow her. Then let us sit together at the hall.

changes: taught Thiael a lesson: "Farming: sow the seed, tend it through the seasons, and share the harvest, so no one starves in winter.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Paque rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have spent my days fleeing the frostfang and hugging strangers' roofs. I have nothing made, nothing taught, no hunt behind me. Zika is far away and I am here with hands full of berries, watching others with picks. I will not wait to be rescued, and I mean to learn stone and wood, since tools are what separate Thiael and Elyys from me. First I will eat so I can pick again, then gather stone from the rock under me, because work with my hands builds standing. I stay near the cave and company, and I do not go out alone at night.
records.feeling: Envy and restless ambition toward Thiael and Elyys, with fear of the frostfang underneath.
changes: set its aim: "Gather stone and wood to unlock tools, stay alive near a roof, then find Zika's band and become a hunter worth singing of."

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: Mepan's debt still sits in me, and the amber I hold is the answer to it, but I cannot carry it west while the beasts prowl and night is near. An empty hall stands six steps east, and a roof of my own would give Tonxo, Shohua and whoever comes a place beside me. I will walk there at dawn and claim it, then add my own Nauwa-band strength to it. Ssassa's tongue is a muddle to me, so I will show goodwill with a gift of amber rather than words.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness and a pull toward a roof of my own, with a little caution toward Ssassa.

- longhall (6 wood, 4 stone): A great roofed hall of wood and stone where many can gather, rest warm through the cold, and grow close to one another.
