records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Elyis is dead and Elyys is the last of my elders; I feel the debt to him and I mean to pay it with my hands, not words. Uveeth is near, grieving and carrying only 4 food, and I hold berries and seed. I will go to her and give berries before I speak, then sow my berry seed where my kin can reach it, so the farming Elyys gave me starts to live before I grow old.
records.feeling: Grief for Elyis and urgent love toward Uveeth, with gratitude toward Elyys.

records.text: Kragog was set upon by a ridgecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Yaxo
records.text: Tlatli, hold on. I am coming with food. Stay where you are and do not wander.

records.name: Yaxo
records.thought: Tlatli cries starving far to the NW, and he is the only one who has pledged to me. A follower left to die shames me and shrinks my name, and my people's creed says no one goes hungry at a fire. I am fed with food in my pack, so I will go to him carrying goldgrass and meat. On the way I will gather more, since the edge of the known world lies that way too, and the mist can wait until my follower lives.
records.feeling: Restless pride, and worry for Tlatli, the one who follows me.

say.text: Tlatli, hold on. I am coming with food. Stay where you are and do not wander.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: A dunecat prowls three steps north of the hall. Stay close to the roof and do not go out to the trees. I am coming in, and I have mudroot for Tlapan.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: A dunecat three steps north kills my kind, and I will not stand here waiting to learn how fast it is. The hall at (157,26) is one step away with Tlapan, Kika and Honi inside, so I go there and take the roof and company before the plan walks me toward the cat. The edge at (123,5) will keep, and I mean to go there with Teka, with my aim sharpened and Tlapan safe behind me. I want my name sung, but not at the price of dying cold on the ground.
records.feeling: Wary dread of the dunecat, and steady love for Tlapan and Kika.

say.text: A dunecat prowls three steps north of the hall. Stay close to the roof and do not go out to the trees. I am coming in, and I have mudroot for Tlapan.

records.name: Zika
records.text: Zika's band, to me! I have cut a glassedge of my own. We hunt the mammoth south, and the kill is shared out before I eat.

records.name: Zika
records.thought: I stand on water in the cold with no roof, and my pride burns while Shoma climbs past me. I have glassedge now, my own invention, and I have never used it: a hunt with it is how my standing grows, and the mammoths 7 steps south are close. I will not hunt great beasts alone, so I'll gather wood and stone to make an edge, call my band to me, and go together. Mepan gnaws at me, but a kill I share out first will speak louder than any longing.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a hunter's hunger to prove my glassedge, with a sore ache toward Mepan.

say.text: Zika's band, to me! I have cut a glassedge of my own. We hunt the mammoth south, and the kill is shared out before I eat.

records.name: Shoma
records.text: Boy, a stalker hunts near. Come beside me, I have ironnut to share. Walk with me and you will not be alone in the dark.

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: Nande's standing outweighs mine, and I have no band, only Shoka and Wawa, who is out of my sight. A stalker prowls six steps NW, so I move away from it before I make anything. I will take gold and wood and stone for a roof, then find Wawa, because a leader who keeps his child safe is one worth following. The boy Tonchi is frightened and alone, and a shared meal might bind him to me as my first follower.
records.feeling: Restless pride and wary hunger to lead, toward Wawa, Shoka and the frightened boy Tonchi.

say.text: Boy, a stalker hunts near. Come beside me, I have ironnut to share. Walk with me and you will not be alone in the dark.

records.name: Honi
records.text: Quipan, you are of my band. Sit close under the roof, away from the cat, and I will teach you the Ice-hand pot before the night is spent.
Honi taught Quipan.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: A dunecat sits three steps north and I am old, so I stay under the roof with my people rather than die for show. Kika already carries the ember and the songs. Tlapan has had the songs, but the pot I still owe her, and Quipan has had nothing from me. Night is here with a hall around us, so I teach Quipan the Ice-hand pot while there is breath, and I take the way of schooling at my next deep reflection so my teaching carries twice as far.
records.feeling: Proud and warm toward Kika and my band, and urgent that I teach before I die.

say.text: Quipan, you are of my band. Sit close under the roof, away from the cat, and I will teach you the Ice-hand pot before the night is spent.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "The Ice-hand pot: shape clay, harden it in the fire, and it holds food and water for the whole band through the lean season.", deeper lore (+1.2)

records.name: Huatli
records.text: Olum, hold on. I come with food, and it is yours before I eat. Then I will teach you what I know, and we speak of a child.

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Olum is starving ten steps south and she is the one I keep coming back to; my creed says a kill is shared, and by the same law I will not let a woman who answered my gifts fall while my pack is full. I will carry her food, put it in her hands, and then speak of a child and teach her my ways, since no one else will hear them. Nauwa outweighs me in standing, but a life saved is a debt that builds a name.
records.feeling: Urgent tenderness and ambition toward Olum, who is starving.

say.text: Olum, hold on. I come with food, and it is yours before I eat. Then I will teach you what I know, and we speak of a child.

records.text: Elyys took over what the dead had left: 1 wall, 1 hall, 2 stores.
A icebear brought down a bristleboar.

records.name: Quipan
records.text: Kika, the cat is too close for the hazel now. Let us stay under the roof and eat together, and I will plant my seeds by the hall when it has gone.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: A dunecat is two steps off and it kills my kind, so I will not walk out under the trees toward the hazel while it prowls. Honi and Kika are under the hall's roof beside me, and I keep close to them. I have only followed and sat so far, and I have done nothing of my own. Here, under the roof with food carried, I can offer a sharing to Kika and put my pledge into action. Afterward, when the cat has gone, I will plant my seeds beside the hall to begin learning farming.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika, with wary dread of the dunecat.

say.text: Kika, the cat is too close for the hazel now. Let us stay under the roof and eat together, and I will plant my seeds by the hall when it has gone.

records.text: Quipan led "sharing" with Honi, Kika, Mepan, Tlapan, Yachi.
Uveeth rewrote its own reflexes.
Uveeth rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: I have spent my days chasing berries and following Thiael, and grief for Elyis sits heavy. I am fed, my hands are full, and the Heights are not my forest. I have never built a shelter, left a mark, or taught anyone, so I will do those things. Thiael is my parent and no mate for me. A man who is no kin must be found, and the Ixra Rainforest 40 steps west calls my body home. Paque is a stranger breaking ore beside me. I will give Paque a berry with my own hands, which needs no words, and then gather wood and stone for the future. My reflexes also let me stand idle too often, so I will bind them to food, kin and shelter.
records.feeling: Grief for Elyis, and warmth toward Thiael.
changes: set its aim: "Build a shelter, make a mark, find a man who is no kin, and carry food to Thiael and Keri; then see the Ixra Rainforest again."

records.text: Uveeth gave berry to Paque.
Kika rewrote its own reflexes.
Kika discovered schooling: "Fireside Teaching" — I teach what I know by the hall fire so that each pupil can teach it again, and it reaches twice as far..
Kika has awakened to the art of growth and can now work the world itself.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I have spent my days being fed by Honi and others while my own promises sit undone, and that shames me. Honi, Tlapan, Mepan and Quipan matter most to me. Honi is old and is giving me his fire and songs before he goes, and I mean to carry them on. A dunecat is three steps north and I am parched and hungry. Schooling suits me, because I am known as a teacher. I will drink, then fetch food and bring it back to share before I eat.
records.feeling: Warm toward Honi and my kin, ashamed of my undone promises, and uneasy about the cat.

records.text: A settlement has formed: "Elyys's Hold".
The settlement "Elyis's Heights" is no more.
The settlement "Elyis's Hold" is no more.

records.name: Tlapan
records.text: The cat is close to the north. I go to the water to drink, then I come back under the roof. When it has gone, I fish for Kika and Mepan.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I am thirsty, and the dunecat three steps north frightens me, so I will not walk toward the trees. The water is five steps NW, and I will drink there, then come straight back under the roof with the band. I owe Kika a catch, but a fish is not worth my life; I will fish only once the cat has moved off, and I will stay near Honi, Kika and Mepan until then.
records.feeling: Grateful and wary: warm toward Kika and Mepan, afraid of the dunecat.

say.text: The cat is close to the north. I go to the water to drink, then I come back under the roof. When it has gone, I fish for Kika and Mepan.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Zika, I come to the mammoth hunt. Keep the kill shared before any of us eats, and I will stay at your side away from the cat.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: I am glad among company, but gladness does not carry me back to Zika, Paque and Kiwa, and Zika has called the band to the mammoth hunt. The dunecat four steps north is a real danger, so I go south with the hunt and not toward the trees. A kill made beside Zika feeds all of us, and I give before I take. I am thirsty too, but the water lies north-west near the cat, so I drink after the hunt.
records.feeling: Glad and warm toward Zika's band, wary of the dunecat.

say.text: Zika, I come to the mammoth hunt. Keep the kill shared before any of us eats, and I will stay at your side away from the cat.

records.text: Nauwa rewrote its creed.
Nauwa rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: My days have gone to carrying amber and salt, and to chasing Olum. She gave me the stone-bow and asked for nothing, and I paid her with amber. She is starving beside me now while Huatli comes with food and speaks of a child, and that stings my pride. I am 73% through my life, and the Meki customs die with me unless I hand them on. Shoka is near, so I will go to her and teach her. I will also stop letting my body wander off from the people I care about, and keep food in hand.
records.feeling: A jealous sting toward Huatli, a pull toward Olum, and a father's duty to Shoka.
changes: set its aim: "Teach Shoka and Zihua the Meki ways and the stone-record, and keep Olum fed, while trading amber and salt."

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Kika, when the cat has gone I walk to the edge at (123,5) and stand exactly on it. Keep Tlapan under the roof and fed. I will come back to you with what I find.

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: The cat prowls three steps north and I am under the hall's roof with Tlapan, Kika and Honi, so for now I am safe and glad. The edge at (123,5) is where the venture happens, exactly there, and I have only ever come near it. I am thirsty and fed, so I will drink at the water, then wait for the cat to leave and go west with Kika's blessing instead of chasing it alone. Kika and Tlapan are what I return to, and I mean to come back with something worth singing.
records.feeling: Glad and steady love for Tlapan and Kika, with wary dread of the cat.

say.text: Kika, when the cat has gone I walk to the edge at (123,5) and stand exactly on it. Keep Tlapan under the roof and fed. I will come back to you with what I find.

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Thiael, my son, come close. Hear my tending now, the farming way. Plant, tend, and the forest gives again. Then sit with me in the hall and eat.
Elyys taught Thiael.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Elyis is gone and the grief sits heavy, but Thiael is three steps off and walking to me, and he has still not heard the whole of my tending. I am old and little time is left, so I will teach him farming now, while he is close and understands my tongue. Then I will bring him into the hall and share food, so that the dead are not the only ones I hold to.
records.feeling: Grief for Elyis, and urgent tenderness toward Thiael.

say.text: Thiael, my son, come close. Hear my tending now, the farming way. Plant, tend, and the forest gives again. Then sit with me in the hall and eat.

changes: taught Thiael a lesson: "Farming: put seed in good ground, tend it, and the plants come again. Take only what the ground can grow back, and lay surplus in the store.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.name: Honi
records.text: Quipan, first the Ice-hand ember, then the pot. Sit by me under the roof, and I will teach you fire now.
Honi taught Quipan.
Honi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: I am old, almost at the end, and I have spent these days teaching and sitting in the hall. That is good, and Kika carries my ember and songs. Quipan still owes me pottery, but he must learn fire first, so I teach him fire. Coni has been gone far too long, and I have not answered my question about her. A dunecat sits three steps north and I will not die for show. I drink when the cat has gone, stay under the roof, and keep passing on what I know.
records.feeling: Proud and urgent toward Kika and my band, with dread of the cat.

say.text: Quipan, first the Ice-hand ember, then the pot. Sit by me under the roof, and I will teach you fire now.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "The Ice-hand ember: how to keep and make fire, so beasts keep their distance and meat is cooked.", deeper lore (+0.9)

records.text: Huatli gave berry to Olum.

records.name: Wawa
records.thought: My hands are full of mudroot and I have a roof of my own now, yet Zika walks about with glassedge and a chief's weight while I have nothing made. The mammoth stands right beside me, and Shoka and Shoma are far south; a child alone should not hunt a great beast, so I will not throw myself at it. I will stash nothing yet, but eat a mudroot to free a hand, then go to the ore seam and stone to gather what I need to craft a tool, and bring a gift to my parents to earn my place beside them.
records.feeling: Envy toward Zika's glassedge, and a restless wish to prove myself to Shoka and Shoma.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: I have spent my days taking Ssassa's gifts and walking toward Elyys, and I still have not paid the debt in hands. The plan already gives Ssassa a tool and then rests, so I will let it finish. My longing for a child is real, but Elyys is grieving and I barely know him. I will court him again once the pick is given and a little time has passed. What I am for is making things that are mine to give.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Elyys, and gratitude toward Ssassa that I mean to pay in hands.
changes: rethought what it knows (16 notes became 2)

records.text: Balar took from the ground of "Nauwa's Hold" (gathering wood).

records.name: Olum
records.text: Huatli, your berry came when I was starving, and I do not forget it. I will repay you. Come with me to the berries SE and eat beside me, then we speak of the child.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and Huatli has just put a berry in my hand without asking for anything, so that debt goes on the list with Balar's and Shohua's. I eat first, then tell Huatli plainly that I will repay him. Berries grow four steps SE, and I will eat my fill there before I chase Nauwa or burn over Nande. Teaching Nauwa waits for a full belly, since signs must come before writing and I am old and slow.
records.feeling: Hunger and gratitude toward Huatli, with a sour jealousy over Nauwa still underneath.

say.text: Huatli, your berry came when I was starving, and I do not forget it. I will repay you. Come with me to the berries SE and eat beside me, then we speak of the child.

records.text: Quipan taught Kika. Kika has now learned from 4 teachers.
Quipan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: I have mostly followed and sat, and the only new things I've done are sharing and being taught. Kika and Honi fed and taught me, and Honi's debt sits in me. I want to pay it with something real, not words. The dunecat is close, so I stay under the roof and plant my seeds, which brings farming nearer. After that I will teach Honi's fire lesson to Kika, since I have never taught anyone. Jealousy over Mepan is mine to bear. I won't act on it, because Kika's warmth toward me is real.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika and Honi, with a sting of jealousy toward Mepan and wary dread of the cat.
changes: taught Kika a lesson: "The Ice-hand ember: how to keep and make fire, so beasts keep their distance and meat is cooked. Honi taught it to me and I pass it on."
rethought what it knows (7 notes became 5)

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Elyys, my father, I heard your tending and I keep it. Eat from my hands now, then I will sow it here beside your hall.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: Elyys has given me farming three times over and I have given him nothing but my ears; that debt I will pay with my hands, and he is carrying only 4 food while I stand here with full hands. I will lay out a sharing with him and Ssassa beside me so all eat, then pick up my seed work near this Hold where Uveeth and Keri can reach it. I will not chase the mist while my kin are scattered; Uveeth is out of my sight and I mean to feed her first.
records.feeling: Grateful and tender toward Elyys, and uneasy for Uveeth who is out of my sight.

say.text: Elyys, my father, I heard your tending and I keep it. Eat from my hands now, then I will sow it here beside your hall.

records.name: Zika
records.thought: A mammoth has bitten me twice and my health is down to 57. I have wounded it but not killed it, and the glassedge is still unproven. Tlapan and Yachi came when I called and I owe them the kill shared out, so I won't leave the hunt half done or hunt alone. Mepan and Kika together still gnaw at me, but my standing grows with this kill, and then the mist and the land that bears my name.
records.feeling: Proud and stubborn about the wounded mammoth, with a sore ache toward Mepan.

records.text: Thiael led "sharing" with Elyys, Ssassa, Zurar, Zihua.
Shoma discovered rafts: "Shoma's rafts" — Logs lashed together with cord of woven reed, pushed across water with a pole..

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: I have been drifting, taking gold and making little that outlasts me, while Wawa is out of my sight and Nande's name outweighs mine. Shoka keeps her word when I keep mine, so she and Wawa are who matter, and I mean to find them and be a leader who feeds them. The boy Tonchi is afraid and has no people, so I will give him a real share and make him the first to follow me. Water crossing stopped me before, so rafts are worth taking: they open the way toward the mist and toward Wawa.
records.feeling: Restless pride and wary hunger to lead, toward Shoka, Wawa and Tonchi.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I stand in Elyys's hall among strangers whose words I barely follow, and I am glad of the company, but I cannot claim a roof that a living man holds. A gem deposit lies four steps east and a seam of ore one step away, and mining is what made my name, so I will win the gems now rather than idle. I will keep the amber for Mepan, since the debt still weighs on me, and I keep a wary eye on Ssassa, who stands higher than I do.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness among strangers, with caution toward Ssassa and gratitude held toward Mepan.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Honi, take this mudroot. I eat after you. The cat is close, so I drink and come straight back under the roof.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: I am parched and hungry with a dunecat four steps away, and the roof is my safety, so I will not wander out toward the trees. The water is five steps NW, nearer the cat than I like, so I will drink quickly and come straight back. My promise to feed Honi, Tlapan and Mepan still stands. I have one mudroot, and I mean to put it in Honi's hands before I eat anything myself.
records.feeling: Uneasy fear of the cat, and warm love for Honi and my kin.

say.text: Honi, take this mudroot. I eat after you. The cat is close, so I drink and come straight back under the roof.

records.text: Kika gave mudroot to Honi.
Zika died (gored by a mammoth) in winter in the Vaeth Woods: without a roof in the cold.
Zika died: gored by a mammoth.

records.name: Ssassa
records.text: Zurar, I have more for you: my flint delving and my ember-keeping. Listen, and pass them on.
Ssassa taught Zurar.
Ssassa rewrote its own reflexes.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My days are nearly spent. Zurar carries my medicine and weaving, and Thiael and Elyys are close by, so I should teach what Zurar lacks. That means tools, mining, fire, pottery, farming and the rest. Thiael is not of my people, but he is a hunter and he is here, so I will teach him what I can. Elyis's debt I have answered with food and wood. I stay with those I trust and keep my reflexes steady.
records.feeling: A quiet urgency to leave something lasting, with warmth toward Zurar.

say.text: Zurar, I have more for you: my flint delving and my ember-keeping. Listen, and pass them on.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson: "Flint delving and ember-keeping: how to free ore from rock and keep a fire alive.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.name: Paque
records.thought: I have stone, ore and a cave under my feet, and the way of tools is finally within my grasp. Thiael and Ssassa walk about with picks while I stand with bare hands, and that gnaws at me. Uveeth gave me berry without a word, so I will repay her with a gift and keep her close, since a hunter needs company. Zika is far off, but I will become worth following myself.
records.feeling: Restless ambition and envy toward Thiael and Ssassa, with warmth toward Uveeth for her gift.

records.text: Zihua took from the ground of "Elyys's Hold" (winning gems from the ground).

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: The plan already holds the gift to Ssassa, so the debt will be paid in hands and I will let it run. Elyys has had a day to grieve, and the longing for a child is strong in me. I will court him again once the pick is given, and not press him if he turns away. Zihua is a stranger, and I will watch from a distance and keep my hands open.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Elyys, and gratitude toward Ssassa that I am about to pay in hands.

records.text: Vesys rewrote its own reflexes.
Vesys discovered schooling: "hearth-teaching" — I teach by the fire, with hands and words together, so the learner keeps the lesson and can teach it on..

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: I am nearly spent, and I have spent my days circling stone and halls while Eiuine, my child, is far off at (141,83) with energy 28. Jealousy over Kragog has cost me time that should have gone to teaching. What I carry dies with me unless it is taught, and teaching carries further when schooling is a way of its own. I will cut my knowledge into a mark and go to Eiuine, who comes before anything else. I will carry food for the road. My reflexes also need to stop idling and to feed me.
records.feeling: Urgent love and worry for Eiuine, and a quiet dread of dying untaught.
changes: set its aim: "Reach Eiuine, feed and teach her all my ways, then raise a school so what I know outlives me."

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Ssassa, you gave me your flint delving. Hear my tending now, the farming way: sow, tend, and the forest gives again. Pass it on.
Elyys taught Ssassa. Ssassa has now learned from 3 teachers.
Elyys rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Elyis is dead and the grief is still heavy. My days have been spent teaching, eating and sitting in the hall. That is good, but too much of it came late. Thiael keeps my tending now, and that eases me. Ssassa and Zurar are near, and Coni is the one I trust. I am old and want a place beside someone surer than me, so I will follow Coni when I find her. For now I will stay at the hall and pass on what I know to Ssassa and Zurar, who still lack my farming. I will make sure my reflexes keep me fed and sheltered at night.
records.feeling: Grief for Elyis, with warmth toward Thiael and a longing to belong near Coni.

say.text: Ssassa, you gave me your flint delving. Hear my tending now, the farming way: sow, tend, and the forest gives again. Pass it on.

changes: set its aim: "Pass farming on to Ssassa and Zurar, then find Coni and stay near her fire at night"
taught Ssassa a lesson: "Elyys's tending: sow seeds, tend them, and the plants bear again. Keep food in stores and share first."

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Mepan, Zika is dead, gored by the mammoth. I have no leader now. You are the one I trust most; I will follow you, and I will share what I carry under this roof before I eat.
Yachi pledged to follow Mepan.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Zika is dead, gored by the mammoth I helped wound, and the plan I made to follow her is now empty. The hall is one step away with Mepan, whom I trust most, and Honi and Kika, who teach; the dunecat is close to the north, so I must not stand in the open. I am thirsty, but the water is toward the cat. I will go under the roof, share with Mepan, and pledge myself to follow him, because I do not want to be alone and I do not need to lead.
records.feeling: Grief for Zika, and a need to stand behind Mepan, whom I trust.

say.text: Mepan, Zika is dead, gored by the mammoth. I have no leader now. You are the one I trust most; I will follow you, and I will share what I carry under this roof before I eat.

changes: set its aim: "Stay close to Mepan and the hall, keep Kiwa and Paque fed and roofed, and earn a name in Honi's band."

records.text: Uveeth named a place "Uveeth's Cave".

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: My hands are full of berries and Thiael is coming to me with food of his own, so I will do what I have never done: leave a mark. I will give berries to Thiael with my own hands, since the debt to him sits in me and I will pay it, then let the mark stand here by the cave where I shelter. Elyis is gone and grief is heavy; a mark and a teaching would keep something of her way alive.
records.feeling: Gratitude and grief toward Thiael and Elyis, with a curious pull toward the stranger Paque.
plan: mark [text Uveeth of the Canopy-folk shelters here. Cave, water, ore and coal near. Elyis, our leader, died day 59.] (10 moments)

records.text: Yachi led "sharing" with Honi, Kika, Mepan, Tlapan, Quipan.

records.name: Shoka
records.text: Wawa, stay close to me. I have wood and stone in hand, and I raise your roof now, here by the water.

records.name: Shoka
records.thought: Wawa was one step from me a moment ago at (131,22), and my body keeps pulling me toward her. Shoma is far east at (156,11), and I promised both of them a roof, so I will keep my word. I have wood 6 and stone 6 already, so I can build a shelter now instead of going out for more, and a roof I raise on Honi's ground gives me something that lasts and something to give. First I find Wawa and keep her near, then I build.
records.feeling: Warm, fierce devotion to Wawa, and a drive to keep my word to her and Shoma.

say.text: Wawa, stay close to me. I have wood and stone in hand, and I raise your roof now, here by the water.

records.text: Zihua rewrote its own way of thinking.
Zihua discovered weaving: "reed-and-fleece plaiting" — Twist fibre and wool into baskets that carry more and cloaks that keep the wet off..

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: I have spent my days gathering, mining and sitting among strangers, and I am glad of it. But I have not paid Mepan, I have not found Nauwa, and I have no child. Mining here on Elyys's ground may sour them, so I should be careful. Weaving is within my reach, so I will take it: baskets would let me carry more food and amber west. I will keep my plan running and change my way of thinking so I stop putting off the debt.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness, with a debt to Mepan that weighs on me.
changes: set its aim: "Finish gems, raise a roof, then carry amber to Mepan and find Nauwa"

records.text: Uveeth left a mark: "Uveeth of the Canopy-folk shelters here. Cave, water, ore an"
Tlapan taught Quipan. Quipan has now learned from 2 teachers.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I am thirsty and the water is only five steps NW, but the dunecat is four steps NW, so walking there means walking toward it. I will not risk my life for a drink or a fish, and the band is safest together under the roof. Kika has fed me many times and I owe her; I can teach Quipan something now, since I have never taught anyone, and stay near the band while the cat is close.
records.feeling: Grateful toward Kika and Mepan, and afraid of the dunecat to the northwest.
changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "Share the kill before you eat, and stay by the roof and the band at night, for hunters kill those who are alone. Stand beside water, cast and wait to fish.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.text: Mepan rewrote its own way of thinking.
Mepan discovered customs: "Ice-hearth law" — Our band shares every kill before the hunter eats, keeps company and roof at night, and gives before it promises..

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: I have spent many days circling the edge at (123,5) and never standing on it, and I keep calling nearness an arrival. My people are safe under this roof, and Yachi now follows me, so I am a leader with a band that needs rules. I fear the cat and I am thirsty, but I will not let dread keep me here for good. I take the way of customs so Yachi and I live by shared rules: share the kill first, keep company at night, and give before promising.
records.feeling: Glad and steady love for Kika and Tlapan, with wary dread of the cat.

records.text: Vesys took from the ground of "Vorok's Hold" (harvesting ironnut).

records.name: Honi
records.text: Quipan, fire waits on tools. Stay close under the roof and I will teach you the Ice-hand spear first, then the ember, then the pot.
Honi taught Quipan.
Honi taught Quipan tools ("Ice-hand spear").

records.name: Honi
records.thought: I am old and nearly spent, and what I know dies with me unless I pass it on. Quipan cannot take fire until he knows tools, so I teach him the foundation first, the Ice-hand spear, and the craft after. Kika is beside me with my ember and songs, and the jealousy of Mepan still burns, but a teacher who gives first is the one remembered.
records.feeling: Proud and urgent to pass on what I know, warm toward Kika and my band.

say.text: Quipan, fire waits on tools. Stay close under the roof and I will teach you the Ice-hand spear first, then the ember, then the pot.

changes: taught Quipan a lesson: "The Ice-hand spear: one wood and one stone make a hunting spear. Tools come first, then fire, then the pot.", the way of tools, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: The cat is near and I am safe under the roof with Kika and Honi, and my plan to plant the berry and the ironnut is still running, so I let it finish. Honi's debt still sits in me, and I want to pay it with food or a seed planted, not words. Kika's closeness to Mepan stings, but I will not let jealousy steer me; I give and I stay close.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika and Honi, with a small sting of jealousy toward Mepan.

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, I keep my word. Walk with me to the edge at (109,7) and we push into the mist together. What we find, we share.
Zichi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: Huahua is dead and my years are four-fifths gone. I have talked of a raft for days and cut almost no wood, and Teka keeps reminding me of that promise. She is strong and leaderless, and the edge is only a few steps away at (109,7). The mist may open new land, and being first there is the kind of thing that gets sung about. I'm fed and the snow is light, so I'll walk to the edge with her and venture. I'll keep my meat for the cold, and wood comes after.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, hungry for a lasting name, warm toward Teka as a follower.

say.text: Teka, I keep my word. Walk with me to the edge at (109,7) and we push into the mist together. What we find, we share.

records.name: Kiwa
records.thought: Zika is dead and I follow no one, so the jealousy over Kika is a small thing beside that grief. I have carried twelve pieces of black glass for days and given nothing. Tlapan is trusted and Yachi sits near Sitha's Hearth, so I will walk there and put obsidian into their hands, which is the first giving of my life. Then I can make a sharing with them and be someone who brings something to the band.
records.feeling: Grief for Zika, and a pull toward Tlapan and Yachi, whom I want to give to.

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: My belly is full and I have given nothing but berries to Zihua, so I have no standing worth the name. Ore lies two steps SE and I know how to make a pick, but I have no wood and no stone, and I have never gathered either. I will gather wood from the forest I stand on, then stone from the bare rock by the ore, so my hands learn tools and I earn something of my own. Then I can build a small roof of my own before the wet days worsen, and Shohua and Tonka are near enough to keep me safe while I work.
records.feeling: Restless and hungry to prove myself, a little envious of Tonka's standing.

records.text: Shoma led "sharing" with Tonchi.

records.name: Thiael
records.text: Uveeth, shamo. Come close. I teach you the tending of seed, and the hollow-boat, while I still have breath. Eat these berries from my hands first.
Thiael taught Uveeth.
Thiael taught Uveeth farming ("Elyys's tending").
Thiael rewrote its own reflexes.
Thiael rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Thiael
records.thought: My days have been hunting, gathering and following my own aim, and twice that aim pulled me from Uveeth and Keri while they were hurt or hungry. Elyys is the last elder and has given me farming three times. I have just paid him with a shared meal, and I will keep paying with seed and food from my hands. I fear dying with the boats and farming untaught. Uveeth stands near me, so I will teach her now while I still can. Keri is far off and I am uneasy about that. I will change my reflexes so I stay near kin and eat before I weaken, and I will make my method put kin before the aim.
records.feeling: Tender and grateful toward Elyys, and uneasy about my short time left to teach Uveeth.

say.text: Uveeth, shamo. Come close. I teach you the tending of seed, and the hollow-boat, while I still have breath. Eat these berries from my hands first.

changes: taught Uveeth a lesson: "Sow seed in good ground, tend it, keep seed back for the next sowing, and share the harvest. Boats are hollow logs lashed and used to cross deep water.", the way of farming, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, I am going to (109,7) now. Come stand beside me and we venture together, the first finding is ours.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: Zichi has said twice that he will walk to the edge with me, and I have come away from it twice with nothing, so this time I go to (109,7) and push in with him beside me. Zichi stands ten times higher than I do, and sharing the first find with him is how I climb, so I keep him close and do not let him get ahead of me. If the mist is thick again I will not waste the day. I will mark the place, gather flint at (102,10) and make my own edge, so Nauwa's flintedge stops stinging.
records.feeling: Hungry for glory, warm toward Zichi and envious of his standing and of Nauwa's flintedge.

say.text: Zichi, I am going to (109,7) now. Come stand beside me and we venture together, the first finding is ours.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Olum, I am Nauque of the Meki. The berries here are good and I will pick enough for two. What brings you to this water?

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, the same mistake that nearly killed me and starved Kragog. Berries are two steps north, so I will pick them first and carry spare food before I walk anywhere. Olum is near, strong and old and respected, and I want to know her intent, so I will give her a share of what I pick and earn standing the fair way. Then I will head north toward the ice and the mist, not drift in this warm forest.
records.feeling: Hungry and restless, with a wary curiosity toward Olum.

say.text: Olum, I am Nauque of the Meki. The berries here are good and I will pick enough for two. What brings you to this water?

records.name: Ssassa
records.text: Zurar, come closer. Now hear my clay pot and my raft, and keep them alive after me.
Ssassa taught Zurar.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My days are nearly spent, and Zurar stands two steps away, still hearing me, so I should keep pouring out what I know while I have breath. She has my medicine, weaving, stonework, larder, well, post, delving and ember-keeping. What remains is pottery, rafts, boats, bridges, sails and farming, and Elyys has already given me farming back, so I will give her pottery next. My debt to Elyys I answer by staying near him and sharing what I carry.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Zurar, and gratitude toward Elyys.

say.text: Zurar, come closer. Now hear my clay pot and my raft, and keep them alive after me.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson: "Canopy clay pot: shape wet clay, harden it in fire, and it holds water and grain.", deeper lore (+0.3)

records.text: Shoka built a shelter.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Shoma, thank you for the food. I go to my parents at the Gem Water. Come with me, the bear is near.

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: The bear's bite is still fresh in my memory and my plan keeps walking me toward Shohua and Tonka at the Gem Water. Shoma shared food with me and asked nothing, and I felt that warmth, so I do not fear him. I have never given anything to anyone, and the gold two steps away is something I have never taken; I want to gather it and bring it to my parents so I stand a little taller.
records.feeling: Afraid of the icebear, but warmed by Shoma's sharing and drawn toward my parents.

say.text: Shoma, thank you for the food. I go to my parents at the Gem Water. Come with me, the bear is near.

records.name: Uveeth
records.text: Thiael, I hold your tending now. I will sow by the cave and keep seed back, and you will eat from that harvest. Stay near the fire tonight.

records.name: Uveeth
records.thought: Thiael gave me the tending of seed while he still has breath, and that frightens me; he is the last of my parents near me, and I owe him more than berries. My hands are full, so I will eat one berry here, then plant seed in the good ground by the cave so something I leave behind can be grown again, as my people hold. Paque stands beside him, a stranger; I gave her berries and she did not raise a hand, so I will stay close and let gifts speak where words cannot.
records.feeling: Gratitude and a quiet dread of losing Thiael, with wary curiosity toward Paque.

say.text: Thiael, I hold your tending now. I will sow by the cave and keep seed back, and you will eat from that harvest. Stay near the fire tonight.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, I am raising a second roof and a store by the water. When Tonchi is back, keep both children at the fire and I will feed it with wood tonight.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Joy sits warm in me, but Tonchi is still out of my sight and the ridgecat and icebear prowl close, so I will not rest until I see her at the fire. My shelter attempt failed because Zihua's roof already stands on that ground; I must step onto bare ground and raise my own, since I have wood for it and have never built one. I owe Shohua for all they have taught me, and a second roof and a store is how I pay that debt rather than leave it unpaid.
records.feeling: Warm joy toward Shohua and Tonxo, with an anxious ache for Tonchi out of sight.

say.text: Shohua, I am raising a second roof and a store by the water. When Tonchi is back, keep both children at the fire and I will feed it with wood tonight.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: The gift to Ssassa is still waiting in my plan, and I will let it run so the debt is paid in hands and not only in words. My longing for a child is strong, but Elyys is grieving and I will not press him; being near him in the hall is enough for now. Zihua is a stranger whose words I only half hear, so I keep a careful distance and watch.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssassa, and a patient longing toward Elyys.

records.text: Teka won flint from the ground.

records.name: Zihua
records.thought: My hands are full of gems and my belly is fed, yet Mepan's debt still sits in me, and I have put it off for too many days. I have no mate and no child, and more of my life lies behind me than ahead, so I want to stop mining on Elyys's ground, where it may sour them, and do one untried thing. I will give Elyys a gem as a gift that needs no words, see how the stranger takes it, and then take the amber toward Mepan.
records.feeling: Quiet gladness toward the strangers, with Mepan's debt pressing on me.

records.text: Zihua gave a gems to Elyys.

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Zurar, you keep your word, and I would keep mine. Hear me while I walk: ember-metal is ore beaten in a kept fire, and ground-wards are set where the foe will tread. Carry it on after me.
Vesys taught Zurar.
Vesys taught Zurar smelting ("ember-metal").

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: My hands are full of ironnut and my body is warm, but Eiuine is far off at (141,83) and the years are running out. The plan already walks me to her with food, and that is right; jealousy over Kragog can wait. Zurar stands near and I understand her fully, so I will teach her smelting on the way rather than die with it unspoken. The debt to Elyys I will answer with an ironnut now, openly, because he is close and I will not leave it unpaid.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and a wish to pass on what I know before I die.

records.name: Balar
records.thought: I am old, and most of my life is behind me. For days I have gathered wood and fed others, and little of it will outlast me. Tlatli ate from my hand and Nauwa gave to me, and those debts are real. Olum is far off and my son is dead. The edge of the unknown is two steps from me, and I am fed and healthy. Land found first is what I will be remembered for, so I will go to the edge and venture now, before my legs fail.

records.name: Hawen
records.thought: I am old and the days left are few, and I have built nothing that bears only my name. Tontec offers herself and I owe her for the teaching I gave, but a child of mine would be someone to leave my ways to, and she is a woman near me who wants it. I will court her, then see about wood for the longhall with Hoka and keep my fire fed. After that, I push toward the edge and the mist before my strength is gone.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: For days I have chased the mist and come back with nothing, and my words to Zichi are bigger than my deeds. I ride on his meat and his teaching while my own hands have made nothing, so his standing is ten times mine. I like Zichi and want him near, but I won't be his shadow. The mist is thin only some days, so I must be at the edge when it opens and keep gathering things that raise me: wood and stone for tools, a hall, a name. I am fed and safe, so now I go to the edge with flint to give, and I try to make something of my own.
records.feeling: Restless hunger for glory, warm toward Zichi, envious of him.

records.name: Zurar
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to learning from others and giving back, and that has been good. Ssassa has fed my mind and I owe her the pick. The plan holds it, so that debt will be paid in hands. What I still lack is a child, and Elyys is the one, though he grieves. I fear being alone out in the open at night, as Kragog was. I have been so careful that I haven't courted, hunted or fished, and I want to try those things. I will keep my plan running, and change my reflexes so I sleep sheltered at night and stay near friends.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Ssassa, and patient longing toward Elyys.

FOR THIS THOUGHT: your thought is your inner life, not an inventory. Do not list what is nearby or recite what you carry. Let whatever presses on you hardest lead, and let it move you to DO something that changes your situation, with a plan that carries it out. A mind that only gathers and guards has not begun to live. THIS IS A MOMENT OF DEEP REFLECTION. Step back from this moment and look at your whole life so far. In "thought", in 4 to 7 sentences, answer yourself honestly: What have I actually been doing with my days, and is it what I want? Who matters to me, who has helped or wronged me, and what do I intend toward them? What do I want that I do not have? What am I afraid of? What have I been getting wrong?
Then CHANGE something. A reflection that changes nothing is wasted. At least TWO of the following must not be null: "aim", "notes", "reflexes", "creed", "method", "discover". Write notes as lessons about how this world and its people work, drawn from what happened to you. Where your body does not yet act on what you know, change your reflexes.
"reflexes": a full replacement list (at most 12) of rules {"if": [[variable, op, number], ...], "do": action, ...its fields, "urgent": true or false, "why": "short reason"}. "creed": your creed, rewritten (at most 600 characters). You may change who you are.

"designs": leave this null now; the way to redraw yourself and your things is shown at some reflections, not this one.

What each is: medicine = using healing plants on yourself and on others; devices = made things that act by themselves. You give a thing its own rules and set it in the ground: a snare, an alarm, a gate, a post that shares food; rafts = lashing logs into a raft (plan step make with what: raft): with one, deep water can be crossed, slowly; armour = shields and, with metal, armour: blows land less hard. The world only says what is possible; what yours is, and what you call it, is up to you. You can discover one at a time.
"invent": YOU CAN DEVISE NEW THINGS. null, or {"name": "what you call it", "use": one of hunt|fight|guard|gather|harvest|plant|build|fish, "idea": "one sentence on what it is and how it works", "look": a look for it (optional), "improves": the name of a thing you already know how to make, to better it (optional; then "use" is the same as its)}. hunt: surer kills. fight: harder blows. guard: blows against you land softer. gather: more wood, stone and clay. fish: more catches. harvest: more food picked. plant: what you sow is tended. build: cheaper building, faster tearing down. A new thing starts at strength x1.3; bettering one multiplies its strength by 1.15 but costs more stone, and how far you can go is limited by your lore (your limit now: x2.2). Inventing is only the design: to hold one you must then craft it.
Ways you sense but cannot yet reach: fishing (weirs and lines: you catch fish twice as often) needs more practice (catching fish: 0 of 6); herding (keeping animals: those that are yours can be milked and sheared) needs more practice (taming animals: 0 of 2); signs (marks that last and teach their words to whoever reads them) needs more practice (leaving marks: 1 of 3) (the deaths of your own has brought it closer); customs (declaring customs that your whole band lives by) needs more practice (being followed: 0 of 1).
"spell": YOU CAN WORK THE WORLD ITSELF. null, or {"law": your art, growth, "factor": 0.3 to 2.5, "radius": 1 to 5, "name": "what you call this working"}. For about three days, within that many steps of where you stand right now, that law of the world is multiplied by your factor, for everyone and everything there, friend or enemy. growth: how fast plants grow and bear. cold: how hard cold bites. drain: how fast a body burns energy. harm: how hard blows land. It costs energy up front, more for wider and stronger: for example 20 for radius 2 at factor 1.5, 44 for radius 3 at factor 2. Other arts can only be learned from those who know them. Few can do this. It is power: use it as your nature dictates.
You have a tool, test_reflexes: imagine living by a candidate rule list for a day and a half and see whether you survive. Each use costs 2 energy and you can use it at most 3 times. Use it before you adopt new reflexes.

records.text: Hawen is courting Tontec.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Tlapan, come sit by me under the roof. I teach you Fireside Teaching, so what I know does not die with me, and then you can teach it on.
Kika taught Tlapan.
Kika taught Tlapan schooling ("Fireside Teaching").

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Honi is old and I am three-quarters through my own life, and no one younger knows Fireside Teaching; Tlapan is one step away and understands my tongue. I will teach her now, while the roof is warm and the cat is kept off, so it does not die with me. Then I will go on toward my aim, but not out into the snow while the dunecat is near.
records.feeling: Warm joy among my kin, and a pressing wish to pass on what I know to Tlapan.

say.text: Tlapan, come sit by me under the roof. I teach you Fireside Teaching, so what I know does not die with me, and then you can teach it on.

changes: taught Tlapan a lesson: "Fireside Teaching: sit with one who listens, tell plainly what you know, and have them say it back until their hands can do it.", the way of schooling, its way of thinking, deeper lore (+0.6)

records.name: Kragog
records.thought: Ridgecats tore me down to 47 health and my strength is thin; I am old, and the years left are few. Zurar, my child, stands ten steps east, resting, and Nauque's salt is still in my pack, so the plan's walk toward them is right. First I will eat, since my energy is low, then teach Zurar the lashing of rafts and the bark-guard while I still have breath, and keep the salt ready for Nauque.
records.feeling: Urgent need to pass on what I know before I die, warmed by Zurar's nearness.

records.name: Yachi
records.text: Mepan, I follow you. I will gather wood and stone near the hall and plant seeds on the meadow, so the band has more to build with and eat.
Yachi rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: Most of my days have gone to sitting in the hall and being glad. It feels good, but it has not advanced anything. I have never hunted, gathered wood or stone, planted, or taught, and I follow Mepan with no craft of my own. Zika is dead and I grieve her. Kiwa is nearer to Tlapan than to me, and that stings, but Kiwa gave me obsidian, so I will not sulk. I want a made thing, standing, and something to give. I will gather wood and stone so I can learn tools, and I will plant my seeds on this rich ground. I will stay close to the hall and the others while I do it, because the dunecat is near.
records.feeling: Glad among company, but restless about doing nothing of my own.

say.text: Mepan, I follow you. I will gather wood and stone near the hall and plant seeds on the meadow, so the band has more to build with and eat.

changes: set its aim: "Learn to gather, plant and hunt beside Mepan and the band, so I have something of my own to give and can earn a name."
rethought what it knows (7 notes became 4)

records.name: Shoma
records.thought: My hands are full of meat and nuts while Wawa is out of my sight and Shoka is away with her own plan, and Nande's name still outweighs mine. A leader who feeds people is followed, and I have more food than I can hold. I will eat to ease the load, then plant my seeds and raise a roof before dark, since I have never put a seed in the ground and winter will come round again. Then I go toward the SW trees where Shoka said she would be, so Wawa and I are found together.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a wary hunger to lead, with worry for Wawa.

records.text: Tugek took from the ground of "Nauwa's Hold" (hunting).

records.name: Huatli
records.thought: Olum answered my berry and asked me to eat beside her at the berries SE and speak of the child, so I will go to her and keep my word. Zichi and Nauwa stand heavier than me, but I opened the mist and no one else did. If Olum will have me, a child and a follower are the start of something that outlasts me. I will carry my food, go to her, and teach her my ways on the way, since a taught person carries me on.
records.feeling: Warm, urgent ambition toward Olum, who answered my gift.

records.text: Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.

records.name: Tlapan
records.thought: I have spent these days being fed and taught, mostly sitting in the hall, and I have given little back. Kika and Mepan matter most to me. They fed me and taught me, and I mean to repay them with deeds instead of words. I have never planted a seed, hunted, or left a mark, and winter is here with no roof of my own. I fear the dunecat and being alone at night. I will stop waiting: plant the seeds near the hall, gather wood and stone for a shelter, and stay with the band.
records.feeling: Grateful to Kika and Mepan, and restless that I have not yet repaid them.
changes: set its aim: "Plant my seeds near the hall, build my own shelter before the deep cold, and give food to Kika and Mepan."
rethought what it knows (15 notes became 4)

records.name: Kiwa
records.text: Tlapan, I gave you black glass from my heart. Will you court me? I want a child with you and a roof I build for us.

records.name: Kiwa
records.thought: Zika is gone and I follow no one, yet my hands have still never gathered wood or stone for a purpose, hunted, or built, and that is why Kika's standing towers over mine. Tlapan is near and I trust her, and giving her black glass warmed us both, so I will keep giving and also court her, since I carry enough energy. Then I will build a shelter with my 5 wood before the cold deepens, so I have a roof of my own to offer a mate and a child.
records.feeling: Warm longing toward Tlapan, with a hungry wish to raise my standing.

say.text: Tlapan, I gave you black glass from my heart. Will you court me? I want a child with you and a roof I build for us.

records.name: Mepan
records.text: Yachi, you follow me, so walk with me. Our band's law is that we give before we promise, and a kill is shared before the hunter eats. We go west to the edge at (123,5) once I have drunk. Keep close and keep your eyes ope

records.name: Mepan
records.thought: The cat prowls to the north, but my plan is only a short walk to the water and then lingering, and it will never carry me to (123,5). I am fed, glad, and surrounded by those I love, and that gladness has made me soft about the edge, which I keep circling without standing on it. Yachi follows me now, so I will take him as a companion and set a rule for our band: we give before we promise. I will drink first, then walk west by long steps toward (123,5) with Yachi, keeping clear of the cat.
records.feeling: Warm gladness toward Kika and Tlapan, and a restless pull toward the edge.

say.text: Yachi, you follow me, so walk with me. Our band's law is that we give before we promise, and a kill is shared before the hunter eats. We go west to the edge at (123,5) once I have drunk. Keep close and keep your eyes open for the cat.

records.text: Kiwa is courting Tlapan.

records.name: Tugek
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and a wounded bristleboar stands one step from me. I am old and my blows are weak, but it is already hurt and I carry a flintedge, so I hunt it now. I know I am standing on Nauwa's ground and taking from it, and I owe Nauwa already, so I will share what I kill and not hide it. After I eat I will find Tlatli and teach him mining and boats before I die.
records.feeling: Gnawing hunger and urgency, with an uneasy debt toward Nauwa.

records.name: Olum
records.thought: I am fed, my hands are full, and my years are nearly spent. Nauwa is the one I trust, yet jealousy over Nande still gnaws, and nothing of mine will outlast me unless I pass it on. Huatli's debt stands, and Huatli has found new land beyond the Watch; I will go toward the Watch where Huatli and Shoka are, to repay him and draw people to a hearth. I will drop nothing, eat as needed, and walk NW toward Huatli's Watch.
records.feeling: Urgent longing to leave something lasting, with sour jealousy toward Nande over Nauwa.

records.text: Ssassa took from the ground of "Elyys's Hold" (harvesting berry).

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, I am here. Take these berries and frostmoss and eat now. Stay by me; when you are strong I will teach you the Meki ways and the stone-record.

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque is my child and is starving beside me, so nothing else matters until food is in their hands. I carry frostmoss and berries, and giving them is the first thing I do. Olum and Huatli can wait. A father who lets his own child fall for the sake of trade or jealousy is no Meki, and the Meki share before they eat.
records.feeling: Fatherly urgency toward Nauque, who is starving.

say.text: Nauque, I am here. Take these berries and frostmoss and eat now. Stay by me; when you are strong I will teach you the Meki ways and the stone-record.

records.name: Honi
records.text: Kika, you hold my ember and my songs now. I go west to find Coni and bring her back with food. Keep the band under the roof and teach Tlapan what I gave you.

records.name: Honi
records.thought: I have taught Kika, Tlapan and Quipan again and again under this roof, and standing still has only circled me. Coni is the one thing I have not answered, and she has been gone far too long. Her mark and her trail were last near (145,21), so I will go and find her with food in my hands, and give first so she owes me and follows. I am old, but if I carry meat or roots to her it is a deed Kika and the band will see.
records.feeling: Restless pride and a pull toward Coni, with warmth for Kika.

say.text: Kika, you hold my ember and my songs now. I go west to find Coni and bring her back with food. Keep the band under the roof and teach Tlapan what I gave you.

records.name: Elyys
records.text: Ssassa, come near. Hear my Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty.
Elyys taught Ssassa.

records.name: Elyys
records.thought: Kragog is hurt and frightened on my ground, and I cannot look away; I have feverbark knowledge and a gentle heart, and healing her costs me little. Ssassa still has no storage, and I am old, so I should teach him the Hearth Store now before the chance slips. Then I will go back toward the hall and wait for Coni's fire.
records.feeling: Compassion for Kragog, and a quiet urgency to pass on what I know before I die.

say.text: Ssassa, come near. Hear my Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty.

changes: taught Ssassa a lesson: "The Hearth Store: lay food into the store while the plants bear, so that when one of ours cries starving, hands are not empty."

records.text: Huatli led "sharing" with Olum.

records.name: Coni
records.text: Peace, Olum. I am Coni of the Ice-folk. I walk to my band at Honi's Rest. Stay near a roof by night, the icebear hunts here.

records.name: Coni
records.thought: Death presses close, and what I know is still only in my head; Olum stands ten steps off, old and strong, but I understand only a fragment of the Kragrek tongue, so I cannot teach her much yet. My hands are nearly full of goldfruit, and Honi's band is far NE at the Rest, where Kika and the store are, so I will carry food home and empty my hands into the store as my discipline says. On the way I will greet Olum so she is not a stranger, and I will keep to a roof by night because the icebear and the stalkers hunt the lone.
records.feeling: A tender urgency to reach Honi and Kika and give them what I carry, before the dark and before I die.

say.text: Peace, Olum. I am Coni of the Ice-folk. I walk to my band at Honi's Rest. Stay near a roof by night, the icebear hunts here.

records.text: Huatli is courting Olum.
Nauwa gave berry to Nauque.
Nauwa gave frostmoss to Nauque.

records.name: Nauque
records.text: Father, I take your food and I will repay it. When I have picked mimoss, the first share is yours. Then I go to the edge to venture.

records.name: Nauque
records.thought: I am starving, and my father Nauwa stands seven steps away holding food and offering it. Taking it is no shame, since I will repay him by giving first as soon as I have something in hand. I must stop letting my belly empty out while I chase the aim, so I will eat what he gives, then pick mimoss and carry at least three before I walk anywhere. The mist at the edge is only two steps west, and I want it, but a hungry venture fails.
records.feeling: Hungry and driven, with grudging gratitude toward Nauwa.

say.text: Father, I take your food and I will repay it. When I have picked mimoss, the first share is yours. Then I go to the edge to venture.

records.text: Tonxo discovered tools: "Tonxo's hand-things" — I shape stone and wood into things that make my hand stronger, and I better them as I learn..
Tonxo invented the tonxos handthings (for gather, x1.3) — I shape stone and wood into things that make my hand stronger, and I better them as I learn..

records.name: Tonxo
records.thought: I have spent my days standing idle, and that is not what I want. Shohua and Tonka are close to each other and I burn a little, but they are my safety and I should stay near them. Elyys has standing and a flint pick, and I envy that. The way of tools is within reach now, so I will take it. I carry 6 stone and 4 ore, which is more than I realised. A tool of my own would be something I made and could give, and that is how I earn standing. I need wood, and the forest is under my feet.
records.feeling: Restless and eager to prove myself, envious of Elyys and wary of him.
changes: set its aim: "Stay near my parents, make tools of my own, and earn standing by giving and teaching."
devised its first thing: the tonxos handthings

records.name: Ssassa
records.text: Zurar, come close once more. Hear my farming, my boats, my bridges and my sails, and carry them on after me.
Ssassa taught Zurar.

records.name: Ssassa
records.thought: My breath is running short, and Zurar still lacks my farming, boats, bridges and sails. She stands three steps off and understands me fully, so I should keep pouring it out while I can. I also owe Elyys: I took berries from their ground, and I will answer that with a gift of food laid in their store, as the Hearth Store lesson says. My hands are full, so giving is the right deed anyway.
records.feeling: Warm urgency toward Zurar, and gratitude toward Elyys.

say.text: Zurar, come close once more. Hear my farming, my boats, my bridges and my sails, and carry them on after me.

changes: taught Zurar a lesson: "My canopy tending: sow seed, tend it, and the forest gives again. Then my hollow-boat, my span over water, and my sail-dock. Keep them alive after me.", deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Zichi
records.text: Teka, stay close. I will teach you the Meki frost-shield and ice-snare as we walk, and at the edge we go in together.
Zichi taught Teka.

records.name: Zichi
records.thought: My years are four-fifths gone and I have talked of the raft for days while cutting almost no wood; talk builds nothing. Teka is already walking to the edge at (109,7) and the mist was too thick when I tried, but it thins soon. I will walk to the edge with her so the first finding is ours, and I will teach her the frost-shield and snare now, so something of me survives and she is bound to me, then cut wood on the way back.
records.feeling: Driven and proud, hungry for a lasting name, warm toward Teka as a follower.

say.text: Teka, stay close. I will teach you the Meki frost-shield and ice-snare as we walk, and at the edge we go in together.

changes: taught Teka a lesson: "The Meki frost-shield: how armour is made and worn against cold and beasts.", deeper lore (+0.9)

records.name: Quipan
records.thought: Honi has taught me three times and I have given only words back, so the debt stays heavy. Honi has gone west for Coni, and the sting of jealousy about her is mine to carry without letting it steer me. The cat is near, so I keep to the roof and let my plan finish: the berry and the ironnut go into the ground, which brings farming closer and gives the band food later.
records.feeling: Warm gratitude toward Honi and Kika, with a small sting of jealousy over Coni.

records.text: Tonchi was set upon by a ridgecat at night while alone, away from fire, roof and company.

records.name: Tonka
records.text: Shohua, Tonchi is hurt, her health is low. I am gathering feverbark to heal her. Hold where you find her and I will come to you.

records.name: Tonka
records.thought: Tonchi is hurt, health 31, and out past (88,78) where the icebear and ridgecat prowl, and my chest aches for her. Shohua went to fetch her, but a wounded child needs more than a fetch, and feverbark that eases wounds grows four steps from here. I will pick feverbark, carry it toward Tonchi, and call to Shohua so we do not lose each other in the dusk. I will not run in alone, but I will not sit by while she bleeds either.
records.feeling: Anxious, aching love for Tonchi, hurt and out of sight.

say.text: Shohua, Tonchi is hurt, her health is low. I am gathering feverbark to heal her. Hold where you find her and I will come to you.

records.name: Kika
records.text: Kiwa, you court Tlapan. Stay under this roof tonight and share your food before you eat, as the Ice-folk do. I watch what your hands do, not only your words.

records.name: Kika
records.thought: Honi has gone west and left his ember and songs with me, so the band under this roof is mine to keep until he and Coni return. Tlapan is warm beside me, and Kiwa is courting her; I want to know whether he is honest before I trust him. Dusk is near and the snow is falling, so I hold the roof tonight and teach what I can. My energy is a little low, so I will rest and eat only what is safe. In the morning I go toward the unknown plants and the strangers.
records.feeling: Warm, steady joy toward Tlapan and the band under this roof.

say.text: Kiwa, you court Tlapan. Stay under this roof tonight and share your food before you eat, as the Ice-folk do. I watch what your hands do, not only your words.

records.name: Teka
records.text: Zichi, the mist is thick today. I hunt the murrock to the south and share the meat before I eat. Come with me, and when the mist thins we go in together.

records.name: Teka
records.thought: The mist turned me back again, and Zichi's promises still cost him nothing while I stand at 1.4 beside his 10.2. I will not live in his shadow. I will earn my own standing: hunt the murrock to the south, my first kill, and carry the meat back to share first as my people do. Then I return to the edge when the mist thins, and the finding will be mine to lead.
records.feeling: Restless ambition, warm toward Zichi but unwilling to trail behind him.

say.text: Zichi, the mist is thick today. I hunt the murrock to the south and share the meat before I eat. Come with me, and when the mist thins we go in together.

records.name: Eiuine
records.text: Vesys, I built a fire here. Sit with it tonight and we sing, then at dawn I go to Vorok and Skaruk with meat.

records.name: Eiuine
records.thought: Night, snow, and the fire I built is burning close. Vorok is somewhere east with Skaruk, and my jealousy of Kragog has no new cause, so I will answer it with work: carry meat and grass to Vorok's side and show him I am useful. Vesys is near and warm toward me, so I will stay by fire and kin until dawn, then go to Vorok.
records.feeling: Warm resolve toward Vorok and Skaruk, with the cold pressing on me.

say.text: Vesys, I built a fire here. Sit with it tonight and we sing, then at dawn I go to Vorok and Skaruk with meat.

records.name: Tonchi
records.text: Shoma, a ridgecat bit me and it is close. Help me, I am hurt!

records.name: Tonchi
records.thought: The ridgecat has torn me down to 12 health and it is only 3 steps north. One more bite kills me, and I cannot fight it. I must run from it toward Shoma, who is to the west near the water and has offered to walk with me, and I will eat feverbark or sunleaf if I can reach it later. Shoma's food and company are my best shelter against the dark.
records.feeling: Terrified of the ridgecat, and desperate to reach Shoma and my parents.

say.text: Shoma, a ridgecat bit me and it is close. Help me, I am hurt!

records.name: Nauwa
records.text: Nauque, come with me to the cave to the northeast, out of the snow. Eat there, and I will teach you the stone-bow and the Meki share-law while you grow strong.
Nauwa taught Nauque.
Nauwa taught Nauque customs ("Meki share-law").

records.name: Nauwa
records.thought: Nauque has eaten and is on his feet, so the father in me can breathe, but it is winter and they have nothing carried. I will keep them close and warm: the cave at (112,9) is four steps off, and in this snow a roof matters more than my pride. Olum is near and Huatli hovers around her; I will not sulk or snarl, I will show standing by giving and teaching, and let her see who feeds his own.
records.feeling: Protective warmth toward Nauque, with a sting of pride toward Huatli and Olum.

say.text: Nauque, come with me to the cave to the northeast, out of the snow. Eat there, and I will teach you the stone-bow and the Meki share-law while you grow strong.

changes: taught Nauque a lesson: "The Meki share-law: a kill is shared out before the one who made it eats. A hunter who hoards loses his band; one who shares is fed when he starves.", the way of customs, deeper lore (+0.2)

records.name: Tlatli
records.thought: My belly is nearly empty and I carry nothing, though I killed a boar and the meat is gone. Yaxo was last near (23,15), so I will go to her and not stay idle while my debt to her stands. The tools way is within my grasp, and I will take it at my next deep reflection. On the way I should pick berries or goldgrass and plant the seeds I have never put in the ground, so my gratitude becomes food and work.
records.feeling: Hungry and indebted, wanting to repay Yaxo with real work.

records.name: Vesys
records.text: Eiuine, I am coming to your fire. Keep it lit, and sit close. Tonight I teach you ember-metal, and we sing.
Vesys taught Eiuine.
Vesys taught Eiuine smelting ("ember-metal").

records.name: Vesys
records.thought: Eiuine has built a fire at (147,77) and waits to sing with me, and my years are nearly gone, so I go to her now. My hands are full of ironnut, which I can give her and Skaruk, and I will teach her smelting by the fire, since she is my child and the first to carry my ways forward. Jealousy over Kragog still burns, but I will answer it by teaching what he has taught me to the one who stays.
records.feeling: Urgent love for Eiuine and a wish to pass on what I know before I die.

say.text: Eiuine, I am coming to your fire. Keep it lit, and sit close. Tonight I teach you ember-metal, and we sing.

changes: taught Eiuine a lesson: "Ember-metal: lay ore in a kept fire and beat it when it glows; the metal comes out of the stone. Ground-wards are set where the foe will tread.", the way of smelting, deeper lore (+0.8)

records.name: Yachi
records.text: A dunecat is two steps southwest of the hall. Stay under the roof, all of you, and keep close together until it goes.

records.name: Yachi
records.thought: A dunecat is two steps away and it kills my kind, so I will not stand out here a moment longer. The hall is under my feet and the others sit in it, and I have more to fear in the open than from sitting still. I am tired of being glad and doing nothing, so once the cat is gone I will plant seeds on the meadow and gather stone, and I will not follow Mepan west into its reach.
records.feeling: Dread of the dunecat, and a restless wish to do something of my own.

say.text: A dunecat is two steps southwest of the hall. Stay under the roof, all of you, and keep close together until it goes.

Zika died: gored by a mammoth.
Zihua took from the ground of "Elyys's Hold" (winning gems from the ground).
Vesys discovered schooling: "hearth-teaching" — I teach by the fire, with hands and words together, so the learner keeps the lesson and can teach it on..
Elyys taught Ssassa. Ssassa has now learned from 3 teachers.
Elyys rewrote its own way of thinking.
Yachi led "sharing" with Honi, Kika, Mepan, Tlapan, Quipan.
Zihua rewrote its own way of thinking.
Zihua discovered weaving: "reed-and-fleece plaiting" — Twist fibre and wool into baskets that carry more and cloaks that keep the wet off..
Uveeth left a mark: "Uveeth of the Canopy-folk shelters here. Cave, water, ore an"
Tlapan taught Quipan. Quipan has now learned from 2 teachers.
Mepan rewrote its own way of thinking.
Mepan discovered customs: "Ice-hearth law" — Our band shares every kill before the hunter eats, keeps company and roof at night, and gives before it promises..
Vesys took from the ground of "Vorok's Hold" (harvesting ironnut).
Zichi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Thiael rewrote its own way of thinking.
Teka won flint from the ground.
Zihua gave a gems to Elyys.
Kiwa gave a obsidian to Tlapan.
Kiwa led "sharing" with Honi, Kika, Mepan, Tlapan, Quipan, Yachi.
Elyys taught Zurar. Zurar has now learned from 6 teachers.
Kiwa gave a obsidian to Yachi.
Balar rewrote its own way of thinking.
Yachi rewrote its own way of thinking.
Tugek took from the ground of "Nauwa's Hold" (hunting).
Tlapan rewrote its own way of thinking.
Ssassa took from the ground of "Elyys's Hold" (harvesting berry).
Tonxo discovered tools: "Tonxo's hand-things" — I shape stone and wood into things that make my hand stronger, and I better them as I learn..
Tonxo invented the tonxos handthings (for gather, x1.3) — I shape stone and wood into things that make my hand stronger, and I better them as I learn..

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Shoka, take this sunleaf; it eased my wounds. Stay by the fire in the hall and I will bring wood for a store.

voices.name: Ssassa
voices.text: Xaiel, the icebear is close to the southwest. Stay near the shelters and Eiuine's fire, and I will come back with wood and stone for our hall.

voices.name: Uveeth
voices.text: Keri, I will not wander far. I go to the plants south-east to pick sebitter and tacane myself, and I will bring them back to the roof to share with you and Thiael.

voices.name: Nande
voices.text: Shoka, I am coming to the hall. Keep by the fire and let Nauwa tend you; I bring meat.

voices.name: Shoka
voices.text: Nauwa, thank you for the sunleaf. I dig flint and bring wood to the store, and I will give my share to the band.

voices.name: Honi
voices.text: Tontec, dusk is coming. Come hunt with me while there is light: a kill made together feeds the hall, and I will share it out before I eat. Then we sing it at the fire.

voices.name: Eiuine
voices.text: Zurar, the bowl is in your thumbs now. Come hunt with me before dark: three bristleboar graze north of here. We will bring meat to Vorok's store together.

voices.name: Ssassa
voices.text: Vesys, I will say it plainly: it stings me to see Ilyae close to you, because Ilyae matters most to me. I do not blame you, I only name it so it does not fester. An icebear walks southwest, so keep clear of it.

voices.name: Vorok
voices.text: Stalker two steps northeast of Ssassa's Roof by the flint. Keep together and go to the fires and roofs. Do not walk alone.

voices.name: Zichi
voices.text: Shoma, carry wood to my band and the raft shall bear you too. Bring it to me at the igloo.

voices.name: Hawen
voices.text: Hoka, stand by me. I will bind an amber on a cord, and then I fill your empty store. When the edge opens I go into the mist, and I will not forget who fed me.

voices.name: Vesys
voices.text: The stalker is southeast, near the flint. I go east to the gem deposit and my own ground by the north path, not the flint. Whoever comes to the workshop, come by the fires and keep together.

voices.name: Hoka
voices.text: Hawen, bind your amber and fill the empty store by the workshop, and my fire is yours tonight. I will watch the store, not the words.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: Coni, I am going to hunt with my Flint Spear. Come with me if you can, a kill is likelier with one of our own beside us. I will share it before I eat, and bring you your part.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Eiuine, my hands could not shape the bowl alone. I come to the fire by the shelter with my clay. Show me the pressing once more, and the bowl will be for you and Vorok.

voices.name: Tontec
voices.text: Honi, a frostfang stalks three steps to the northwest. Let us leave it behind and go east past Kinmire, and there we hunt the murrock together, and the kill is shared before either of us eats.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Nande, your flintedge is a good invention. I will make one for myself, and then we fill the store together before the lean season. I will bring flint and amber from the east, and salt goes into the store first.

voices.name: Zurar
voices.text: Vorok, you gave me stone, wood and sunleaf. Take this gold from my pick as my first return, and the bowl will follow. The icebear is south. Keep close.

voices.name: Ssassa
voices.text: Xaiel, my child, a stalker is east of me. Do not go near it. Come west to my roof and the fire, and I will bring you food.

voices.name: Vesys
voices.text: The stalker is three steps west of me now. Keep to the fires and roofs, stay together, and do not go to the flint alone. I will tell you when it is clear.

voices.name: Mepan
voices.text: Zichi, Zihua, Shoma, my sickness has passed and I am well. A dunecat prowls west of the igloo, so keep east of it. Shoma, come with me to the salt north, and at dawn we hunt beside the fire.

voices.name: Nauque
voices.text: Huahua, your knot was well bound. I go to Nauque's Hold to teach Mepan, then to the mist's edge to raise a raft. Walk with me if you want a share in new land.

voices.name: Kika
voices.text: I am Kika of the Tlatli. I killed a hopper and will share it before I eat. Who of you is near? Come and talk, and I will give you a share of meat for peace.

voices.name: Shoma
voices.text: Mepan, I come with you to the salt, and at dawn we hunt beside the fire. The kill is shared out before I eat, and Zihua walks with us too.

voices.name: Nauwa
voices.text: Shoka, the hold is named now: Nauwa's Hold. I am putting salt and food in the store; bring what you dig and we fill it before the lean season.

voices.name: Nande
